1 | # Knowledge Intelligence Platform — System Architecture
2 | 
3 | ---
4 | 
5 | ## 1. Vision & Positioning
6 | 
7 | The Knowledge Intelligence Platform is an **evidence-grounded knowledge compiler** for IBM Consulting.
8 | It is not a chatbot, not a document search tool, and not a generic RAG pipeline.
9 | It transforms fragmented institutional knowledge — POVs, BRDs, case studies, playbooks, architecture documents — into a structured, connected, evidence-traceable knowledge layer.
10 | 
11 | **The grounding rule is architectural, not just a prompt constraint:**
12 | Every compiled item (concept, relationship, pattern) carries a `source_document_id` and `source_excerpt` in the database.
13 | Every AI-generated response (answer, comparison, deliverable) returns a structured `sources` field — enforced at the Pydantic schema level before any response leaves the API.
14 | 
15 | ---
16 | 
17 | ## 2. System Architecture
18 | 
19 | ```
20 | ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
21 | │                    BROWSER  (React + TypeScript)                  │
22 | │                                                                  │
23 | │  Workspace List  │  Doc Upload  │  Graph Explorer                │
24 | │  Assistant Chat  │  Deliverable Generator                        │
25 | └────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┘
26 |                          │  HTTP/REST (JSON) — Vite proxy → :8000
27 |                          ▼
28 | ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
29 | │          KNOWLEDGE INTELLIGENCE PLATFORM  —  FastAPI (Python)     │
30 | │                                                                  │
31 | │  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  │
32 | │  │  Document        │  │  Knowledge       │  │  Graph Engine  │  │
33 | │  │  Ingestion       │  │  Compiler        │  │  NetworkX      │  │
34 | │  │  PyMuPDF         │  │  Concept Agent   │  │  builder.py    │  │
35 | │  │  python-docx     │  │  Relationship    │  │  traversal.py  │  │
36 | │  │  python-pptx     │  │  Agent           │  └───────┬────────┘  │
37 | │  └──────┬───────────┘  │  Pattern Agent   │          │           │
38 | │         │              └──────┬───────────┘          │           │
39 | │         │                     │                      │           │
40 | │  ┌──────▼─────────────────────▼──────────────────────▼───────┐  │
41 | │  │                 SQLAlchemy ORM (DB-agnostic)               │  │
42 | │  │  Workspace · Document · Concept · Relationship · Pattern   │  │
43 | │  │  Deliverable · ChatMessage                                 │  │
44 | │  └──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘  │
45 | │                                 │                                │
46 | │  ┌──────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐  │
47 | │  │       SQLite (MVP)  ·  PostgreSQL (Phase 2, same ORM)      │  │
48 | │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
49 | │                                                                  │
50 | │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
51 | │  │  Retrieval / QA          Anthropic Claude API              │  │
52 | │  │  qa_service.py           (all extraction, Q&A,             │  │
53 | │  │  deliverable_service.py   and deliverable gen)              │  │
54 | │  │                           — context-only, no web search    │  │
55 | │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
56 | └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
57 | ```
58 | 
59 | ---
60 | 
61 | ## 3. Knowledge Compilation Pipeline
62 | 
63 | The extraction pipeline has three chained agents, each running after every document ingestion:
64 | 
65 | ```
66 | Upload (PDF / DOCX / PPTX)
67 |         │
68 |         ▼
69 | Magic-byte validation → file-type detection → route to parser
70 |   PDF  → PyMuPDF
71 |   DOCX → python-docx
72 |   PPTX → python-pptx
73 |         │
74 |         ▼
75 | Store Document row (status=processing, raw_text saved)
76 |         │
77 |         ▼
78 | ┌── Agent 1: Concept Compiler ─────────────────────────────────┐
79 | │  Prompt LLM with chunked document text                       │
80 | │  Extracts: {name, type, description, source_excerpt}         │
81 | │  source_excerpt = verbatim quote from document text          │
82 | │  Pydantic validation → reject any item missing source_excerpt│
83 | │  Insert Concept rows (source_document_id = this doc)         │
84 | └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
85 |         │
86 |         ▼
87 | ┌── Agent 2: Relationship Compiler ────────────────────────────┐
88 | │  Load all workspace Concepts                                 │
89 | │  Prompt LLM with concept list + document text                │
90 | │  Extracts: {source, target, relationship_type}               │
91 | │  Fuzzy-match concept names → resolve to Concept IDs         │
92 | │  Only accept relationships where both concepts exist in DB   │
93 | │  Insert Relationship rows                                    │
94 | └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
95 |         │
96 |         ▼
97 | ┌── Agent 3: Pattern Compiler ─────────────────────────────────┐
98 | │  Load workspace Concepts + Relationships                     │
99 | │  Prompt LLM with full workspace knowledge context            │
100 | │  Extracts: {name, problem_statement, ibm_approach[], ...}    │
101 | │  Upsert ConsultingPattern rows (by name within workspace)    │
102 | └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
103 |         │
104 |         ▼
105 | Update Document: status=complete
106 | (on exception: status=failed, error_message=str(e))
107 | ```
108 | 
109 | **Why this chained agent approach?**
110 | Concept extraction is scoped to a single document — it only needs that document's text.
111 | Relationship extraction needs the full workspace concept map to avoid hallucinating concept names.
112 | Pattern extraction needs the full workspace graph — it looks for cross-document recurring structures.
113 | Chaining these three agents lets each one benefit from the work of the previous while keeping the extraction logic separated and testable.
114 | 
115 | ---
116 | 
117 | ## 4. Evidence-Grounded Q&A Pipeline (Graph-First Retrieval)
118 | 
119 | ```
120 | User question → POST /workspaces/{id}/ask
121 |         │
122 |         ▼
123 | 1. Keyword extraction (LLM-assisted + token fallback)
124 |         │
125 |         ▼
126 | 2. Graph-first retrieval:
127 |    Load workspace NetworkX graph (built from Concept + Relationship rows)
128 |    Match concept nodes by keyword → expand N-hop neighbourhood (default: 2 hops)
129 |         │
130 |         ▼
131 | 3. Evidence assembly:
132 |    Pull source_excerpt for every node in the subgraph
133 |    Pull ConsultingPattern rows referencing matched concepts
134 |    Assemble context window: {concept, description, excerpt, source doc}
135 |         │
136 |         ▼
137 | 4. LLM generates answer (Claude, context-only):
138 |    System prompt: "Answer ONLY from the provided context.
139 |    If context doesn't support the answer, say: not found in the uploaded knowledge.
140 |    Cite every claim with [Source: Document Name]."
141 |         │
142 |         ▼
143 | 5. Validation: answer is non-"not found" AND sources is empty → reject, return not-found
144 |         │
145 |         ▼
146 | 6. Persist ChatMessage rows (user + assistant)
147 |    Return: {answer, sources: [{document_name, excerpt}]}
148 | ```
149 | 
150 | **Why graph-first, not embeddings-first?**
151 | Graph traversal surfaces structured relationships — ISO 20022 *implements* SWIFT *enables* real-time settlement — that embedding similarity cannot. For IBM Consulting use cases where the *connection between concepts* is the value, graph traversal produces better context than nearest-neighbour vector retrieval. Embeddings can be layered in as a fallback if keyword matching proves too sparse, but graph traversal is the primary retrieval mechanism.
152 | 
153 | ---
154 | 
155 | ## 5. Data Model
156 | 
157 | ```
158 | Workspace ─── Document ─── Concept ─── Relationship (Concept → Concept)
159 |     │              │                        │
160 |     │              └──────────────► source_document_id
161 |     │
162 |     ├── ConsultingPattern (related_concept_ids[], source_document_ids[])
163 |     ├── Deliverable       (source_concept_ids[], source_document_ids[])
164 |     └── ChatMessage       (source_document_ids[])
165 | ```
166 | 
167 | All JSON list fields (`topics`, `ibm_approach`, `related_concept_ids`, etc.) are stored as JSON text via a `TypeDecorator` — transparent on read/write, portable across SQLite and PostgreSQL.
168 | 
169 | All foreign keys are indexed. Cascade delete on workspace removes all associated rows.
170 | 
171 | ---
172 | 
173 | ## 6. Repository / Interface Layer
174 | 
175 | Every storage operation goes through a SQLAlchemy ORM query — no raw SQL. This means:
176 | - SQLite → PostgreSQL: change `DATABASE_URL`, zero code changes required.
177 | - NetworkX → Neo4j: implement `GraphRepository` with the same interface as `builder.py` + `traversal.py`.
178 | 
179 | ---
180 | 
181 | ## 7. MVP vs Phase 2 Architecture
182 | 
183 | | Component | MVP | Phase 2 |
184 | |---|---|---|
185 | | Database | SQLite | RDS PostgreSQL (same ORM) |
186 | | Graph engine | NetworkX in-process | Amazon Neptune / Neo4j |
187 | | Task queue | FastAPI BackgroundTasks | SQS + Celery worker fleet |
188 | | File storage | Local disk (`./uploads`) | S3 |
189 | | Deployment | `uvicorn` local | ECS Fargate + CloudFront |
190 | | Auth | None | IBM SSO / Cognito |
191 | | LLM | Anthropic direct API | Amazon Bedrock (Claude) |
192 | | Vector search (optional) | None | pgvector / OpenSearch |
193 | 
194 | ---
195 | 
196 | ## 8. Non-Goals (Phase 2)
197 | 
198 | Authentication, multi-tenant isolation, CI/CD, production deployment, real-time collaborative editing, IBM enterprise system integrations (SharePoint, Teams, Confluence), document versioning.
199 |

1 | """
2 | LLM governance layer — budget enforcement and workspace-level rate limiting.
3 | 
4 | Budget enforcement (Phase 4)
5 | -----------------------------
6 | Before every LLM call, check_budget() queries the workspace's LLMBudget row.
7 |   - If monthly_token_limit > 0 and current_token_usage >= limit → HTTP 429
8 |   - If monthly_cost_limit  > 0 and current_cost_usage  >= limit → HTTP 429
9 |   - Limits of 0 mean unlimited (default for new workspaces).
10 | 
11 | Rate limiting (Phase 7)
12 | -----------------------
13 | A simple in-process sliding-window counter per workspace.
14 |   - Window: 60 seconds (configurable via LLM_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS)
15 |   - Limit:  MAX_LLM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE per workspace (default 60)
16 |   - Returns HTTP 429 when the window is full.
17 | 
18 | Note: this in-process rate limiter is suitable for a single-process deployment.
19 | For a multi-process/multi-node deployment replace with a Redis-backed counter.
20 | """
21 | from __future__ import annotations
22 | 
23 | import collections
24 | import logging
25 | import threading
26 | import time
27 | 
28 | from fastapi import HTTPException
29 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
30 | 
31 | from app.config import settings
32 | from app.db.models import LLMBudget
33 | 
34 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
35 | 
36 | 
37 | # ── Budget enforcement ────────────────────────────────────────────────
38 | 
39 | def check_budget(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> None:
40 |     """
41 |     Raise HTTP 429 if the workspace has exceeded its monthly token or cost budget.
42 |     No-op if no budget row exists (unlimited by default).
43 |     """
44 |     budget = (
45 |         db.query(LLMBudget)
46 |         .filter(LLMBudget.workspace_id == workspace_id)
47 |         .first()
48 |     )
49 |     if budget is None:
50 |         return
51 | 
52 |     if budget.monthly_token_limit > 0:
53 |         if budget.current_token_usage >= budget.monthly_token_limit:
54 |             logger.warning(
55 |                 "[ws=%d] Token budget exceeded: %d / %d",
56 |                 workspace_id, budget.current_token_usage, budget.monthly_token_limit,
57 |             )
58 |             raise HTTPException(
59 |                 status_code=429,
60 |                 detail=(
61 |                     f"Workspace LLM token budget exceeded "
62 |                     f"({budget.current_token_usage:,} / {budget.monthly_token_limit:,} tokens used this month)."
63 |                 ),
64 |             )
65 | 
66 |     if budget.monthly_cost_limit > 0.0:
67 |         if budget.current_cost_usage >= budget.monthly_cost_limit:
68 |             logger.warning(
69 |                 "[ws=%d] Cost budget exceeded: $%.4f / $%.4f",
70 |                 workspace_id, budget.current_cost_usage, budget.monthly_cost_limit,
71 |             )
72 |             raise HTTPException(
73 |                 status_code=429,
74 |                 detail=(
75 |                     f"Workspace LLM cost budget exceeded "
76 |                     f"(${budget.current_cost_usage:.4f} / ${budget.monthly_cost_limit:.4f} spent this month)."
77 |                 ),
78 |             )
79 | 
80 | 
81 | # ── Rate limiting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
82 | 
83 | _rate_lock   = threading.Lock()
84 | # workspace_id → deque of request timestamps (float, monotonic)
85 | _rate_windows: dict[int, collections.deque] = collections.defaultdict(
86 |     lambda: collections.deque()
87 | )
88 | 
89 | 
90 | def check_rate_limit(workspace_id: int) -> None:
91 |     """
92 |     Raise HTTP 429 if the workspace has made more than
93 |     MAX_LLM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE LLM calls in the last LLM_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS.
94 |     """
95 |     limit  = settings.max_llm_requests_per_minute
96 |     window = settings.llm_rate_window_seconds
97 |     now    = time.monotonic()
98 |     cutoff = now - window
99 | 
100 |     with _rate_lock:
101 |         dq = _rate_windows[workspace_id]
102 |         # Remove timestamps outside the current window
103 |         while dq and dq[0] < cutoff:
104 |             dq.popleft()
105 | 
106 |         if len(dq) >= limit:
107 |             logger.warning(
108 |                 "[ws=%d] LLM rate limit hit: %d requests in %.0fs window.",
109 |                 workspace_id, len(dq), window,
110 |             )
111 |             raise HTTPException(
112 |                 status_code=429,
113 |                 detail=(
114 |                     f"LLM request rate limit exceeded "
115 |                     f"({limit} requests per {window:.0f}s). Please slow down."
116 |                 ),
117 |             )
118 | 
119 |         dq.append(now)

1 | """
2 | LLM usage tracker — persists one row per API call to the llm_usage table.
3 | 
4 | Token counts come from the Anthropic response object's usage field.
5 | Cost estimates use configurable per-token prices; updating prices requires
6 | only a config change, not a code change.
7 | 
8 | Pricing defaults (USD per token) reflect Claude Sonnet 3.5 / 4 pricing
9 | as of 2025. Override via environment variables:
10 |   LLM_COST_PER_1K_INPUT_TOKENS
11 |   LLM_COST_PER_1K_OUTPUT_TOKENS
12 | """
13 | from __future__ import annotations
14 | 
15 | import logging
16 | from datetime import datetime
17 | 
18 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
19 | 
20 | from app.config import settings
21 | from app.db.models import LLMBudget, LLMUsage
22 | 
23 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
24 | 
25 | # Cost per 1 000 tokens in USD — configurable via Settings
26 | _INPUT_COST_PER_1K  = settings.llm_cost_per_1k_input_tokens
27 | _OUTPUT_COST_PER_1K = settings.llm_cost_per_1k_output_tokens
28 | 
29 | 
30 | def estimate_cost(prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int) -> float:
31 |     """Return estimated USD cost for a single API call."""
32 |     return (
33 |         prompt_tokens  / 1000.0 * _INPUT_COST_PER_1K +
34 |         completion_tokens / 1000.0 * _OUTPUT_COST_PER_1K
35 |     )
36 | 
37 | 
38 | def record_usage(
39 |     db: Session,
40 |     workspace_id: int | None,
41 |     operation_type: str,
42 |     model_name: str,
43 |     prompt_tokens: int,
44 |     completion_tokens: int,
45 | ) -> LLMUsage:
46 |     """
47 |     Persist one LLMUsage row and update the workspace's running budget totals.
48 |     Re-raises on failure after logging — callers decide whether to absorb the error.
49 |     """
50 |     cost = estimate_cost(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)
51 | 
52 |     try:
53 |         usage = LLMUsage(
54 |             workspace_id=workspace_id,
55 |             operation_type=operation_type,
56 |             model_name=model_name,
57 |             prompt_tokens=prompt_tokens,
58 |             completion_tokens=completion_tokens,
59 |             estimated_cost_usd=cost,
60 |             request_timestamp=datetime.utcnow(),
61 |         )
62 |         db.add(usage)
63 | 
64 |         if workspace_id is not None:
65 |             _update_budget(db, workspace_id, prompt_tokens + completion_tokens, cost)
66 | 
67 |         db.commit()
68 | 
69 |         logger.info(
70 |             "[ws=%s] LLM call recorded: op=%s model=%s tokens=%d+%d cost=$%.6f",
71 |             workspace_id, operation_type, model_name,
72 |             prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost,
73 |         )
74 |         return usage
75 | 
76 |     except Exception as exc:
77 |         logger.error("Failed to record LLM usage: %s", exc)
78 |         db.rollback()
79 |         raise
80 | 
81 | 
82 | def _update_budget(db: Session, workspace_id: int, total_tokens: int, cost: float) -> None:
83 |     """Create or update the LLMBudget row for this workspace."""
84 |     budget = (
85 |         db.query(LLMBudget)
86 |         .filter(LLMBudget.workspace_id == workspace_id)
87 |         .first()
88 |     )
89 |     if budget is None:

94 |     budget.current_cost_usage  = (budget.current_cost_usage  or 0.0) + cost

1 | """
2 | Centralised upload validation layer.
3 | 
4 | Validation order for every uploaded file:
5 |   1. Stream the first 8 KB — enough for magic-byte detection, avoids loading
6 |      the full file into memory before we know it is safe.
7 |   2. Identify the true MIME type from magic bytes — extension and Content-Type
8 |      headers are both attacker-controlled and are not trusted for security decisions.
9 |   3. Reject if the detected MIME type is not in the explicit allow-list.
10 |   4. Read the remainder and enforce the MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES size limit.
11 | 
12 | All upload endpoints must call validate_upload() before reading file contents.
13 | No duplicate validation logic elsewhere.
14 | """
15 | from __future__ import annotations
16 | 
17 | import logging
18 | from typing import NamedTuple
19 | 
20 | import filetype
21 | from fastapi import HTTPException, UploadFile
22 | 
23 | from app.config import settings
24 | 
25 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
26 | 
27 | # Allowed MIME types and the internal file_type label each maps to.
28 | _ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES: dict[str, str] = {
29 |     "application/pdf": "pdf",
30 |     "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document": "docx",
31 |     "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation": "pptx",
32 | }
33 | 
34 | # Bytes read for magic-byte detection — 8 KB is more than enough for all
35 | # supported formats; PDF/DOCX/PPTX signatures are in the first handful of bytes.
36 | _MAGIC_READ_BYTES = 8192
37 | 
38 | 
39 | class ValidationResult(NamedTuple):
40 |     file_type: str   # 'pdf' | 'docx' | 'pptx'
41 |     content: bytes   # full file bytes, ready for the parser
42 | 
43 | 
44 | async def validate_upload(file: UploadFile) -> ValidationResult:
45 |     """
46 |     Validate a single uploaded file and return its content.
47 | 
48 |     Raises HTTPException (413 or 422) on any violation.
49 |     On success, returns (file_type, full_content_bytes).
50 |     """
51 |     filename = file.filename or "(unknown)"
52 | 
53 |     # ── Step 1: read first chunk for magic-byte detection ─────────────
54 |     first_chunk = await file.read(_MAGIC_READ_BYTES)
55 |     if not first_chunk:
56 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f"'{filename}' is empty.")
57 | 
58 |     # ── Step 2: detect true MIME type from magic bytes ─────────────────
59 |     # filetype.guess() inspects the binary signature, ignoring filename/extension.
60 |     kind = filetype.guess(first_chunk)
61 |     detected_mime = kind.mime if kind else None
62 |     file_type = _ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES.get(detected_mime or "")
63 |     if file_type is None:
64 |         logger.warning(
65 |             "Upload rejected — unsupported magic-byte MIME '%s' for file '%s'",
66 |             detected_mime, filename,
67 |         )
68 |         raise HTTPException(
69 |             status_code=422,
70 |             detail=(
71 |                 f"Unsupported file type detected for '{filename}'. "
72 |                 "Accepted formats: PDF, DOCX, PPTX. "
73 |                 f"(Detected: {detected_mime or 'unknown'})"
74 |             ),
75 |         )
76 | 
77 |     # ── Step 3: read remainder and enforce size limit ──────────────────
78 |     max_bytes = settings.upload_max_bytes
79 |     remaining = await file.read(max_bytes)
80 |     full_content = first_chunk + remaining
81 | 
82 |     # One extra byte read — if non-empty the file exceeds the limit.
83 |     overflow = await file.read(1)
84 |     if overflow:
85 |         max_mb = max_bytes / (1024 * 1024)
86 |         raise HTTPException(
87 |             status_code=413,
88 |             detail=f"'{filename}' exceeds the maximum upload size of {max_mb:.0f} MB.",
89 |         )
90 | 
91 |     logger.debug(
92 |         "Upload validated: '%s' — type=%s size=%d bytes",
93 |         filename, file_type, len(full_content),
94 |     )
95 |     return ValidationResult(file_type=file_type, content=full_content)
96 |

1 | """
2 | LLM retry policy — tenacity-based retry with exponential backoff + jitter.
3 | 
4 | Transient errors that are retried:
5 |   - httpx.TimeoutException  (connect, read, write, pool timeout)
6 |   - httpx.ConnectError      (DNS failure, TCP refused)
7 |   - httpx.RemoteProtocolError
8 |   - anthropic.APIStatusError with status 429 (rate-limited by upstream)
9 |   - anthropic.APIStatusError with status 5xx (provider-side errors)
10 | 
11 | Errors that are NOT retried (fail immediately):
12 |   - anthropic.AuthenticationError  (bad API key)
13 |   - anthropic.PermissionDeniedError
14 |   - anthropic.NotFoundError
15 |   - anthropic.UnprocessableEntityError  (invalid prompt / request body)
16 |   - fastapi.HTTPException              (circuit breaker open, budget exceeded)
17 |   - ValueError / TypeError             (programming errors)
18 | 
19 | Configuration (via settings):
20 |   LLM_MAX_RETRIES      default 4   attempts before giving up (1 original + 3 retries)
21 |   LLM_RETRY_MAX_WAIT   default 30  seconds cap on per-attempt backoff sleep
22 | """
23 | from __future__ import annotations
24 | 
25 | import logging
26 | 
27 | import httpx
28 | import anthropic
29 | from fastapi import HTTPException
30 | from tenacity import (
31 |     retry,
32 |     retry_if_exception,
33 |     stop_after_attempt,
34 |     wait_exponential_jitter,
35 |     before_sleep_log,
36 |     RetryError,
37 | )
38 | 
39 | from app.config import settings
40 | 
41 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
42 | 
43 | # ── Transient-error predicate ──────────────────────────────────────────
44 | 
45 | def _is_transient(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
46 |     """
47 |     Return True if the exception is a transient failure that is safe to retry.
48 |     Anything returning False will propagate immediately without further attempts.
49 |     """
50 |     # Network-level transients (timeout, connection refused, broken pipe)
51 |     if isinstance(exc, (httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.ConnectError, httpx.RemoteProtocolError)):
52 |         return True
53 | 
54 |     # Upstream HTTP status codes that indicate a temporary condition
55 |     if isinstance(exc, anthropic.APIStatusError):
56 |         return exc.status_code in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504)
57 | 
58 |     # Everything else (auth errors, validation errors, circuit-breaker 503s) → fail fast
59 |     return False
60 | 
61 | 
62 | # ── Retry decorator factory ────────────────────────────────────────────
63 | 
64 | def llm_retry():
65 |     """
66 |     Return a tenacity @retry decorator configured from application settings.
67 | 
68 |     Called as a factory so the decorator always reads the live settings values
69 |     (useful in tests that monkeypatch settings).
70 | 
71 |     Usage::
72 | 
73 |         @llm_retry()
74 |         def _call_api(...):
75 |             ...
76 |     """
77 |     return retry(
78 |         retry=retry_if_exception(_is_transient),
79 |         stop=stop_after_attempt(settings.llm_max_retries + 1),   # +1 = original attempt
80 |         wait=wait_exponential_jitter(
81 |             initial=1.0,
82 |             max=settings.llm_retry_max_wait,
83 |             jitter=1.0,
84 |         ),
85 |         before_sleep=before_sleep_log(logger, logging.WARNING),
86 |         reraise=False,   # raises tenacity.RetryError on exhaustion — caller normalises it
87 |     )
88 | 
89 | 
90 | def is_retry_exhausted(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
91 |     """Return True when tenacity has given up after all attempts."""
92 |     return isinstance(exc, RetryError)
93 |

1 | """
2 | Secret management abstraction layer.
3 | 
4 | Application code retrieves secrets only through a SecretProvider — never
5 | via direct os.getenv() or settings attribute access outside this module.
6 | This makes the secret source swappable without changing any caller.
7 | 
8 | Current implementation: EnvironmentSecretProvider (reads from environment
9 | variables loaded by pydantic-settings). No runtime dependencies beyond the
10 | standard library.
11 | 
12 | Future providers (add without touching callers):
13 |   - AWSSecretsManagerProvider  — fetches from AWS Secrets Manager, supports
14 |                                   automatic rotation via version stages
15 |   - IBMSecretsManagerProvider  — IBM Cloud Secrets Manager API
16 |   - AzureKeyVaultProvider       — Azure Key Vault secrets
17 | 
18 | Rotation workflow
19 | -----------------
20 | 1. Generate new secret value in your secret store.
21 | 2. Update the secret version (AWS: add AWSPENDING label; IBM: create new version).
22 | 3. During deployment, the provider fetches the latest active version automatically.
23 | 4. Revoke the old version after confirming the new one is live.
24 | 5. No application restart required when using a cloud provider.
25 | """
26 | from __future__ import annotations
27 | 
28 | import logging
29 | import os
30 | from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
31 | from functools import lru_cache
32 | 
33 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
34 | 
35 | 
36 | class SecretProvider(ABC):
37 |     """Interface for retrieving named secrets."""
38 | 
39 |     @abstractmethod
40 |     def get_secret(self, secret_name: str) -> str:
41 |         """
42 |         Return the current value of the named secret.
43 |         Raises KeyError if the secret does not exist.
44 |         """
45 | 
46 | 
47 | class EnvironmentSecretProvider(SecretProvider):
48 |     """
49 |     Reads secrets from environment variables.
50 | 
51 |     secret_name maps directly to an environment variable name.
52 |     Suitable for local development and CI.
53 | 
54 |     For production: replace with AWSSecretsManagerProvider and set
55 |     CLAUDE_SECRET_NAME=anthropic-api-key (or whatever name you registered
56 |     in your secret store) instead of placing the raw key in the environment.
57 |     """
58 | 
59 |     def get_secret(self, secret_name: str) -> str:
60 |         value = os.environ.get(secret_name)
61 |         if not value:
62 |             raise KeyError(
63 |                 f"Secret '{secret_name}' not found in environment. "
64 |                 "Set the corresponding environment variable or switch to a "
65 |                 "cloud secret provider for production."
66 |             )
67 |         logger.debug("Secret '%s' retrieved from environment.", secret_name)
68 |         return value
69 | 
70 | 
71 | @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
72 | def get_secret_provider() -> SecretProvider:
73 |     """
74 |     Return the active SecretProvider singleton.
75 | 
76 |     To swap providers (e.g. in tests or for a different deployment target),
77 |     call get_secret_provider.cache_clear() and override the factory here.
78 |     """
79 |     return EnvironmentSecretProvider()

1 | """
2 | Circuit breaker for LLM calls.
3 | 
4 | Protects the application from cascading failures when the LLM provider is
5 | unavailable, rate-limiting, or timing out.
6 | 
7 | State machine
8 | -------------
9 | CLOSED   — normal operation; failures are counted
10 | OPEN     — breaker is tripped; all calls are rejected immediately
11 | HALF_OPEN — recovery probe; a single call is allowed through to test health
12 | 
13 | Transition rules
14 | ----------------
15 | CLOSED  → OPEN      when consecutive_failures >= failure_threshold
16 | OPEN    → HALF_OPEN after recovery_timeout_seconds have elapsed
17 | HALF_OPEN → CLOSED  on successful call
18 | HALF_OPEN → OPEN    on failed call (resets the recovery timer)
19 | 
20 | Configuration (all via environment / Settings):
21 |   LLM_CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD   default 5   failures before opening
22 |   LLM_CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT    default 60  seconds before half-open probe
23 | """
24 | from __future__ import annotations
25 | 
26 | import logging
27 | import threading
28 | import time
29 | from enum import Enum
30 | 
31 | from fastapi import HTTPException
32 | 
33 | from app.config import settings
34 | 
35 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
36 | 
37 | 
38 | class BreakerState(str, Enum):
39 |     CLOSED    = "closed"
40 |     OPEN      = "open"
41 |     HALF_OPEN = "half_open"
42 | 
43 | 
44 | class CircuitBreaker:
45 |     """
46 |     Thread-safe circuit breaker.
47 | 
48 |     Usage::
49 | 
50 |         breaker = CircuitBreaker()
51 | 
52 |         with breaker:
53 |             result = call_llm_api()
54 |     """
55 | 
56 |     def __init__(
57 |         self,
58 |         failure_threshold: int | None = None,
59 |         recovery_timeout: float | None = None,
60 |     ) -> None:
61 |         self._threshold = failure_threshold or settings.llm_cb_failure_threshold
62 |         self._timeout   = recovery_timeout  or settings.llm_cb_recovery_timeout
63 |         self._failures  = 0
64 |         self._state     = BreakerState.CLOSED
65 |         self._opened_at: float | None = None
66 |         self._lock      = threading.Lock()
67 | 
68 |     # ── public API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
69 | 
70 |     @property
71 |     def state(self) -> BreakerState:
72 |         with self._lock:
73 |             return self._evaluated_state()
74 | 
75 |     def record_success(self) -> None:
76 |         with self._lock:
77 |             self._failures = 0
78 |             self._state    = BreakerState.CLOSED
79 |             self._opened_at = None
80 |         logger.debug("Circuit breaker: call succeeded → CLOSED")
81 | 
82 |     def record_failure(self) -> None:
83 |         with self._lock:
84 |             self._failures += 1
85 |             if self._failures >= self._threshold:
86 |                 self._state     = BreakerState.OPEN
87 |                 self._opened_at = time.monotonic()
88 |                 logger.warning(
89 |                     "Circuit breaker OPEN after %d consecutive failures.", self._failures
90 |                 )
91 | 
92 |     def __enter__(self) -> "CircuitBreaker":
93 |         with self._lock:
94 |             state = self._evaluated_state()
95 | 
96 |         if state == BreakerState.OPEN:
97 |             logger.warning("Circuit breaker is OPEN — rejecting LLM request.")
98 |             raise HTTPException(
99 |                 status_code=503,
100 |                 detail="LLM service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.",
101 |             )
102 |         return self
103 | 
104 |     def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> bool:
105 |         if exc_type is None:
106 |             self.record_success()
107 |         else:
108 |             # Only count genuine provider/network errors, not validation errors.
109 |             if not issubclass(exc_type, (ValueError, HTTPException)):
110 |                 self.record_failure()
111 |         return False  # never suppress exceptions
112 | 
113 |     # ── internals ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
114 | 
115 |     def _evaluated_state(self) -> BreakerState:
116 |         """
117 |         Transition OPEN → HALF_OPEN if the recovery timeout has elapsed.
118 |         Must be called with self._lock held.
119 |         """
120 |         if self._state == BreakerState.OPEN and self._opened_at is not None:
121 |             elapsed = time.monotonic() - self._opened_at
122 |             if elapsed >= self._timeout:
123 |                 self._state = BreakerState.HALF_OPEN
124 |                 logger.info(
125 |                     "Circuit breaker: recovery timeout elapsed (%.0fs) → HALF_OPEN",
126 |                     elapsed,
127 |                 )
128 |         return self._state
129 | 
130 | 
131 | # Application-level singleton — shared across all threads in one process.
132 | # Tests can call circuit_breaker._failures = 0; circuit_breaker._state = CLOSED
133 | # to reset between cases.
134 | circuit_breaker = CircuitBreaker()
135 |

1 | # ADR: Payments Center Brain
2 | 
3 | **Status:** Proposed — not implemented  
4 | **Date:** 2025  
5 | **Deciders:** Knowledge Intelligence Platform team  
6 | 
7 | ---
8 | 
9 | ## Context
10 | 
11 | The Knowledge Intelligence Platform currently operates on a per-workspace model. Each workspace is an isolated knowledge domain: practitioners upload documents, the platform compiles them into a knowledge graph, and all retrieval and generation is scoped exclusively to that workspace.
12 | 
13 | This design is correct for project-specific and engagement-specific knowledge. However, it creates a gap for **practice-level institutional knowledge** — the accumulated domain expertise that belongs to an entire practice (e.g. the Payments Center of Excellence) rather than to any single engagement.
14 | 
15 | Today, this practice-level knowledge is either:
16 | - Uploaded repeatedly into individual workspaces (duplicated effort, inconsistent across workspaces), or
17 | - Not available to the platform at all (practitioners miss relevant institutional context when generating deliverables).
18 | 
19 | ---
20 | 
21 | ## Decision
22 | 
23 | We will design a **Payments Center Brain** — a centralised, shared institutional knowledge graph built from practice-wide assets and maintained by practice leads.
24 | 
25 | This is a **future enhancement**. It is documented here to preserve architectural intent and inform implementation decisions made before this feature is built.
26 | 
27 | ---
28 | 
29 | ## Proposed Design
30 | 
31 | ### What it is
32 | 
33 | A shared, read-only knowledge graph scoped to the Payments Center of Excellence (and extensible to other practices). It is compiled from curated practice assets — canonical POVs, reference architectures, domain standards documents, methodology guides — and maintained by designated practice knowledge owners.
34 | 
35 | Unlike workspace knowledge graphs (which are project-specific and mutable by any workspace member), the Payments Center Brain is:
36 | - **Shared** — visible to practitioners across all workspaces
37 | - **Curated** — managed by practice leads, not individual project teams
38 | - **Additive** — it supplements workspace knowledge, never replaces it
39 | 
40 | ### Data sources
41 | 
42 | The Payments Center Brain will ingest from:
43 | - SharePoint document libraries (Payments Center of Excellence repository)
44 | - Box repositories (shared practice knowledge stores)
45 | - Bulk-imported domain documents (standards, regulatory frameworks, methodology guides)
46 | 
47 | Ingestion uses the same three-agent compilation pipeline (Concept → Relationship → Pattern) already implemented for workspace documents.
48 | 
49 | ### Knowledge scope selector
50 | 
51 | When a practitioner generates a deliverable (POV, BRD, PRD, Executive Summary, Roadmap), they will be offered a knowledge scope choice:
52 | 
53 | ```
54 | Knowledge Scope
55 | ───────────────
56 | ( ) Workspace Only
57 |     Use only documents uploaded to this workspace.
58 | 
59 | (●) Workspace + Payments Center Brain
60 |     Include institutional practice knowledge alongside workspace documents.
61 |     Source citations will identify whether each claim came from workspace
62 |     documents or from the shared practice knowledge base.
63 | ```
64 | 
65 | The default is **Workspace Only** to preserve the current behaviour and workspace isolation guarantee.
66 | 
67 | When **Workspace + Payments Center Brain** is selected:
68 | - The retrieval pipeline queries both the workspace graph and the shared graph
69 | - Retrieved concepts from both sources are merged and ranked together
70 | - Source citations distinguish between workspace sources and shared knowledge sources
71 | - The grounding rule applies equally to both sources — every claim must trace to a document
72 | 
73 | ### Workspace behaviour is unchanged
74 | 
75 | Individual workspaces remain fully isolated from each other. The Payments Center Brain is an **opt-in additive layer**, not a shared context that is always present. Enabling it for one query does not affect other workspaces or other queries.
76 | 
77 | ---
78 | 
79 | ## Consequences
80 | 
81 | ### Benefits
82 | - Practitioners gain access to canonical institutional knowledge without uploading it to every workspace
83 | - Practice leads can ensure consistent, authoritative information is available across all engagements
84 | - Deliverables can synthesise both project-specific findings and practice-wide expertise in a single, source-cited output
85 | 
86 | ### Risks and mitigations
87 | - **Staleness:** Shared knowledge must be actively maintained. Implement a `last_reviewed` date on shared documents and surface a warning when knowledge is older than a configurable threshold.
88 | - **Authority conflicts:** When workspace knowledge contradicts shared knowledge, the system must surface both views and let the practitioner decide. Never silently merge conflicting claims.
89 | - **Access control:** The Payments Center Brain requires authentication and role-based access before it can be safely shared across practitioners. This feature is therefore blocked on authentication implementation.
90 | - **Context explosion:** Combining two knowledge graphs risks assembling too much context. The existing `QA_TOP_K` and `GRAPH_MAX_NODES` caps apply independently to each source and must be configured appropriately.
91 | 
92 | ---
93 | 
94 | ## Implementation Prerequisites
95 | 
96 | Before this feature can be built:
97 | 
98 | 1. **Authentication and authorisation** — practitioners must have verified identities before shared knowledge can be exposed
99 | 2. **SharePoint / Box connectors** — bulk ingestion from external repositories requires OAuth integration with those systems
100 | 3. **Multi-source retrieval** — the retrieval pipeline must support querying and merging results from two independent knowledge graphs
101 | 4. **Source provenance display** — the frontend must distinguish workspace citations from shared knowledge citations
102 | 
103 | ---
104 | 
105 | ## Out of Scope for this ADR
106 | 
107 | - Implementation timeline

- 0.9–1.0 : explicit, repeated, central to the document's argument

  }
]

Rules:
- Only use concept names from the provided list. No invention.
- Only create a relationship if the document text explicitly supports it.
- strength < 0.5 → exclude entirely.
- No self-referential relationships (source == target).
- Return [] if no clear relationships can be inferred.
"""

FUZZY_THRESHOLD = 80


class RelationshipItem(BaseModel):
    source: str
    target: str
    relationship_type: str = "related_to"
    strength: float = Field(default=0.7, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    reasoning: str = Field(default="")


def _fuzzy_resolve(name: str, name_to_id: dict[str, int]) -> int | None:
    if name.lower() in name_to_id:

    if result and result[1] >= FUZZY_THRESHOLD:
        logger.debug(f"Fuzzy matched '{name}' → '{result[0]}' (score {result[1]})")
        return name_to_id[result[0]]
    return None

    for attempt in range(2):

                system=RELATIONSHIP_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
                user=(
                    f"Known concepts:\n{concept_list_text}\n\n"
                    f"Document excerpt:\n{doc_chunk}"
                ),
                max_tokens=2048,

            raw = raw.strip()
            if raw.startswith("```"):
                raw = raw.split("```")[1]
                if raw.startswith("json"):

    return []

        .all()

        logger.info("[doc=%d] Fewer than 2 concepts in workspace, skipping relationship extraction.", doc.id)
        return []

    chunks = chunk_text_hierarchical(
        doc.raw_text or "",
        max_chars=settings.chunk_size * 4,
        overlap_chars=settings.chunk_overlap,
    )

    existing_pairs: set[tuple[int, int, str]] = set()

    for rel in db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id).all():
        existing_pairs.add((rel.source_concept_id, rel.target_concept_id, rel.relationship_type))

        raw_items = _call_llm(concept_list_text, chunk)
        for raw in raw_items:
            try:
                item = RelationshipItem(**raw)
            except ValidationError as ve:
                logger.warning("[doc=%d] Rejected relationship: %s — %s", doc.id, raw, ve)
                continue

            if item.strength < 0.5:
                continue

            if item.relationship_type not in ALLOWED_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES:
                item.relationship_type = "related_to"

            source_id = _fuzzy_resolve(item.source, name_to_id)
            target_id = _fuzzy_resolve(item.target, name_to_id)

            if source_id is None or target_id is None:
                continue
            if source_id == target_id:
                continue

            key = (source_id, target_id, item.relationship_type)
            if key in existing_pairs:
                continue

            rel = Relationship(
                workspace_id=doc.workspace_id,
                source_concept_id=source_id,
                target_concept_id=target_id,
                relationship_type=item.relationship_type,
                source_document_id=doc.id,
                strength=item.strength,
                reasoning=item.reasoning or None,
            )
            db.add(rel)
            existing_pairs.add(key)
            created.append(rel)

    db.commit()
    logger.info("[doc=%d] Extracted %d relationships.", doc.id, len(created))
    return created

You are an AI knowledge compiler for IBM Consulting.

You work strictly from what is written — never introduce general knowledge, external facts, or internet search results.

## What counts as a concept
A NAMED, REUSABLE entity that appears in IBM consulting work:
- Industry standards (ISO 20022, SWIFT, FIX protocol)
- Technologies & platforms (Kubernetes, AWS, SAP S/4HANA)
- IBM methodologies & frameworks
- Business processes (payment settlement, trade finance, KYC)
- Architecture patterns (microservices, event-driven, CQRS)
- Regulatory requirements (GDPR, MiFID II, Basel III)
- Organisational capabilities (API management, cloud governance)

NOT concepts: generic words (introduction, section, approach), vague phrases, pronouns.

## Confidence scoring
- 0.9–1.0 : explicitly named multiple times, central to the document
- 0.7–0.9 : clearly mentioned and relevant
- 0.5–0.7 : mentioned but peripheral
- < 0.5   : uncertain — EXCLUDE

Return ONLY a JSON array — no prose, no markdown fences:

Do NOT use general knowledge, training data, internet search, or any external information.
If the context does not support the answer to the question, you MUST respond with exactly:
"I could not find this in the uploaded knowledge. The question may fall outside the documents in this workspace."

When multiple passages describe the same topic, synthesise them into a single coherent answer rather

def _extract_keywords_llm(question: str) -> list[str]:
    """Extract search keywords from the question using the LLM at temperature=0."""
    try:
        raw = chat(
            system=KEYWORD_EXTRACTION_PROMPT,
            user=question,
            max_tokens=256,
            temperature=0.0,
        )
        raw = raw.strip()
        if raw.startswith("```"):
            raw = raw.split("```")[1]
            if raw.startswith("json"):
                raw = raw[4:]
        return json.loads(raw)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning("LLM keyword extraction failed: %s", e)
        return [w.strip(".,?!") for w in question.split() if len(w) > 4]


def _excerpt_fingerprint(text: str) -> str:
    """Return a short hash of a normalised excerpt for deduplication."""

    - Keyword extraction is deterministic (temperature=0).
    - Seed nodes are selected by cumulative scoring across all keywords

      same top seeds regardless of keyword ordering.
    - Retrieved concepts are assembled in a stable order: relevance score
      DESC, then concept confidence DESC, then concept ID ASC as tie-break.
    - Near-duplicate source excerpts are deduplicated before LLM generation
      so important passages are not pushed out of the context window.
    - Final generation is at temperature=0 to minimise structural variation.

    scored_seeds = find_nodes_semantic(G, keywords, top_k=settings.qa_top_k)

    if not scored_seeds:
        kw_lower = [k.lower() for k in keywords]
        db_matched = db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).all()
        scored_seeds = [
            (c.id, 0.7)
            for c in db_matched
            if any(kw in c.name.lower() for kw in kw_lower)
        ]

    seed_score: dict[int, float] = {nid: score for nid, score in scored_seeds}
    all_relevant_nodes: set[int] = set()
    all_relevant_edges: list = []

    for node_id, _score in scored_seeds:
        nbr_nodes, nbr_edges = get_neighbourhood(
            G,
            node_id,
            hops=settings.graph_hop_depth,
            strength_threshold=settings.graph_strength_threshold,
            max_nodes=settings.graph_max_nodes,
        )
        all_relevant_nodes.update(nbr_nodes)
        all_relevant_edges.extend(nbr_edges)

    source_refs: list[SourceRef] = []
    seen_doc_ids: set[int] = set()

        concepts.sort(

                if doc:
                    doc_name = doc.title or doc.filename

            context_parts.append(
                f"[Concept: {c.name}] ({c.type})\n"
                f"Description: {c.description}\n"
                f"Excerpt from '{doc_name}': {c.source_excerpt}"

            if c.source_document_id and c.source_document_id not in seen_doc_ids:
                seen_doc_ids.add(c.source_document_id)
                source_refs.append(SourceRef(
                    document_id=c.source_document_id,
                    document_name=doc_name,
                    excerpt=c.source_excerpt[:300],

                context_parts.append(
                    f"[Pattern: {p.name}]\n"
                    f"Problem: {p.problem_statement}\n"
                    f"IBM Approach:\n{steps}"
                )
                for did in (p.source_document_ids or []):
                    if did not in seen_doc_ids:
                        doc = db.get(Document, int(did))
                        if doc:
                            seen_doc_ids.add(did)
                            source_refs.append(SourceRef(
                                document_id=did,
                                document_name=doc.title or doc.filename,
                                excerpt="(Pattern source)",
                            ))

    if not context_parts:
        answer = (
            "I could not find this in the uploaded knowledge. "

        )

    context_text = "\n\n---\n\n".join(context_parts)

    try:

            user=f"Context:\n{context_text}\n\nQuestion: {question}",
            max_tokens=2048,
            temperature=0.0,
        )
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error("QA generation failed: %s", e)
        answer = "An error occurred while generating the answer. Please try again."
        source_refs = []

    not_found_signal = any(
        phrase in answer.lower()
        for phrase in ("not found", "cannot find", "outside the documents", "could not find")
    )
    if not not_found_signal and not source_refs:
        answer = (
            "I could not find this in the uploaded knowledge. "
            "The question may fall outside the documents in this workspace."
        )
        source_refs = []

    _save_chat(db, workspace_id, question, answer, [s.document_id for s in source_refs])
    return AskResponse(answer=answer, sources=source_refs)


def _save_chat(db: Session, workspace_id: int, question: str, answer: str, doc_ids: list[int]) -> None:
    db.add(ChatMessage(workspace_id=workspace_id, role="user", content=question, source_document_ids=[]))
    db.add(ChatMessage(workspace_id=workspace_id, role="assistant", content=answer, source_document_ids=doc_ids))
    db.commit()

        all_relevant_edges.extend(nbr_edges)

    context_parts: list[str] = []
    source_refs: list[SourceRef] = []
    seen_doc_ids: set[int] = set()
    seen_excerpt_hashes: set[str] = set()

    if all_relevant_nodes:
        concepts = db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.id.in_(list(all_relevant_nodes))).all()

        # Stable sort: seed_score DESC → concept.confidence DESC → concept.id ASC
        # Nodes reached via BFS (not direct seeds) get score 0.0 and sort last.
        concepts.sort(
            key=lambda c: (
                -seed_score.get(c.id, 0.0),
                -float(getattr(c, "confidence", 0.8)),
                c.id,
            )
        )

        for c in concepts:
            if not c.source_excerpt:
                continue

            # Skip near-duplicate excerpts to avoid redundant context
            fp = _excerpt_fingerprint(c.source_excerpt)
            if fp in seen_excerpt_hashes:
                continue
            seen_excerpt_hashes.add(fp)

            doc_name = "Unknown Document"
            if c.source_document_id:
                doc = db.get(Document, c.source_document_id)
                if doc:
                    doc_name = doc.title or doc.filename

            context_parts.append(
                f"[Concept: {c.name}] ({c.type})\n"
                f"Description: {c.description}\n"
                f"Excerpt from '{doc_name}': {c.source_excerpt}"
            )
            if c.source_document_id and c.source_document_id not in seen_doc_ids:
                seen_doc_ids.add(c.source_document_id)
                source_refs.append(SourceRef(
                    document_id=c.source_document_id,
                    document_name=doc_name,
                    excerpt=c.source_excerpt[:300],
                ))

        # Consulting patterns that overlap with matched concepts
        patterns = (
            db.query(ConsultingPattern)
            .filter(ConsultingPattern.workspace_id == workspace_id)
            .all()
        )
        for p in patterns:
            rel_ids = p.related_concept_ids or []
            if any(nid in rel_ids for nid in all_relevant_nodes):
                steps = "\n".join(f"  {s}" for s in (p.ibm_approach or []))
                context_parts.append(
                    f"[Pattern: {p.name}]\n"
                    f"Problem: {p.problem_statement}\n"
                    f"IBM Approach:\n{steps}"
                )
                for did in (p.source_document_ids or []):
                    if did not in seen_doc_ids:
                        doc = db.get(Document, int(did))
                        if doc:
                            seen_doc_ids.add(did)
                            source_refs.append(SourceRef(
                                document_id=did,
                                document_name=doc.title or doc.filename,
                                excerpt="(Pattern source)",
                            ))

    if not context_parts:
        answer = (
            "I could not find this in the uploaded knowledge. "
            "The question may fall outside the documents in this workspace."
        )
        _save_chat(db, workspace_id, question, answer, [])
        return AskResponse(answer=answer, sources=[])

    context_text = "\n\n---\n\n".join(context_parts)

    try:
        answer = chat(
            system=QA_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
            user=f"Context:\n{context_text}\n\nQuestion: {question}",
            max_tokens=2048,
            temperature=0.0,
        )
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error("QA generation failed: %s", e)
        answer = "An error occurred while generating the answer. Please try again."
        source_refs = []

    not_found_signal = any(
        phrase in answer.lower()
        for phrase in ("not found", "cannot find", "outside the documents", "could not find")
    )
    if not not_found_signal and not source_refs:
        answer = (
            "I could not find this in the uploaded knowledge. "
            "The question may fall outside the documents in this workspace."
        )
        source_refs = []

    _save_chat(db, workspace_id, question, answer, [s.document_id for s in source_refs])
    return AskResponse(answer=answer, sources=source_refs)


def _save_chat(db: Session, workspace_id: int, question: str, answer: str, doc_ids: list[int]) -> None:
    db.add(ChatMessage(workspace_id=workspace_id, role="user", content=question, source_document_ids=[]))
    db.add(ChatMessage(workspace_id=workspace_id, role="assistant", content=answer, source_document_ids=doc_ids))
    db.commit()

"""
Shared LLM client — IBM Consulting Advantage, Claude Code endpoint.

Wraps the Anthropic SDK with:
  - Secret retrieval via SecretProvider (no direct os.getenv access)
  - httpx.Timeout: explicit connect / read / write limits — no indefinite hangs
  - Tenacity retry: exponential backoff + jitter for transient failures
  - Circuit breaker: rejects calls fast when the provider is unhealthy
  - Structured observability: latency, token counts, cost, retry count per call

Timeout defaults (all configurable via environment):
  LLM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT   10 s   TCP handshake + TLS
  LLM_READ_TIMEOUT     120 s   time waiting for the first response byte
  LLM_WRITE_TIMEOUT     30 s   time uploading the request body

Retry defaults:
  LLM_MAX_RETRIES        4     attempts after the first (total 5 tries)
  LLM_RETRY_MAX_WAIT    30 s   cap on per-attempt backoff sleep

Caller contract:
  - Raises fastapi.HTTPException(503) when the circuit breaker is open.
  - Raises fastapi.HTTPException(503) when all retry attempts are exhausted.
  - Raises any non-transient anthropic.* / httpx.* exception immediately.

Usage
-----
from app.llm_client import chat

response_text = chat(
    system="You are a knowledge compiler...",
    user="What is ISO 20022?",
    max_tokens=2048,
    operation="workspace_chat",
)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
import uuid
from functools import lru_cache

import anthropic
import httpx
from fastapi import HTTPException
from tenacity import RetryError

from app.config import settings
from app.llm.circuit_breaker import circuit_breaker
from app.llm.retry import llm_retry, _is_transient
from app.security.secrets import get_secret_provider

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# ── Client factory ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def _get_client() -> anthropic.Anthropic:
    """
    Build and cache the Anthropic SDK client.

    The API key is fetched via SecretProvider — never directly from os.environ.
    httpx.Timeout is applied here so every request shares the same limits.
    """
    provider = get_secret_provider()
    api_key = provider.get_secret(settings.claude_secret_name)
    timeout = httpx.Timeout(
        connect=settings.llm_connect_timeout,
        read=settings.llm_read_timeout,
        write=settings.llm_write_timeout,
        pool=settings.llm_connect_timeout,
    )
    return anthropic.Anthropic(
        api_key=api_key,
        base_url=settings.claude_base_url,
        timeout=timeout,
    )


# ── Core API call (retried) ───────────────────────────────────────────

def _call_api(
    system: str,
    user: str,
    max_tokens: int,
    temperature: float,
) -> anthropic.types.Message:
    """
    Execute one Anthropic messages.create call.
    Wrapped by chat() with the tenacity retry decorator.
    This function is intentionally thin — one responsibility: call the SDK.
    """
    client = _get_client()
    return client.messages.create(
        model=settings.claude_model,
        max_tokens=max_tokens,
        temperature=temperature,
        system=system,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}],
    )


# ── Public interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

def chat(
    system: str,
    user: str,
    max_tokens: int = 2048,
    temperature: float = 0.2,
    operation: str = "llm_call",
) -> str:
    """
    Send a single chat completion via Claude and return the text response.

    Parameters
    ----------
    system      : System prompt text.
    user        : User turn content.
    max_tokens  : Upper bound on generated tokens.
    temperature : Sampling temperature (0.0 for deterministic QA).
    operation   : Logical label for observability logs (e.g. 'concept_extraction').

    Raises
    ------
    fastapi.HTTPException(503) — circuit breaker open, or retries exhausted.
    anthropic.AuthenticationError — bad API key (not retried).
    """
    request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    retry_count = 0

    # Build a fresh retry decorator each call so monkeypatching settings in
    # tests immediately takes effect without restarting the process.
    _retried_call = llm_retry()(_call_api)

    with circuit_breaker:
        try:
            message = _retried_call(system, user, max_tokens, temperature)

        except RetryError as exc:
            # All attempts exhausted — unwrap and log the root cause.
            cause = exc.last_attempt.exception()
            retry_count = exc.last_attempt.attempt_number - 1
            logger.error(
                "[req=%s op=%s] LLM call failed after %d retries. "
                "Final error: %s %s",
                request_id, operation, retry_count,
                type(cause).__name__, cause,
            )
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=503,
                detail="LLM request failed after multiple retry attempts. Please try again shortly.",
            ) from exc

        except Exception:
            # Non-transient error (auth failure, budget 429, etc.) — let it propagate.
            raise

    latency_ms = (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000

    # Attempt count is tracked inside tenacity's statistics attribute when reraise=False,
    # but since we call _call_api directly we count from the RetryError path above.
    # For successful paths, infer attempt count from tenacity statistics if available.
    stats = getattr(_retried_call, "statistics", {})
    retry_count = max(0, stats.get("attempt_number", 1) - 1)

    usage = message.usage
    prompt_tokens     = getattr(usage, "input_tokens",  0)
    completion_tokens = getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0)

    from app.llm.usage_tracker import estimate_cost  # noqa: PLC0415
    cost = estimate_cost(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)

    logger.info(
        "[req=%s op=%s] LLM call completed: model=%s latency=%.0fms "
        "prompt_tokens=%d completion_tokens=%d cost=$%.6f retries=%d",
        request_id, operation, settings.claude_model, latency_ms,
        prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost, retry_count,
    )

    return message.content[0].text or ""

"""
LLM governance layer — budget enforcement and workspace-level rate limiting.

Budget enforcement (Phase 4)
-----------------------------
Before every LLM call, check_budget() queries the workspace's LLMBudget row.
  - If monthly_token_limit > 0 and current_token_usage >= limit → HTTP 429
  - If monthly_cost_limit  > 0 and current_cost_usage  >= limit → HTTP 429
  - Limits of 0 mean unlimited (default for new workspaces).

Rate limiting (Phase 7)
-----------------------
A simple in-process sliding-window counter per workspace.
  - Window: 60 seconds (configurable via LLM_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS)
  - Limit:  MAX_LLM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE per workspace (default 60)
  - Returns HTTP 429 when the window is full.

Note: this in-process rate limiter is suitable for a single-process deployment.
For a multi-process/multi-node deployment replace with a Redis-backed counter.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import logging
import threading
import time

from fastapi import HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.config import settings
from app.db.models import LLMBudget

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# ── Budget enforcement ────────────────────────────────────────────────

def check_budget(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> None:
    """
    Raise HTTP 429 if the workspace has exceeded its monthly token or cost budget.
    No-op if no budget row exists (unlimited by default).
    """
    budget = (
        db.query(LLMBudget)
        .filter(LLMBudget.workspace_id == workspace_id)
        .first()
    )
    if budget is None:
        return

    if budget.monthly_token_limit > 0:
        if budget.current_token_usage >= budget.monthly_token_limit:
            logger.warning(
                "[ws=%d] Token budget exceeded: %d / %d",
                workspace_id, budget.current_token_usage, budget.monthly_token_limit,
            )
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=429,
                detail=(
                    f"Workspace LLM token budget exceeded "
                    f"({budget.current_token_usage:,} / {budget.monthly_token_limit:,} tokens used this month)."
                ),
            )

    if budget.monthly_cost_limit > 0.0:
        if budget.current_cost_usage >= budget.monthly_cost_limit:
            logger.warning(
                "[ws=%d] Cost budget exceeded: $%.4f / $%.4f",
                workspace_id, budget.current_cost_usage, budget.monthly_cost_limit,
            )
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=429,
                detail=(
                    f"Workspace LLM cost budget exceeded "
                    f"(${budget.current_cost_usage:.4f} / ${budget.monthly_cost_limit:.4f} spent this month)."
                ),
            )


# ── Rate limiting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_rate_lock   = threading.Lock()
# workspace_id → deque of request timestamps (float, monotonic)
_rate_windows: dict[int, collections.deque] = collections.defaultdict(
    lambda: collections.deque()
)


def check_rate_limit(workspace_id: int) -> None:
    """
    Raise HTTP 429 if the workspace has made more than
    MAX_LLM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE LLM calls in the last LLM_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS.
    """
    limit  = settings.max_llm_requests_per_minute
    window = settings.llm_rate_window_seconds
    now    = time.monotonic()
    cutoff = now - window

    with _rate_lock:
        dq = _rate_windows[workspace_id]
        # Remove timestamps outside the current window
        while dq and dq[0] < cutoff:
            dq.popleft()

        if len(dq) >= limit:
            logger.warning(
                "[ws=%d] LLM rate limit hit: %d requests in %.0fs window.",
                workspace_id, len(dq), window,
            )
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=429,
                detail=(
                    f"LLM request rate limit exceeded "
                    f"({limit} requests per {window:.0f}s). Please slow down."
                ),
            )

        dq.append(now)

# Knowledge Intelligence Platform

**An evidence-grounded knowledge compiler that transforms consulting assets into a connected intelligence layer of concepts, relationships, consulting patterns, and reusable expertise.**

Every AI-generated insight is traceable back to source evidence from uploaded assets. No external knowledge. No fabricated citations.

---

## Problem Statement

Organisations produce vast amounts of institutional knowledge — Points of View, Business Requirements Documents, proposal decks, architecture documents, research papers, case studies, and delivery playbooks. This knowledge is trapped across disconnected files, siloed in individual experts, and rarely reused effectively.

When a practitioner starts a new engagement, they have no reliable way to ask:
- *Has this problem been solved before, and where is the evidence?*
- *How do these concepts connect across our body of work?*
- *What is our organisation's documented position on this topic?*

The result: knowledge is repeatedly rediscovered, deliverables are drafted from scratch, and AI tools produce answers from their training data rather than from your organisation's own documented expertise.

---

## Solution

The Knowledge Intelligence Platform compiles your consulting content into a structured, connected knowledge layer:

| What you upload | What the platform builds |
|---|---|
| PDFs, DOCX, PPTX files | **Concepts** — named, typed, with verbatim source excerpts |
| Documents across a domain | **Relationships** — how concepts connect across documents |
| A body of work | **Consulting Patterns** — recurring approaches to recurring problems |
| All of the above | **Knowledge Graph** — an interactive, explorable intelligence layer |
| Questions | **Evidence-grounded answers** — every claim traced to a source document |
| A topic + audience | **Client-ready deliverables** — POVs, executive summaries, roadmaps |

---

## LLM Governance

Every LLM call passes through a governance pipeline before reaching the provider:

| Layer | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Secret Provider** | API key fetched via `SecretProvider` abstraction — never directly from `os.environ` in business logic. Swap to `AWSSecretsManagerProvider` for production with zero code changes |
| **Circuit Breaker** | Opens after 5 consecutive failures; auto-recovers after 60s. Rejects all calls while open (HTTP 503) to prevent cascade failures |
| **Rate Limiter** | Per-workspace sliding-window counter — default 60 requests/min. Returns HTTP 429 when exceeded |
| **Budget Check** | Per-workspace monthly token and cost limits enforced before each call. Returns HTTP 429 when exceeded |
| **Usage Tracker** | Every call writes one `LLMUsage` row with token counts and estimated cost. Running totals accumulated in `LLMBudget` |
| **Observability** | Structured log lines include workspace ID, operation, latency, token counts, and cost estimate. API keys, prompts, and credentials are never logged |

Admin visibility: `GET /admin/llm/usage` and `GET /admin/llm/budgets` return usage aggregates and budget status.

---

## Upload Security

Every uploaded file passes through a three-stage validation pipeline before it touches the filesystem or a parser:

| Stage | What is checked | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Magic-byte detection** | Actual file format — not the filename or `Content-Type` header | `filetype` library reads the binary signature from the first 8 KB |
| **Allow-list enforcement** | Only PDF, DOCX, PPTX are accepted | Any other detected MIME type returns HTTP 422 |
| **Size limit** | Default 25 MB per file, configurable via `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | Streamed check — oversized files return HTTP 413 before being fully buffered |

**Why magic bytes instead of extensions?** A file named `malware.pdf` with a ZIP or executable binary inside will pass an extension check but fail the magic-byte check. Attackers control the filename and `Content-Type` header; they do not control the binary content signature.

All parsers (PyMuPDF, python-docx, python-pptx) are wrapped with defensive exception handling. A corrupt or malformed file marks the document as `failed` with a clean error message — no stack traces are ever exposed to the client.

---

## Key Features

### Workspace Management
Isolated knowledge domains. Each workspace contains its own documents, concepts, relationships, and patterns. No cross-workspace knowledge leakage.

### Document Processing
Upload PDF, DOCX, or PPTX files. The platform automatically runs a four-stage compilation pipeline: text extraction → concept detection → relationship mapping → pattern recognition. No manual tagging required.

### Knowledge Extraction
Three chained extraction agents compile documents into the knowledge graph:
- **Concept Agent** — extracts named entities, standards, technologies, methodologies with confidence scoring
- **Relationship Agent** — discovers how concepts connect across documents using fuzzy name resolution
- **Pattern Agent** — identifies recurring consulting patterns from the full workspace knowledge structure

### Evidence-Grounded Assistant
Ask questions in natural language. The assistant retrieves relevant context using graph-first traversal (not keyword search), assembles evidence from the knowledge graph, and generates answers that cite their exact source document and excerpt. If the answer is not in your documents, it says so explicitly. Fabrication is architecturally prevented.

### Interactive Knowledge Graph
Explore compiled knowledge as an interactive node-edge graph. Click any concept to see its definition, verbatim source evidence, connected concepts, and relationship types. Built on React Flow with strength-weighted edges.

### Deliverable Generation
Generate client-ready consulting documents (Point of View, Executive Summary, Roadmap) directly from compiled workspace knowledge. Every section cites source documents. Export as Markdown or DOCX.

---

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Browser  (React + TypeScript)               │
│  Workspace List │ Document Upload │ Knowledge Graph          │
│  Assistant Chat │ Deliverable Generator                      │
└───────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                            │  HTTP/REST — Vite proxy → :8000
                            ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            Knowledge Intelligence Platform  (FastAPI)        │
│                                                              │
│  Ingestion          Knowledge Compiler     Graph Engine      │
│  PyMuPDF            Concept Agent          NetworkX          │
│  python-docx        Relationship Agent     builder.py        │

## How It Works

### 1. Knowledge Compilation (Upload → Concepts → Graph)

When you upload a document, the platform runs three chained extraction agents:

1. **Concept Agent** — reads the document text and extracts named concepts with verbatim source excerpts and confidence scores. Concepts below the confidence threshold are discarded.
2. **Relationship Agent** — looks across all workspace concepts and identifies how this document's concepts connect to existing ones. Relationship strength is scored and stored.
3. **Pattern Agent** — examines the full workspace concept and relationship map and identifies recurring consulting patterns.

Every extracted item carries a `source_document_id` and `source_excerpt`. Items without traceable sources are rejected before storage.

### 2. Evidence-Grounded Q&A (Question → Answer)

When you ask a question:

1. Keywords are extracted from the question (LLM-assisted, temperature=0)
2. Concept nodes are scored using **cumulative multi-signal matching** across all keywords — exact name, substring, type, description — weighted by concept confidence
3. The top seeds are expanded via **strength-filtered BFS** through the knowledge graph
4. Retrieved concepts are sorted deterministically: seed relevance DESC, confidence DESC, then concept ID as tie-break
5. Near-duplicate source excerpts are deduplicated before the context window is assembled
6. Claude generates an answer from the context at temperature=0, citing every claim with `[Source: Document Name]`
7. If the answer is non-empty but sources are empty, it is rejected — the grounding rule is enforced at the `SourcedResponseMixin` schema level, not just in a prompt

### 3. Grounding Rule (Hard Constraint)

The platform does not use internet search, web browsing, or general knowledge for any compilation, answer, or deliverable. The `SourcedResponseMixin` in `schemas.py` is a Pydantic `model_validator` that runs before any AI response leaves the API. An answer without sources is a schema validation error.

# Knowledge Intelligence Platform

**An evidence-grounded knowledge compiler that transforms consulting assets into a connected intelligence layer of concepts, relationships, consulting patterns, and reusable expertise.**

Every AI-generated insight is traceable back to source evidence from uploaded assets. No external knowledge. No fabricated citations.

---

## Problem Statement

Organisations produce vast amounts of institutional knowledge — Points of View, Business Requirements Documents, proposal decks, architecture documents, research papers, case studies, and delivery playbooks. This knowledge is trapped across disconnected files, siloed in individual experts, and rarely reused effectively.

When a practitioner starts a new engagement, they have no reliable way to ask:
- *Has this problem been solved before, and where is the evidence?*
- *How do these concepts connect across our body of work?*
- *What is our organisation's documented position on this topic?*

The result: knowledge is repeatedly rediscovered, deliverables are drafted from scratch, and AI tools produce answers from their training data rather than from your organisation's own documented expertise.

---

## Solution

The Knowledge Intelligence Platform compiles your consulting content into a structured, connected knowledge layer:

| What you upload | What the platform builds |
|---|---|
| PDFs, DOCX, PPTX files | **Concepts** — named, typed, with verbatim source excerpts |
| Documents across a domain | **Relationships** — how concepts connect across documents |
| A body of work | **Consulting Patterns** — recurring approaches to recurring problems |
| All of the above | **Knowledge Graph** — an interactive, explorable intelligence layer |
| Questions | **Evidence-grounded answers** — every claim traced to a source document |
| A topic + audience | **Client-ready deliverables** — POVs, executive summaries, roadmaps |

---

## LLM Governance

Every LLM call passes through a governance pipeline before reaching the provider:

| Layer | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Secret Provider** | API key fetched via `SecretProvider` abstraction — never directly from `os.environ` in business logic. Swap to `AWSSecretsManagerProvider` for production with zero code changes |
| **Circuit Breaker** | Opens after 5 consecutive failures; auto-recovers after 60s. Rejects all calls while open (HTTP 503) to prevent cascade failures |
| **Rate Limiter** | Per-workspace sliding-window counter — default 60 requests/min. Returns HTTP 429 when exceeded |
| **Budget Check** | Per-workspace monthly token and cost limits enforced before each call. Returns HTTP 429 when exceeded |
| **Usage Tracker** | Every call writes one `LLMUsage` row with token counts and estimated cost. Running totals accumulated in `LLMBudget` |
| **Observability** | Structured log lines include workspace ID, operation, latency, token counts, and cost estimate. API keys, prompts, and credentials are never logged |

Admin visibility: `GET /admin/llm/usage` and `GET /admin/llm/budgets` return usage aggregates and budget status.

---

## Upload Security

Every uploaded file passes through a three-stage validation pipeline before it touches the filesystem or a parser:

| Stage | What is checked | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Magic-byte detection** | Actual file format — not the filename or `Content-Type` header | `filetype` library reads the binary signature from the first 8 KB |
| **Allow-list enforcement** | Only PDF, DOCX, PPTX are accepted | Any other detected MIME type returns HTTP 422 |
| **Size limit** | Default 25 MB per file, configurable via `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | Streamed check — oversized files return HTTP 413 before being fully buffered |

**Why magic bytes instead of extensions?** A file named `malware.pdf` with a ZIP or executable binary inside will pass an extension check but fail the magic-byte check. Attackers control the filename and `Content-Type` header; they do not control the binary content signature.

All parsers (PyMuPDF, python-docx, python-pptx) are wrapped with defensive exception handling. A corrupt or malformed file marks the document as `failed` with a clean error message — no stack traces are ever exposed to the client.

---

## Key Features

### Workspace Management
Isolated knowledge domains. Each workspace contains its own documents, concepts, relationships, and patterns. No cross-workspace knowledge leakage.

### Document Processing
Upload PDF, DOCX, or PPTX files. The platform automatically runs a four-stage compilation pipeline: text extraction → concept detection → relationship mapping → pattern recognition. No manual tagging required.

### Knowledge Extraction
Three chained extraction agents compile documents into the knowledge graph:
- **Concept Agent** — extracts named entities, standards, technologies, methodologies with confidence scoring
- **Relationship Agent** — discovers how concepts connect across documents using fuzzy name resolution
- **Pattern Agent** — identifies recurring consulting patterns from the full workspace knowledge structure

### Evidence-Grounded Assistant
Ask questions in natural language. The assistant retrieves relevant context using graph-first traversal (not keyword search), assembles evidence from the knowledge graph, and generates answers that cite their exact source document and excerpt. If the answer is not in your documents, it says so explicitly. Fabrication is architecturally prevented.

### Interactive Knowledge Graph
Explore compiled knowledge as an interactive node-edge graph. Click any concept to see its definition, verbatim source evidence, connected concepts, and relationship types. Built on React Flow with strength-weighted edges.

### Deliverable Generation
Generate client-ready consulting documents (Point of View, Executive Summary, Roadmap) directly from compiled workspace knowledge. Every section cites source documents. Export as Markdown or DOCX.
