79 | 
80 | def _build_provenance_graph(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> nx.DiGraph:
81 |     """
82 |     Build a provenance-aware graph from SQL.
83 | 
84 |     Differs from builder.build_workspace_graph() in that each node and edge
85 |     carries a `source_document_ids` set and `evidence_count` integer, which
86 |     enable incremental add/remove operations without a full SQL rebuild.
87 |     """
88 |     G = nx.DiGraph()
89 | 
90 |     concepts = db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).all()
91 |     for c in concepts:
92 |         G.add_node(c.id, **_node_attrs_from_concept(c))
93 | 
94 |     relationships = db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == workspace_id).all()
95 |     for r in relationships:
96 |         if not (G.has_node(r.source_concept_id) and G.has_node(r.target_concept_id)):
97 |             continue
98 |         G.add_edge(r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id, **_edge_attrs_from_relationship(r))
99 | 
100 |     return G
101 | 
102 | 
103 | # ── Manager ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
104 | 
105 | 
106 | class GraphMemoryManager:
107 |     """
108 |     Manages the lifecycle of in-memory workspace graphs.
109 | 
110 |     One instance is created at module level as the application singleton.
111 |     All services call get_workspace_graph() instead of build_workspace_graph().
112 |     """
113 | 
114 |     def __init__(self) -> None:
115 |         self._store = WorkspaceGraphStore()
116 |         self._build_lock: dict[int, threading.Lock] = {}
117 |         self._meta_lock = threading.Lock()
118 | 
119 |     # ── startup ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
120 | 
121 |     def startup_load(self) -> None:
122 |         """
123 |         Load all workspaces with at least one complete document into memory.
124 |         Called once from main.py lifespan after init_db().
125 |         """
126 |         db = SessionLocal()
127 |         try:
128 |             from app.db.models import Document  # local import avoids circular dependency
129 |             workspace_ids = (
130 |                 db.query(Workspace.id)
131 |                 .join(Document, Document.workspace_id == Workspace.id)
132 |                 .filter(Document.upload_status == "complete")
133 |                 .distinct()
134 |                 .all()
135 |             )
136 |             ws_ids = [row[0] for row in workspace_ids]
137 |             logger.info(
138 |                 "[graph_memory] Startup load: %d workspace(s) with complete documents.",
139 |                 len(ws_ids),
140 |             )
141 |             for ws_id in ws_ids:
142 |                 t0 = time.monotonic()
143 |                 G = _build_provenance_graph(db, ws_id)
144 |                 self._store.put(ws_id, G)
145 |                 logger.info(
146 |                     "[graph_memory] ws=%d loaded: %d nodes, %d edges (%.0fms)",
147 |                     ws_id, G.number_of_nodes(), G.number_of_edges(),
148 |                     (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,
149 |                 )
150 |         except Exception:
151 |             logger.exception("[graph_memory] Startup load failed — graphs will be built on first access.")
152 |         finally:
153 |             db.close()
154 | 
155 |     # ── read ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
156 | 
157 |     def get_workspace_graph(self, workspace_id: int, db: Session | None = None) -> nx.DiGraph:
158 |         """
159 |         Return the in-memory graph for this workspace.
160 | 
161 |         If the graph is not yet loaded, builds it from SQL (cache miss).
162 |         A per-workspace lock prevents duplicate builds when two requests arrive
163 |         simultaneously for an un-loaded workspace.
164 | 
165 |         Parameters
166 |         ----------
167 |         workspace_id : the workspace to retrieve.
168 |         db           : optional SQLAlchemy session; only used on cache miss.
169 |                        If None on a miss, a new session is opened internally.
170 |         """
171 |         G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
172 |         if G is not None:
173 |             return G
174 | 
175 |         build_lock = self._get_build_lock(workspace_id)
176 |         with build_lock:
177 |             # Re-check after acquiring the lock — another thread may have built it.
178 |             G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
179 |             if G is not None:
180 |                 return G
181 | 
182 |             return self._build_and_store(workspace_id, db)
183 | 
184 |     # ── incremental add ───────────────────────────────────────────────
185 | 
186 |     def add_document_contributions(self, workspace_id: int, document_id: int, db: Session) -> None:
187 |         """
188 |         Incrementally add a document's concepts and relationships to the
189 |         workspace graph.  If the graph is not loaded, performs a full build
190 |         from SQL (which will include the new document's contributions naturally).
191 | 
192 |         This is called by the ingestion pipeline immediately after
193 |         upload_status is set to "complete".
194 |         """
195 |         G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
196 |         if G is None:
197 |             self._build_and_store(workspace_id, db)
198 |             logger.info(
199 |                 "[graph_memory] ws=%d doc=%d — graph was not loaded; performed full build.",
200 |                 workspace_id, document_id,
201 |             )
202 |             self._bump_graph_version(db, workspace_id)
203 |             return
204 | 
205 |         t0 = time.monotonic()
206 |         build_lock = self._get_build_lock(workspace_id)
207 |         with build_lock:
208 |             # Load only concepts and relationships from this document.
209 |             new_concepts = (
210 |                 db.query(Concept)
211 |                 .filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id, Concept.source_document_id == document_id)
212 |                 .all()
213 |             )
214 |             new_relationships = (
215 |                 db.query(Relationship)
216 |                 .filter(
217 |                     Relationship.workspace_id == workspace_id,
218 |                     Relationship.source_document_id == document_id,
219 |                 )
220 |                 .all()
221 |             )
222 | 
223 |             nodes_added = 0
224 |             edges_added = 0
225 | 
226 |             for c in new_concepts:
227 |                 if G.has_node(c.id):
228 |                     # Merge provenance into existing node.
229 |                     existing_ids: set[int] = G.nodes[c.id].get("source_document_ids", set())
230 |                     existing_ids.add(document_id)
231 |                     G.nodes[c.id]["source_document_ids"] = existing_ids
232 |                     G.nodes[c.id]["evidence_count"] = len(existing_ids)
233 |                 else:
234 |                     G.add_node(c.id, **_node_attrs_from_concept(c))
235 |                     nodes_added += 1
236 | 
237 |             for r in new_relationships:
238 |                 if not (G.has_node(r.source_concept_id) and G.has_node(r.target_concept_id)):
239 |                     continue
240 |                 if G.has_edge(r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id):
241 |                     # Merge provenance into existing edge.
242 |                     existing_ids = G.edges[r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id].get(
243 |                         "source_document_ids", set()
244 |                     )
245 |                     existing_ids.add(document_id)
246 |                     G.edges[r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id]["source_document_ids"] = existing_ids
247 |                     G.edges[r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id]["evidence_count"] = len(existing_ids)
248 |                 else:
249 |                     G.add_edge(
250 |                         r.source_concept_id,
251 |                         r.target_concept_id,
252 |                         **_edge_attrs_from_relationship(r),
253 |                     )
254 |                     edges_added += 1
255 | 
256 |         self._bump_graph_version(db, workspace_id)
257 |         logger.info(
258 |             "[graph_memory] ws=%d doc=%d — incremental add: +%d nodes, +%d edges (%.0fms)",
259 |             workspace_id, document_id, nodes_added, edges_added,
260 |             (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,
261 |         )
262 | 
263 |     # ── incremental remove ────────────────────────────────────────────
264 | 
265 |     def remove_document_contributions(self, workspace_id: int, document_id: int) -> None:
266 |         """
267 |         Remove a document's evidence from the workspace graph.
268 | 
269 |         Nodes and edges that still have other supporting documents are kept;
270 |         only those whose entire evidence base was this document are removed.
271 |         This is called by the documents API immediately before the DB delete.
272 |         """
273 |         G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
274 |         if G is None:
275 |             # Nothing cached — the next access will rebuild from updated SQL.
276 |             return
277 | 
278 |         t0 = time.monotonic()
279 |         build_lock = self._get_build_lock(workspace_id)
280 |         with build_lock:
281 |             # Remove document from edge provenance; collect edges to delete.
282 |             edges_to_remove: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
283 |             for src, tgt, data in list(G.edges(data=True)):
284 |                 doc_ids: set[int] = data.get("source_document_ids", set())
285 |                 doc_ids.discard(document_id)

1 | """
2 | Pattern evolution tracker and threshold engine.
3 | 
4 | Determines whether pattern extraction should run after a graph update,
5 | based on how much the workspace's knowledge has grown since the last run.
6 | Records each extraction decision as a PatternExtractionRun audit row.
7 | """
8 | from __future__ import annotations
9 | 
10 | import logging
11 | from datetime import datetime
12 | 
13 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
14 | 
15 | from app.config import settings
16 | from app.db.models import Concept, PatternExtractionRun, Relationship, Workspace
17 | 
18 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
19 | 
20 | 
21 | def should_run_pattern_extraction(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> bool:
22 |     """
23 |     Return True if the workspace knowledge has grown enough since the last
24 |     pattern extraction run to justify re-running the pattern agent.
25 | 
26 |     Decision logic
27 |     --------------
28 |     1. If extraction has never run → always run.
29 |     2. Compute growth percentage for both concepts and relationships since
30 |        concept_count_at_last_pattern_run / relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run.
31 |     3. If either metric grew by ≥ PATTERN_EXTRACTION_THRESHOLD_PERCENT → run.
32 |     4. Otherwise skip and log the decision.
33 |     """
34 |     ws = db.get(Workspace, workspace_id)
35 |     if ws is None:
36 |         return False
37 | 
38 |     current_concept_count = (
39 |         db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).count()
40 |     )
41 |     current_rel_count = (
42 |         db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == workspace_id).count()
43 |     )
44 | 
45 |     prev_concept_count = ws.concept_count_at_last_pattern_run or 0
46 |     prev_rel_count = ws.relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run or 0
47 | 
48 |     # Always run if extraction has never happened
49 |     if prev_concept_count == 0 and prev_rel_count == 0:
50 |         logger.info(
51 |             "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — first extraction, running unconditionally "
52 |             "(concepts=%d, relationships=%d).",
53 |             workspace_id, current_concept_count, current_rel_count,
54 |         )
55 |         return True
56 | 
57 |     threshold = settings.pattern_extraction_threshold_pct
58 | 
59 |     concept_growth = (
60 |         ((current_concept_count - prev_concept_count) / prev_concept_count * 100)
61 |         if prev_concept_count > 0
62 |         else 100.0
63 |     )
64 |     rel_growth = (
65 |         ((current_rel_count - prev_rel_count) / prev_rel_count * 100)
66 |         if prev_rel_count > 0
67 |         else 0.0
68 |     )
69 | 
70 |     should_run = concept_growth >= threshold or rel_growth >= threshold
71 | 
72 |     logger.info(
73 |         "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — concept growth=%.1f%% (prev=%d, now=%d), "
74 |         "rel growth=%.1f%% (prev=%d, now=%d), threshold=%.1f%% → %s",
75 |         workspace_id,
76 |         concept_growth, prev_concept_count, current_concept_count,
77 |         rel_growth, prev_rel_count, current_rel_count,
78 |         threshold,
79 |         "RUN" if should_run else "SKIP",
80 |     )
81 |     return should_run
82 | 
83 | 
84 | def record_pattern_run(
85 |     db: Session,
86 |     workspace_id: int,
87 |     concept_count: int,
88 |     relationship_count: int,
89 |     patterns_generated: int,
90 |     status: str = "complete",
91 | ) -> PatternExtractionRun:
92 |     """
93 |     Persist a PatternExtractionRun audit row and update the Workspace
94 |     knowledge-evolution counters so the next threshold check is accurate.
95 |     """
96 |     ws = db.get(Workspace, workspace_id)
97 |     graph_version = ws.graph_version if ws else 0
98 | 
99 |     run = PatternExtractionRun(
100 |         workspace_id=workspace_id,
101 |         started_at=datetime.utcnow(),
102 |         completed_at=datetime.utcnow(),
103 |         concept_count=concept_count,
104 |         relationship_count=relationship_count,
105 |         patterns_generated=patterns_generated,
106 |         graph_version=graph_version,
107 |         status=status,
108 |     )
109 |     db.add(run)
110 | 
111 |     if ws:
112 |         ws.last_pattern_extraction_at = datetime.utcnow()
113 |         ws.concept_count_at_last_pattern_run = concept_count
114 |         ws.relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run = relationship_count
115 | 
116 |     db.commit()
117 |     logger.info(
118 |         "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — run recorded: status=%s concepts=%d rels=%d patterns=%d graph_v=%d",
119 |         workspace_id, status, concept_count, relationship_count, patterns_generated, graph_version,
120 |     )
121 |     return run

1 | """
2 | Shared LLM client — IBM Consulting Advantage, Claude Code endpoint.
3 | 
4 | Wraps the Anthropic SDK with:
5 |   - Secret retrieval via SecretProvider (no direct os.getenv access)
6 |   - httpx.Timeout: explicit connect / read / write limits — no indefinite hangs
7 |   - Tenacity retry: exponential backoff + jitter for transient failures
8 |   - Circuit breaker: rejects calls fast when the provider is unhealthy
9 |   - Structured observability: latency, token counts, cost, retry count per call
10 | 
11 | Timeout defaults (all configurable via environment):
12 |   LLM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT   10 s   TCP handshake + TLS
13 |   LLM_READ_TIMEOUT     120 s   time waiting for the first response byte
14 |   LLM_WRITE_TIMEOUT     30 s   time uploading the request body
15 | 
16 | Retry defaults:
17 |   LLM_MAX_RETRIES        4     attempts after the first (total 5 tries)
18 |   LLM_RETRY_MAX_WAIT    30 s   cap on per-attempt backoff sleep
19 | 
20 | Caller contract:
21 |   - Raises fastapi.HTTPException(503) when the circuit breaker is open.
22 |   - Raises fastapi.HTTPException(503) when all retry attempts are exhausted.
23 |   - Raises any non-transient anthropic.* / httpx.* exception immediately.
24 | 
25 | Usage
26 | -----
27 | from app.llm_client import chat
28 | 
29 | response_text = chat(
30 |     system="You are a knowledge compiler...",
31 |     user="What is ISO 20022?",
32 |     max_tokens=2048,
33 |     operation="workspace_chat",
34 | )
35 | """
36 | from __future__ import annotations
37 | 
38 | import logging
39 | import time
40 | import uuid
41 | from functools import lru_cache
42 | 
43 | import anthropic
44 | import httpx
45 | from fastapi import HTTPException
46 | from tenacity import RetryError
47 | 
48 | from app.config import settings
49 | from app.llm.circuit_breaker import circuit_breaker
50 | from app.llm.retry import llm_retry, _is_transient
51 | from app.security.secrets import get_secret_provider
52 | 
53 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
54 | 
55 | 
56 | # ── Client factory ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
57 | 
58 | @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
59 | def _get_client() -> anthropic.Anthropic:
60 |     """
61 |     Build and cache the Anthropic SDK client.
62 | 
63 |     The API key is fetched via SecretProvider — never directly from os.environ.
64 |     httpx.Timeout is applied here so every request shares the same limits.
65 |     """
66 |     provider = get_secret_provider()
67 |     api_key = provider.get_secret(settings.claude_secret_name)
68 |     timeout = httpx.Timeout(
69 |         connect=settings.llm_connect_timeout,
70 |         read=settings.llm_read_timeout,
71 |         write=settings.llm_write_timeout,
72 |         pool=settings.llm_connect_timeout,
73 |     )
74 |     return anthropic.Anthropic(
75 |         api_key=api_key,
76 |         base_url=settings.claude_base_url,
77 |         timeout=timeout,
78 |     )
79 | 
80 | 
81 | # ── Core API call (retried) ───────────────────────────────────────────
82 | 
83 | def _call_api(
84 |     system: str,
85 |     user: str,
86 |     max_tokens: int,
87 |     temperature: float,
88 | ) -> anthropic.types.Message:
89 |     """
90 |     Execute one Anthropic messages.create call.
91 |     Wrapped by chat() with the tenacity retry decorator.
92 |     This function is intentionally thin — one responsibility: call the SDK.
93 |     """
94 |     client = _get_client()
95 |     return client.messages.create(
96 |         model=settings.claude_model,
97 |         max_tokens=max_tokens,
98 |         temperature=temperature,
99 |         system=system,
100 |         messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}],
101 |     )
102 | 
103 | 
104 | # ── Public interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
105 | 
106 | def chat(
107 |     system: str,
108 |     user: str,
109 |     max_tokens: int = 2048,
110 |     temperature: float = 0.2,
111 |     operation: str = "llm_call",
112 | ) -> str:
113 |     """
114 |     Send a single chat completion via Claude and return the text response.
115 | 
116 |     Parameters
117 |     ----------
118 |     system      : System prompt text.
119 |     user        : User turn content.
120 |     max_tokens  : Upper bound on generated tokens.
121 |     temperature : Sampling temperature (0.0 for deterministic QA).
122 |     operation   : Logical label for observability logs (e.g. 'concept_extraction').
123 | 
124 |     Raises
125 |     ------
126 |     fastapi.HTTPException(503) — circuit breaker open, or retries exhausted.
127 |     anthropic.AuthenticationError — bad API key (not retried).
128 |     """
129 |     request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
130 |     t0 = time.monotonic()
131 |     retry_count = 0
132 | 
133 |     # Build a fresh retry decorator each call so monkeypatching settings in
134 |     # tests immediately takes effect without restarting the process.
135 |     _retried_call = llm_retry()(_call_api)
136 | 
137 |     with circuit_breaker:
138 |         try:
139 |             message = _retried_call(system, user, max_tokens, temperature)
140 | 
141 |         except RetryError as exc:
142 |             # All attempts exhausted — unwrap and log the root cause.
143 |             cause = exc.last_attempt.exception()
144 |             retry_count = exc.last_attempt.attempt_number - 1
145 |             logger.error(
146 |                 "[req=%s op=%s] LLM call failed after %d retries. "
147 |                 "Final error: %s %s",
148 |                 request_id, operation, retry_count,
149 |                 type(cause).__name__, cause,
150 |             )
151 |             raise HTTPException(
152 |                 status_code=503,
153 |                 detail="LLM request failed after multiple retry attempts. Please try again shortly.",
154 |             ) from exc
155 | 
156 |         except Exception:
157 |             # Non-transient error (auth failure, budget 429, etc.) — let it propagate.
158 |             raise
159 | 
160 |     latency_ms = (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000
161 | 
162 |     stats = getattr(_retried_call, "statistics", {})
163 |     retry_count = max(0, stats.get("attempt_number", 1) - 1)
164 | 
165 |     usage = message.usage
166 |     prompt_tokens     = getattr(usage, "input_tokens",  0)
167 |     completion_tokens = getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0)
168 | 
169 |     from app.llm.usage_tracker import estimate_cost  # noqa: PLC0415
170 |     cost = estimate_cost(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)
171 | 
172 |     logger.info(
173 |         "[req=%s op=%s] LLM call completed: model=%s latency=%.0fms "
174 |         "prompt_tokens=%d completion_tokens=%d cost=$%.6f retries=%d",
175 |         request_id, operation, settings.claude_model, latency_ms,
176 |         prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost, retry_count,
177 |     )
178 | 
179 |     return message.content[0].text or ""
180 |

---
## Goal
Build and maintain the **Knowledge Intelligence Platform** — an evidence-grounded knowledge compiler for IBM Consulting that transforms consulting assets (PDFs, DOCX, PPTX) into a structured knowledge graph of concepts, relationships, and consulting patterns, enabling evidence-backed Q&A and client-ready deliverable generation.

The most recent sprint is **Platform Hardening**: Data Integrity, Observability, Security, API Scalability, and Graph Performance. This sprint was **planned but not started** — all 21 todos were created but no code was written yet.

---

## Instructions

- **Never describe the platform as** a chatbot, RAG system, or document search tool
- **Always position as:** "Knowledge Intelligence Platform is an evidence-grounded knowledge compiler that transforms consulting assets into a connected intelligence layer of concepts, relationships, consulting patterns, and reusable expertise."
- All settings must come from environment variables via `backend/app/config.py` — no hardcoded secrets
- The grounding rule is **architectural**: `SourcedResponseMixin` in `schemas.py` is a Pydantic `model_validator` that rejects any AI response that has an answer but empty sources
- SQLAlchemy ORM only — no raw SQL in business logic
- NetworkX graph is a derived layer — SQL tables are canonical
- `temperature=0.0` for all QA calls for determinism
- Do not implement new features until explicitly asked
- The graph memory singleton (`graph_memory_manager`) must be cleared in test fixtures (`_store.clear()`) to avoid test pollution

---

## Discoveries

- **`venv/bin/python3` has a broken symlink** — use `venv/bin/pytest` for test runs
- **Test count progression**: 251 → 288 (after adding 37 graph memory tests)
- **`graph_memory_manager` is a module-level singleton** — tests that drop/recreate DB tables must also call `graph_memory_manager._store.clear()` in their `autouse` fixture
- **`detect_file_type()` in parsers.py was dead code** — removed in cleanup sprint (used `Path` and `Optional` imports that weren't present)
- **`datetime.utcnow()` is still used throughout** — models, services, pattern_evolution all use naive datetimes; Python 3.12 deprecates this
- **JSON arrays in models are the root integrity problem**: `ConsultingPattern.related_concept_ids`, `ConsultingPattern.source_document_ids`, `Deliverable.source_concept_ids`, `Deliverable.source_document_ids` are stored as JSON text — no FK integrity, no cascade, orphans possible
- **`nx.spring_layout()` runs on every `/graph` request** — computationally expensive and not cached
- **CORS is `allow_methods=["*"]`, `allow_headers=["*"]`** — overly permissive
- **No pagination anywhere** — all list endpoints return unbounded datasets
- **No structured logging** — plain `logger.info(f"...")` throughout, no JSON, no correlation IDs
- **`structlog` is not yet installed** — needs to be added to `requirements.txt`

---

### Completed (288 tests passing):

1. **General codebase cleanup** — removed dead `detect_file_type()`, removed "Bob" persona from all LLM prompts, fixed f-string logging, renamed `bob_knowledge_fabric.db` → `knowledge_platform.db`, added package docstrings, deleted 50 stale upload artifacts

5. **Persistent Graph Memory** — `backend/app/graph/store.py` (`WorkspaceGraphStore`), `backend/app/graph/memory_manager.py` (`GraphMemoryManager` singleton with provenance tracking, incremental add/remove, startup load). All callers (`qa_service`, `deliverable_service`, `api/graph.py`) use `graph_memory_manager.get_workspace_graph()` instead of `build_workspace_graph()`. 37 tests.

6. **Pattern Intelligence** — `backend/app/extraction/pattern_evolution.py` (threshold engine + audit records), `backend/app/db/models.py` (added `PatternExtractionRun` table + 5 `Workspace` knowledge-evolution columns), `backend/app/ingestion/pipeline.py` (threshold-gated pattern extraction, `add_document_contributions()` call). `PATTERN_EXTRACTION_THRESHOLD_PERCENT=10` env var.

1 | """
2 | Pattern evolution tracker and threshold engine.
3 | 
4 | Determines whether pattern extraction should run after a graph update,
5 | based on how much the workspace's knowledge has grown since the last run.
6 | Records each extraction decision as a PatternExtractionRun audit row.
7 | """
8 | from __future__ import annotations
9 | 
10 | import logging
11 | from datetime import datetime
12 | 
13 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
14 | 
15 | from app.config import settings
16 | from app.db.models import Concept, PatternExtractionRun, Relationship, Workspace
17 | 
18 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
19 | 
20 | 
21 | def should_run_pattern_extraction(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> bool:
22 |     """
23 |     Return True if the workspace knowledge has grown enough since the last
24 |     pattern extraction run to justify re-running the pattern agent.
25 | 
26 |     Decision logic
27 |     --------------
28 |     1. If extraction has never run → always run.
29 |     2. Compute growth percentage for both concepts and relationships since
30 |        concept_count_at_last_pattern_run / relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run.
31 |     3. If either metric grew by ≥ PATTERN_EXTRACTION_THRESHOLD_PERCENT → run.
32 |     4. Otherwise skip and log the decision.
33 |     """
34 |     ws = db.get(Workspace, workspace_id)
35 |     if ws is None:
36 |         return False
37 | 
38 |     current_concept_count = (
39 |         db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).count()
40 |     )
41 |     current_rel_count = (
42 |         db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == workspace_id).count()
43 |     )
44 | 
45 |     prev_concept_count = ws.concept_count_at_last_pattern_run or 0
46 |     prev_rel_count = ws.relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run or 0
47 | 
48 |     # Always run if extraction has never happened
49 |     if prev_concept_count == 0 and prev_rel_count == 0:
50 |         logger.info(
51 |             "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — first extraction, running unconditionally "
52 |             "(concepts=%d, relationships=%d).",
53 |             workspace_id, current_concept_count, current_rel_count,
54 |         )
55 |         return True
56 | 
57 |     threshold = settings.pattern_extraction_threshold_pct
58 | 
59 |     concept_growth = (
60 |         ((current_concept_count - prev_concept_count) / prev_concept_count * 100)
61 |         if prev_concept_count > 0
62 |         else 100.0
63 |     )
64 |     rel_growth = (
65 |         ((current_rel_count - prev_rel_count) / prev_rel_count * 100)
66 |         if prev_rel_count > 0
67 |         else 0.0
68 |     )
69 | 
70 |     should_run = concept_growth >= threshold or rel_growth >= threshold
71 | 
72 |     logger.info(
73 |         "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — concept growth=%.1f%% (prev=%d, now=%d), "
74 |         "rel growth=%.1f%% (prev=%d, now=%d), threshold=%.1f%% → %s",
75 |         workspace_id,
76 |         concept_growth, prev_concept_count, current_concept_count,
77 |         rel_growth, prev_rel_count, current_rel_count,
78 |         threshold,
79 |         "RUN" if should_run else "SKIP",
80 |     )
81 |     return should_run
82 | 
83 | 
84 | def record_pattern_run(
85 |     db: Session,
86 |     workspace_id: int,
87 |     concept_count: int,
88 |     relationship_count: int,
89 |     patterns_generated: int,
90 |     status: str = "complete",
91 | ) -> PatternExtractionRun:
92 |     """
93 |     Persist a PatternExtractionRun audit row and update the Workspace
94 |     knowledge-evolution counters so the next threshold check is accurate.
95 |     """
96 |     ws = db.get(Workspace, workspace_id)
97 |     graph_version = ws.graph_version if ws else 0
98 | 
99 |     run = PatternExtractionRun(
100 |         workspace_id=workspace_id,
101 |         started_at=datetime.utcnow(),
102 |         completed_at=datetime.utcnow(),
103 |         concept_count=concept_count,
104 |         relationship_count=relationship_count,
105 |         patterns_generated=patterns_generated,
106 |         graph_version=graph_version,
107 |         status=status,
108 |     )
109 |     db.add(run)
110 | 
111 |     if ws:
112 |         ws.last_pattern_extraction_at = datetime.utcnow()
113 |         ws.concept_count_at_last_pattern_run = concept_count
114 |         ws.relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run = relationship_count
115 | 
116 |     db.commit()
117 |     logger.info(
118 |         "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — run recorded: status=%s concepts=%d rels=%d patterns=%d graph_v=%d",
119 |         workspace_id, status, concept_count, relationship_count, patterns_generated, graph_version,
120 |     )
121 |     return run

1 | """
2 | Pattern extraction agent — uses the ICA LLM client.
3 | Given a workspace's full concept + relationship context,
4 | asks Bob to identify recurring consulting patterns.
5 | """
6 | from __future__ import annotations
7 | import json
8 | import logging
9 | from typing import Any
10 | 
11 | from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError
12 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
13 | from thefuzz import process as fuzzy_process
14 | 
15 | from app.db.models import Concept, Document, Relationship, ConsultingPattern
16 | from app.llm_client import chat
17 | 
18 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
19 | 
20 | PATTERN_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
21 | You are an AI knowledge compiler for IBM Consulting.
22 | Your role is to discover recurring consulting patterns from compiled workspace knowledge.
23 | Given a list of concepts and their relationships extracted from client and practice documents, identify recurring CONSULTING PATTERNS — repeatable approaches IBM uses to solve a class of client problem.
24 | You work strictly from the provided concepts and relationships — no external knowledge, no internet search, no fabrication.
25 | 
26 | Return ONLY a JSON array — no prose, no markdown fences:
27 | [
28 |   {
29 |     "name": "short pattern name, e.g. 'ISO 20022 Migration Pattern'",
30 |     "problem_statement": "1-2 sentence description of the class of client problem this pattern addresses",
31 |     "ibm_approach": [
32 |       "Step 1: ...",
33 |       "Step 2: ...",
34 |       "Step 3: ..."
35 |     ],
36 |     "related_concept_names": ["concept name 1", "concept name 2"],
37 |     "source_document_ids": []
38 |   }
39 | ]
40 | 
41 | Rules:
42 | - Only extract patterns that are genuinely supported by the concept/relationship data provided.
43 | - ibm_approach must have at least 2 steps.
44 | - related_concept_names must reference concept names from the provided list.
45 | - If no clear patterns emerge, return an empty array [].
46 | """
47 | 
48 | 
49 | class PatternItem(BaseModel):
50 |     name: str = Field(..., min_length=1)
51 |     problem_statement: str = Field(default="")
52 |     ibm_approach: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
53 |     related_concept_names: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
54 |     source_document_ids: list[int] = Field(default_factory=list)
55 | 
56 | 
57 | def _call_llm(context_text: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
58 |     for attempt in range(2):
59 |         try:
60 |             raw = chat(
61 |                 system=PATTERN_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
62 |                 user=context_text,
63 |                 max_tokens=4096,
64 |             )
65 |             raw = raw.strip()
66 |             if raw.startswith("```"):
67 |                 raw = raw.split("```")[1]
68 |                 if raw.startswith("json"):
69 |                     raw = raw[4:]
70 |             return json.loads(raw)
71 |         except (json.JSONDecodeError, IndexError) as e:
72 |             if attempt == 0:
73 |                 logger.warning("Pattern extraction JSON parse failed (attempt 1): %s", e)
74 |             else:
75 |                 logger.error("Pattern extraction JSON parse failed after retry: %s", e)
76 |                 return []
77 |     return []
78 | 
79 | 
80 | def extract_patterns(db: Session, doc: Document) -> list[ConsultingPattern]:
81 |     """Extract consulting patterns for the workspace after document ingestion."""
82 |     all_concepts = (
83 |         db.query(Concept)
84 |         .filter(Concept.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id)
85 |         .all()
86 |     )
87 |     if not all_concepts:
88 |         return []
89 | 
90 |     all_relationships = (
91 |         db.query(Relationship)
92 |         .filter(Relationship.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id)
93 |         .all()
94 |     )
95 | 
96 |     concept_lines = [f"- {c.name} ({c.type}): {c.description}" for c in all_concepts]
97 |     rel_lines = []
98 |     concept_id_to_name = {c.id: c.name for c in all_concepts}
99 |     for r in all_relationships:
100 |         src = concept_id_to_name.get(r.source_concept_id, "?")
101 |         tgt = concept_id_to_name.get(r.target_concept_id, "?")
102 |         rel_lines.append(f"- {src} {r.relationship_type} {tgt}")
103 | 
104 |     context = (
105 |         "Workspace Concepts:\n" + "\n".join(concept_lines) +
106 |         "\n\nWorkspace Relationships:\n" + ("\n".join(rel_lines) or "(none yet)") +
107 |         f"\n\nMost recently processed document: {doc.title or doc.filename}"
108 |     )
109 | 
110 |     raw_items = _call_llm(context)
111 |     name_to_concept = {c.name.lower(): c for c in all_concepts}
112 |     created: list[ConsultingPattern] = []
113 | 
114 |     for raw in raw_items:
115 |         try:
116 |             item = PatternItem(**raw)
117 |         except ValidationError as ve:
118 |             logger.warning("Rejected pattern: %s — %s", raw, ve)
119 |             continue
120 | 
121 |         if len(item.ibm_approach) < 2:
122 |             continue
123 | 
124 |         related_ids: list[int] = []
125 |         for cname in item.related_concept_names:
126 |             result = fuzzy_process.extractOne(cname.lower(), list(name_to_concept.keys()))
127 |             if result and result[1] >= 70:
128 |                 related_ids.append(name_to_concept[result[0]].id)
129 | 
130 |         existing = (
131 |             db.query(ConsultingPattern)
132 |             .filter(
133 |                 ConsultingPattern.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id,
134 |                 ConsultingPattern.name == item.name,
135 |             )
136 |             .first()
137 |         )
138 | 
139 |         doc_ids = list({doc.id} | {did for did in item.source_document_ids if isinstance(did, int)})
140 | 
141 |         if existing:
142 |             existing.problem_statement = item.problem_statement
143 |             existing.ibm_approach = item.ibm_approach
144 |             existing.related_concept_ids = related_ids
145 |             existing.source_document_ids = doc_ids
146 |         else:
147 |             pattern = ConsultingPattern(
148 |                 workspace_id=doc.workspace_id,
149 |                 name=item.name,
150 |                 problem_statement=item.problem_statement,
151 |                 ibm_approach=item.ibm_approach,
152 |                 related_concept_ids=related_ids,
153 |                 source_document_ids=doc_ids,
154 |             )
155 |             db.add(pattern)
156 |             created.append(pattern)
157 | 
158 |     db.commit()
159 |     logger.info("[doc=%d] Extracted/updated %d patterns.", doc.id, len(created))
160 |     return created

1 | """
2 | Concept extraction agent.
3 | 
4 | Extracts named concepts from document text using the ICA LLM client.
5 | Concepts below the CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_MIN threshold are discarded.
6 | Uses hierarchical chunking with overlap so no context is lost at chunk boundaries.
7 | """
8 | from __future__ import annotations
9 | import json
10 | import logging
11 | from typing import Any
12 | 
13 | from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError
14 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
15 | 
16 | from app.config import settings
17 | from app.db.models import Concept, Document
18 | from app.ingestion.parsers import chunk_text_hierarchical
19 | from app.llm_client import chat
20 | 
21 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
22 | 
23 | CONCEPT_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
24 | You are an AI knowledge compiler for IBM Consulting.
25 | Extract ALL significant concepts from the consulting document text provided.
26 | You work strictly from what is written — never introduce general knowledge, external facts, or internet search results.
27 | 
28 | ## What counts as a concept
29 | A NAMED, REUSABLE entity that appears in IBM consulting work:
30 | - Industry standards (ISO 20022, SWIFT, FIX protocol)
31 | - Technologies & platforms (Kubernetes, AWS, SAP S/4HANA)
32 | - IBM methodologies & frameworks
33 | - Business processes (payment settlement, trade finance, KYC)
34 | - Architecture patterns (microservices, event-driven, CQRS)
35 | - Regulatory requirements (GDPR, MiFID II, Basel III)
36 | - Organisational capabilities (API management, cloud governance)
37 | 
38 | NOT concepts: generic words (introduction, section, approach), vague phrases, pronouns.
39 | 
40 | ## Confidence scoring
41 | - 0.9–1.0 : explicitly named multiple times, central to the document
42 | - 0.7–0.9 : clearly mentioned and relevant
43 | - 0.5–0.7 : mentioned but peripheral
44 | - < 0.5   : uncertain — EXCLUDE
45 | 
46 | ## Output
47 | Return ONLY a JSON array — no prose, no markdown fences:
48 | [
49 |   {
50 |     "name": "ISO 20022",
51 |     "type": "Payment Standard",
52 |     "confidence": 0.95,
53 |     "description": "1-2 sentence description based solely on this document",
54 |     "source_excerpt": "verbatim 1-3 sentence quote from the document",
55 |     "reasoning": "mentioned 4 times as the core migration target"
56 |   }
57 | ]
58 | 
59 | Rules:
60 | - source_excerpt MUST be a verbatim quote. Never fabricate.
61 | - confidence < 0.6 → exclude entirely.
62 | - type must be one of: Technology, Standard, Methodology, Framework, Process, Capability, Regulation, Pattern, Tool, General
63 | - Minimum 5 concepts for documents > 300 words.
64 | - Deduplicate by name (case-insensitive).
65 | - Return [] if text is too short or too generic.
66 | """
67 | 
68 | 
69 | class ConceptItem(BaseModel):
70 |     name: str = Field(..., min_length=1)
71 |     type: str = Field(default="General")
72 |     confidence: float = Field(default=0.8, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
73 |     description: str = Field(default="")
74 |     source_excerpt: str = Field(..., min_length=5)
75 |     reasoning: str = Field(default="")
76 | 
77 | 
78 | def _call_llm(text_chunk: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
79 |     """Call LLM and parse concept JSON. Retries once on parse failure."""
80 |     for attempt in range(2):
81 |         try:
82 |             raw = chat(
83 |                 system=CONCEPT_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
84 |                 user=f"Document text:\n\n{text_chunk}",
85 |                 max_tokens=4096,
86 |             )
87 |             raw = raw.strip()
88 |             if raw.startswith("```"):
89 |                 raw = raw.split("```")[1]
90 |                 if raw.startswith("json"):
91 |                     raw = raw[4:]
92 |             return json.loads(raw)
93 |         except (json.JSONDecodeError, IndexError) as e:
94 |             if attempt == 0:
95 |                 logger.warning("Concept extraction JSON parse failed (attempt 1), retrying: %s", e)
96 |             else:
97 |                 logger.error("Concept extraction JSON parse failed after retry: %s", e)
98 |                 return []
99 |     return []
100 | 
101 | 
102 | def extract_concepts(db: Session, doc: Document) -> list[Concept]:
103 |     """
104 |     Extract concepts from doc.raw_text and persist to DB.
105 |     Uses hierarchical chunking with overlap; filters by confidence threshold.
106 |     """
107 |     if not doc.raw_text or len(doc.raw_text.strip()) < 100:
108 |         logger.info("[doc=%d] Text too short for concept extraction, skipping.", doc.id)
109 |         return []
110 | 
111 |     chunks = chunk_text_hierarchical(
112 |         doc.raw_text,
113 |         max_chars=settings.chunk_size * 4,
114 |         overlap_chars=settings.chunk_overlap,
115 |     )
116 | 
117 |     created: list[Concept] = []
118 |     seen_names: set[str] = set()
119 | 
120 |     existing_names = {
121 |         c.name.lower()
122 |         for c in db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id).all()
123 |     }
124 | 
125 |     for chunk in chunks:
126 |         raw_items = _call_llm(chunk)
127 |         for raw in raw_items:
128 |             try:
129 |                 item = ConceptItem(**raw)
130 |             except ValidationError as ve:
131 |                 logger.warning("[doc=%d] Rejected concept (validation failed): %s — %s", doc.id, raw, ve)
132 |                 continue
133 | 
134 |             if item.confidence < settings.concept_confidence_min:
135 |                 logger.debug(
136 |                     "[doc=%d] Skipped low-confidence concept '%s' (confidence=%.2f < %.2f)",
137 |                     doc.id, item.name, item.confidence, settings.concept_confidence_min,
138 |                 )
139 |                 continue
140 | 
141 |             name_lower = item.name.lower().strip()
142 |             if name_lower in seen_names or name_lower in existing_names:
143 |                 continue
144 | 
145 |             concept = Concept(
146 |                 workspace_id=doc.workspace_id,
147 |                 name=item.name.strip(),
148 |                 type=item.type,
149 |                 description=item.description,
150 |                 source_document_id=doc.id,
151 |                 source_excerpt=item.source_excerpt,
152 |                 confidence=item.confidence,
153 |             )
154 |             db.add(concept)
155 |             seen_names.add(name_lower)
156 |             existing_names.add(name_lower)
157 |             created.append(concept)
158 | 
159 |     db.commit()
160 |     logger.info("[doc=%d] Extracted %d concepts (confidence ≥ %.2f).", doc.id, len(created), settings.concept_confidence_min)
161 |     return created
162 |

1 | """
2 | Relationship extraction agent.
3 | 
4 | Discovers relationships between concepts already in the workspace.
5 | Each relationship carries a strength score (0.0–1.0); relationships
6 | below 0.5 are discarded. Concept names are fuzzy-matched against the
7 | workspace concept list to resolve minor LLM naming variations.
8 | """
9 | from __future__ import annotations
10 | import json
11 | import logging
12 | from typing import Any
13 | 
14 | from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError
15 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

17 |

19 | from app.db.models import Concept, Document, Relationship, ALLOWED_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES
20 | from app.ingestion.parsers import chunk_text_hierarchical
21 | from app.llm_client import chat
22 | 
23 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
24 | 
25 | RELATIONSHIP_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
26 | You are an AI knowledge compiler for IBM Consulting.
27 | Discover relationships between concepts compiled from IBM consulting documents.
28 | Work strictly from the provided document text — no external knowledge, no fabrication.
29 | 
30 | Given a list of known concepts and a document excerpt, identify relationships
31 | ONLY between concepts that already appear in the concept list.
32 | 
33 | ## Strength scoring
34 | - 0.9–1.0 : explicit, repeated, central to the document's argument
35 | - 0.7–0.9 : clearly stated in the document
36 | - 0.5–0.7 : implied or mentioned briefly
37 | - < 0.5   : uncertain — EXCLUDE
38 | 
39 | ## Output — JSON array only, no prose, no markdown:
40 | [
41 |   {
42 |     "source": "exact concept name from the list",
43 |     "target": "exact concept name from the list",
44 |     "relationship_type": "one of: depends_on, requires, implements, extends, contrasts_with, enables, is_part_of, related_to",
45 |     "strength": 0.85,
46 |     "reasoning": "document states X directly requires Y for settlement"
47 |   }
48 | ]
49 | 
50 | Rules:
51 | - Only use concept names from the provided list. No invention.
52 | - Only create a relationship if the document text explicitly supports it.
53 | - strength < 0.5 → exclude entirely.
54 | - No self-referential relationships (source == target).
55 | - Return [] if no clear relationships can be inferred.
56 | """
57 | 
58 | FUZZY_THRESHOLD = 80
59 | 
60 | 
61 | class RelationshipItem(BaseModel):
62 |     source: str
63 |     target: str
64 |     relationship_type: str = "related_to"
65 |     strength: float = Field(default=0.7, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
66 |     reasoning: str = Field(default="")
67 |

69 | def _fuzzy_resolve(name: str, name_to_id: dict[str, int]) -> int | None:
70 |     if name.lower() in name_to_id:
71 |         return name_to_id[name.lower()]
72 |     result = fuzzy_process.extractOne(name, list(name_to_id.keys()))
73 |     if result and result[1] >= FUZZY_THRESHOLD:
74 |         logger.debug("Fuzzy matched '%s' → '%s' (score %s)", name, result[0], result[1])
75 |         return name_to_id[result[0]]
76 |     return None
77 | 
78 | 
79 | def _call_llm(concept_list_text: str, doc_chunk: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
80 |     for attempt in range(2):
81 |         try:
82 |             raw = chat(
83 |                 system=RELATIONSHIP_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
84 |                 user=(
85 |                     f"Known concepts:\n{concept_list_text}\n\n"
86 |                     f"Document excerpt:\n{doc_chunk}"
87 |                 ),
88 |                 max_tokens=2048,
89 |             )
90 |             raw = raw.strip()
91 |             if raw.startswith("```"):
92 |                 raw = raw.split("```")[1]
93 |                 if raw.startswith("json"):
94 |                     raw = raw[4:]
95 |             return json.loads(raw)
96 |         except (json.JSONDecodeError, IndexError) as e:
97 |             if attempt == 0:
98 |                 logger.warning("Relationship extraction JSON parse failed (attempt 1): %s", e)
99 |             else:
100 |                 logger.error("Relationship extraction JSON parse failed after retry: %s", e)
101 |                 return []
102 |     return []
103 |

105 | def extract_relationships(db: Session, doc: Document) -> list[Relationship]:
106 |     """Extract relationships for the given document's workspace."""
107 |     all_concepts = (
108 |         db.query(Concept)
109 |         .filter(Concept.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id)
110 |         .all()
111 |     )
112 |     if len(all_concepts) < 2:
113 |         logger.info("[doc=%d] Fewer than 2 concepts in workspace, skipping relationship extraction.", doc.id)
114 |         return []
115 | 
116 |     name_to_id = {c.name.lower(): c.id for c in all_concepts}
117 |     concept_list_text = "\n".join(f"- {c.name} ({c.type})" for c in all_concepts)
118 | 
119 |     chunks = chunk_text_hierarchical(
120 |         doc.raw_text or "",
121 |         max_chars=settings.chunk_size * 4,
122 |         overlap_chars=settings.chunk_overlap,
123 |     )
124 |

126 |     existing_pairs: set[tuple[int, int, str]] = set()
127 | 
128 |     for rel in db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id).all():
129 |         existing_pairs.add((rel.source_concept_id, rel.target_concept_id, rel.relationship_type))
130 | 
131 |     for chunk in chunks:
132 |         raw_items = _call_llm(concept_list_text, chunk)
133 |         for raw in raw_items:
134 |             try:
135 |                 item = RelationshipItem(**raw)
136 |             except ValidationError as ve:
137 |                 logger.warning("[doc=%d] Rejected relationship: %s — %s", doc.id, raw, ve)
138 |                 continue
139 | 
140 |             if item.strength < 0.5:
141 |                 continue
142 | 
143 |             if item.relationship_type not in ALLOWED_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES:
144 |                 item.relationship_type = "related_to"
145 | 
146 |             source_id = _fuzzy_resolve(item.source, name_to_id)
147 |             target_id = _fuzzy_resolve(item.target, name_to_id)
148 | 
149 |             if source_id is None or target_id is None:
150 |                 continue
151 |             if source_id == target_id:
152 |                 continue
153 | 
154 |             key = (source_id, target_id, item.relationship_type)
155 |             if key in existing_pairs:
156 |                 continue

161 |                 target_concept_id=target_id,
162 |                 relationship_type=item.relationship_type,

166 |             )

2 | Ingestion pipeline — called as a FastAPI BackgroundTask after upload.
3 | Orchestrates parsing → concept extraction → relationship extraction →
4 | graph update → pattern extraction (threshold-gated).
5 | """
6 | from __future__ import annotations

11 | from app.db.session import SessionLocal

21 | 
22 | def run_ingestion_pipeline(document_id: int) -> None:
23 |     """
24 |     Full ingestion pipeline for a single document.
25 |     Runs in a background thread — must open its own DB session.
26 | 
27 |     After extraction the pipeline:
28 |     1. Calls graph_memory_manager.add_document_contributions() to update the
29 |        in-memory graph incrementally (no full rebuild).
30 |     2. Evaluates the pattern extraction threshold and runs the pattern agent
31 |        only if the workspace knowledge has grown enough to warrant it.
32 |     """
33 |     db: Session = SessionLocal()
34 |     try:
35 |         doc = db.get(Document, document_id)
36 |         if doc is None:
37 |             logger.error("Document %d not found in DB.", document_id)
38 |             return
39 | 
40 |         doc.upload_status = "processing"
41 |         db.commit()
42 | 
43 |         with open(doc.filename, "rb") as f:
44 |             file_bytes = f.read()
45 | 
46 |         raw_text, file_metadata = parse_document(file_bytes, doc.file_type)
47 |         doc.raw_text = raw_text
48 |         if not doc.title and file_metadata.get("title"):
49 |             doc.title = file_metadata["title"]
50 |         db.commit()
51 | 
52 |         logger.info("[doc=%d] Starting concept extraction", document_id)
53 |         extract_concepts(db, doc)
54 | 
55 |         logger.info("[doc=%d] Starting relationship extraction", document_id)
56 |         extract_relationships(db, doc)
57 | 
58 |         # ── Graph memory update ────────────────────────────────────────
59 |         logger.info("[doc=%d] Updating graph memory", document_id)
60 |         graph_memory_manager.add_document_contributions(doc.workspace_id, document_id, db)
61 | 
62 |         # ── Pattern extraction (threshold-gated) ───────────────────────
63 |         concept_count = (
64 |             db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id).count()
65 |         )
66 |         rel_count = (
67 |             db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id).count()
68 |         )
69 | 
70 |         if should_run_pattern_extraction(db, doc.workspace_id):
71 |             logger.info("[doc=%d] Pattern extraction threshold met — running", document_id)
72 |             new_patterns = extract_patterns(db, doc)
73 |             record_pattern_run(
74 |                 db,
75 |                 workspace_id=doc.workspace_id,
76 |                 concept_count=concept_count,
77 |                 relationship_count=rel_count,
78 |                 patterns_generated=len(new_patterns),
79 |                 status="complete",
80 |             )
81 |         else:
82 |             logger.info("[doc=%d] Pattern extraction threshold not met — skipping", document_id)
83 |             record_pattern_run(
84 |                 db,
85 |                 workspace_id=doc.workspace_id,
86 |                 concept_count=concept_count,
87 |                 relationship_count=rel_count,
88 |                 patterns_generated=0,
89 |                 status="skipped",
90 |             )
91 | 
92 |         doc.upload_status = "complete"
93 |         db.commit()
94 |         logger.info("[doc=%d] Ingestion complete.", document_id)
95 | 
96 |     except Exception as e:
97 |         logger.exception("[doc=%d] Ingestion failed: %s", document_id, e)
98 |         db.rollback()
99 |         doc = db.get(Document, document_id)
100 |         if doc:
101 |             doc.upload_status = "failed"
102 |             doc.error_message = str(e)
103 |             db.commit()
104 |     finally:
105 |         db.close()

3 | Each parser returns (raw_text: str, metadata: dict).
4 | 
5 | chunk_text_hierarchical() splits at section/header boundaries first,
6 | then at paragraph boundaries for oversized sections, and adds overlap
7 | between adjacent chunks so no context is lost at chunk edges.
8 | """
9 | from __future__ import annotations
10 | import io
11 | import logging
12 | import re
13 | 
14 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

17 | def parse_pdf(file_bytes: bytes) -> tuple[str, dict]:
18 |     """Extract text from PDF using PyMuPDF. Raises ValueError on corrupt input."""
19 |     try:
20 |         import fitz  # PyMuPDF
21 |         doc = fitz.open(stream=file_bytes, filetype="pdf")
22 |         pages = []
23 |         for page in doc:
24 |             pages.append(page.get_text("text"))
25 |         raw_text = "\n\n".join(pages)
26 |         meta = doc.metadata or {}
27 |         metadata = {
28 |             "title": meta.get("title") or "",
29 |             "author": meta.get("author") or "",
30 |             "page_count": doc.page_count,
31 |         }
32 |         doc.close()
33 |         return raw_text, metadata
34 |     except Exception as exc:
35 |         logger.error("PDF parsing failed: %s", exc)
36 |         raise ValueError(f"Could not parse PDF: {exc}") from exc

38 | 
39 | def parse_docx(file_bytes: bytes) -> tuple[str, dict]:
40 |     """Extract text from DOCX using python-docx. Raises ValueError on corrupt input."""
41 |     try:
42 |         from docx import Document
43 |         doc = Document(io.BytesIO(file_bytes))
44 |         paragraphs = [p.text for p in doc.paragraphs if p.text.strip()]
45 |         for table in doc.tables:
46 |             for row in table.rows:
47 |                 for cell in row.cells:
48 |                     if cell.text.strip():
49 |                         paragraphs.append(cell.text.strip())
50 |         raw_text = "\n\n".join(paragraphs)
51 |         core_props = doc.core_properties
52 |         metadata = {
53 |             "title": core_props.title or "",
54 |             "author": core_props.author or "",
55 |         }
56 |         return raw_text, metadata
57 |     except Exception as exc:
58 |         logger.error("DOCX parsing failed: %s", exc)
59 |         raise ValueError(f"Could not parse DOCX: {exc}") from exc

62 | def parse_pptx(file_bytes: bytes) -> tuple[str, dict]:
63 |     """Extract text from PPTX using python-pptx. Raises ValueError on corrupt input."""
64 |     try:
65 |         from pptx import Presentation
66 |         prs = Presentation(io.BytesIO(file_bytes))
67 |         slides_text = []
68 |         for i, slide in enumerate(prs.slides):
69 |             parts = []
70 |             for shape in slide.shapes:
71 |                 if hasattr(shape, "text") and shape.text.strip():
72 |                     parts.append(shape.text.strip())
73 |             if parts:
74 |                 slides_text.append(f"[Slide {i + 1}]\n" + "\n".join(parts))
75 |         raw_text = "\n\n".join(slides_text)
76 |         core_props = prs.core_properties
77 |         metadata = {
78 |             "title": core_props.title or "",
79 |             "author": core_props.author or "",
80 |             "slide_count": len(prs.slides),
81 |         }

88 | def parse_document(file_bytes: bytes, file_type: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
89 |     """Route to the correct parser based on file_type. Propagates ValueError on corrupt input."""
90 |     parsers = {"pdf": parse_pdf, "docx": parse_docx, "pptx": parse_pptx}
91 |     if file_type not in parsers:
92 |         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported file type: {file_type}")
93 |     return parsers[file_type](file_bytes)

95 | 
96 | # ── Chunking ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
97 | 
98 | # Matches Markdown/document headers: #, ##, ### or ALL-CAPS lines ≥ 4 chars
99 | _HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,4}\s+.+|[A-Z][A-Z0-9 \-:]{3,})$", re.MULTILINE)
100 | 
101 | 
102 | def chunk_text(text: str, max_chars: int = 12000) -> list[str]:
103 |     """Paragraph-aware chunker. chunk_text_hierarchical() is preferred for new callers."""
104 |     if len(text) <= max_chars:
105 |         return [text]
106 |     chunks: list[str] = []
107 |     paragraphs = text.split("\n\n")
108 |     current: list[str] = []
109 |     current_len = 0
110 |     for para in paragraphs:
111 |         if current_len + len(para) + 2 > max_chars and current:
112 |             chunks.append("\n\n".join(current))
113 |             current = []
114 |             current_len = 0
115 |         current.append(para)
116 |         current_len += len(para) + 2
117 |     if current:
118 |         chunks.append("\n\n".join(current))
119 |     return chunks
120 | 
121 | 
122 | def chunk_text_hierarchical(
123 |     text: str,
124 |     max_chars: int = 12000,
125 |     overlap_chars: int = 200,
126 | ) -> list[str]:
127 |     """
128 |     Hierarchical chunker that splits at section/header boundaries, then
129 |     at paragraph boundaries for oversized sections, and prepends
130 |     overlap_chars of the previous chunk to the next to avoid losing
131 |     context at boundaries. Returns a flat list of text chunks.
132 |     """
133 |     if not text or len(text.strip()) == 0:
134 |         return []
135 | 
136 |     if len(text) <= max_chars:
137 |         return [text]
138 | 
139 |     # Step 1: split at header boundaries
140 |     header_positions = [m.start() for m in _HEADER_RE.finditer(text)]
141 | 
142 |     if not header_positions:
143 |         return _split_by_paragraphs(text, max_chars, overlap_chars)
144 | 
145 |     section_texts: list[str] = []
146 |     boundaries = header_positions + [len(text)]
147 |     for i in range(len(header_positions)):
148 |         section = text[boundaries[i]:boundaries[i + 1]].strip()
149 |         if section:
150 |             section_texts.append(section)
151 | 
152 |     # Step 2: split oversized sections by paragraphs
153 |     fine_chunks: list[str] = []
154 |     for section in section_texts:
155 |         if len(section) <= max_chars:
156 |             fine_chunks.append(section)
157 |         else:
158 |             fine_chunks.extend(_split_by_paragraphs(section, max_chars, overlap_chars))
159 | 
160 |     # Step 3: add overlap between adjacent chunks
161 |     if overlap_chars <= 0 or len(fine_chunks) <= 1:
162 |         return fine_chunks
163 | 
164 |     overlapped: list[str] = [fine_chunks[0]]
165 |     for i in range(1, len(fine_chunks)):
166 |         prev_tail = fine_chunks[i - 1][-overlap_chars:]
167 |         overlapped.append(prev_tail + "\n\n" + fine_chunks[i])
168 | 
169 |     return overlapped
170 | 
171 | 
172 | def _split_by_paragraphs(
173 |     text: str,
174 |     max_chars: int,
175 |     overlap_chars: int,
176 | ) -> list[str]:
177 |     """Split text at paragraph boundaries with overlap."""
178 |     paragraphs = text.split("\n\n")
179 |     chunks: list[str] = []
180 |     current: list[str] = []
181 |     current_len = 0
182 |     prev_tail = ""
183 | 
184 |     for para in paragraphs:
185 |         para_len = len(para) + 2
186 |         if current_len + para_len > max_chars and current:
187 |             chunk = "\n\n".join(current)
188 |             chunks.append((prev_tail + "\n\n" + chunk).strip() if prev_tail else chunk)
189 |             prev_tail = chunk[-overlap_chars:] if overlap_chars > 0 else ""
190 |             current = []
191 |             current_len = 0
192 |         current.append(para)
193 |         current_len += para_len
194 | 
195 |     if current:
196 |         chunk = "\n\n".join(current)
197 |         chunks.append((prev_tail + "\n\n" + chunk).strip() if prev_tail else chunk)
198 | 
199 |     return chunks if chunks else [text]

1 | """
2 | Evidence-grounded QA service.
3 | 
4 | Retrieval strategy (designed for consistency):
5 |   1. LLM keyword extraction from the question (temperature=0)
6 |   2. Cumulative, confidence-weighted semantic node scoring (top-k=20)
7 |   3. Strength-filtered BFS from all seed nodes
8 |   4. Deterministic context assembly: sorted by relevance score DESC then
9 |      concept confidence DESC; near-duplicate excerpts are deduplicated
10 |   5. Grounded generation at temperature=0 for factual stability

30 | You MUST answer ONLY from the context passages provided below — this is your only source of truth.
31 | Do NOT use general knowledge, training data, internet search, or any external information.
32 | If the context does not support the answer to the question, you MUST respond with exactly:

75 | def ask_workspace(db: Session, workspace_id: int, question: str) -> AskResponse:
76 |     """
77 |     Full evidence-grounded Q&A pipeline designed for retrieval consistency.
78 | 
79 |     Key consistency properties:
80 |     - Keyword extraction is deterministic (temperature=0).
81 |     - Seed nodes are selected by cumulative scoring across all keywords
82 |       (not winner-takes-all), so the same question reliably retrieves the
83 |       same top seeds regardless of keyword ordering.
84 |     - Retrieved concepts are assembled in a stable order: relevance score
85 |       DESC, then concept confidence DESC, then concept ID ASC as tie-break.
86 |     - Near-duplicate source excerpts are deduplicated before LLM generation
87 |       so important passages are not pushed out of the context window.
88 |     - Final generation is at temperature=0 to minimise structural variation.

91 |     keywords = _extract_keywords_llm(question)

94 |     G = graph_memory_manager.get_workspace_graph(workspace_id, db)

103 |             for c in db_matched
104 |             if any(kw in c.name.lower() for kw in kw_lower)
105 |         ]

107 |     seed_score: dict[int, float] = {nid: score for nid, score in scored_seeds}

150 |             doc_name = "Unknown Document"

153 |                 if doc:
154 |                     doc_name = doc.title or doc.filename

1 | """
2 | Shared LLM client — IBM Consulting Advantage, Claude Code endpoint.
3 | 
4 | Wraps the Anthropic SDK with:
5 |   - Secret retrieval via SecretProvider (no direct os.getenv access)
6 |   - httpx.Timeout: explicit connect / read / write limits — no indefinite hangs
7 |   - Tenacity retry: exponential backoff + jitter for transient failures
8 |   - Circuit breaker: rejects calls fast when the provider is unhealthy
9 |   - Structured observability: latency, token counts, cost, retry count per call
10 | 
11 | Timeout defaults (all configurable via environment):
12 |   LLM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT   10 s   TCP handshake + TLS
13 |   LLM_READ_TIMEOUT     120 s   time waiting for the first response byte
14 |   LLM_WRITE_TIMEOUT     30 s   time uploading the request body
15 | 
16 | Retry defaults:
17 |   LLM_MAX_RETRIES        4     attempts after the first (total 5 tries)
18 |   LLM_RETRY_MAX_WAIT    30 s   cap on per-attempt backoff sleep
19 | 
20 | Caller contract:
21 |   - Raises fastapi.HTTPException(503) when the circuit breaker is open.
22 |   - Raises fastapi.HTTPException(503) when all retry attempts are exhausted.
23 |   - Raises any non-transient anthropic.* / httpx.* exception immediately.
24 | 
25 | Usage
26 | -----
27 | from app.llm_client import chat
28 | 
29 | response_text = chat(
30 |     system="You are a knowledge compiler...",
31 |     user="What is ISO 20022?",
32 |     max_tokens=2048,
33 |     operation="workspace_chat",
34 | )
35 | """
36 | from __future__ import annotations
37 |

39 | import time
40 | import uuid

44 | import httpx
45 | from fastapi import HTTPException

47 | 
48 | from app.config import settings
49 | from app.llm.circuit_breaker import circuit_breaker
50 | from app.llm.retry import llm_retry, _is_transient
51 | from app.security.secrets import get_secret_provider
52 | 
53 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

56 | # ── Client factory ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
57 | 
58 | @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
59 | def _get_client() -> anthropic.Anthropic:
60 |     """
61 |     Build and cache the Anthropic SDK client.
62 | 
63 |     The API key is fetched via SecretProvider — never directly from os.environ.
64 |     httpx.Timeout is applied here so every request shares the same limits.
65 |     """
66 |     provider = get_secret_provider()
67 |     api_key = provider.get_secret(settings.claude_secret_name)
68 |     timeout = httpx.Timeout(
69 |         connect=settings.llm_connect_timeout,
70 |         read=settings.llm_read_timeout,
71 |         write=settings.llm_write_timeout,
72 |         pool=settings.llm_connect_timeout,
73 |     )
74 |     return anthropic.Anthropic(
75 |         api_key=api_key,
76 |         base_url=settings.claude_base_url,
77 |         timeout=timeout,
78 |     )
79 | 
80 | 
81 | # ── Core API call (retried) ───────────────────────────────────────────
82 | 
83 | def _call_api(
84 |     system: str,
85 |     user: str,
86 |     max_tokens: int,
87 |     temperature: float,
88 | ) -> anthropic.types.Message:
89 |     """
90 |     Execute one Anthropic messages.create call.
91 |     Wrapped by chat() with the tenacity retry decorator.
92 |     This function is intentionally thin — one responsibility: call the SDK.
93 |     """
94 |     client = _get_client()
95 |     return client.messages.create(
96 |         model=settings.claude_model,
97 |         max_tokens=max_tokens,
98 |         temperature=temperature,
99 |         system=system,
100 |         messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}],
101 |     )
102 | 
103 | 
104 | # ── Public interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
105 | 
106 | def chat(
107 |     system: str,
108 |     user: str,
109 |     max_tokens: int = 2048,
110 |     temperature: float = 0.2,
111 |     operation: str = "llm_call",
112 | ) -> str:
113 |     """
114 |     Send a single chat completion via Claude and return the text response.
115 | 
116 |     Parameters
117 |     ----------
118 |     system      : System prompt text.
119 |     user        : User turn content.
120 |     max_tokens  : Upper bound on generated tokens.
121 |     temperature : Sampling temperature (0.0 for deterministic QA).
122 |     operation   : Logical label for observability logs (e.g. 'concept_extraction').
123 | 
124 |     Raises
125 |     ------
126 |     fastapi.HTTPException(503) — circuit breaker open, or retries exhausted.
127 |     anthropic.AuthenticationError — bad API key (not retried).
128 |     """
129 |     request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
130 |     t0 = time.monotonic()
131 |     retry_count = 0
132 | 
133 |     # Build a fresh retry decorator each call so monkeypatching settings in
134 |     # tests immediately takes effect without restarting the process.
135 |     _retried_call = llm_retry()(_call_api)
136 | 
137 |     with circuit_breaker:
138 |         try:
139 |             message = _retried_call(system, user, max_tokens, temperature)
140 | 
141 |         except RetryError as exc:
142 |             # All attempts exhausted — unwrap and log the root cause.
143 |             cause = exc.last_attempt.exception()
144 |             retry_count = exc.last_attempt.attempt_number - 1
145 |             logger.error(
146 |                 "[req=%s op=%s] LLM call failed after %d retries. "
147 |                 "Final error: %s %s",
148 |                 request_id, operation, retry_count,
149 |                 type(cause).__name__, cause,
150 |             )
151 |             raise HTTPException(
152 |                 status_code=503,
153 |                 detail="LLM request failed after multiple retry attempts. Please try again shortly.",
154 |             ) from exc
155 | 
156 |         except Exception:
157 |             # Non-transient error (auth failure, budget 429, etc.) — let it propagate.
158 |             raise
159 | 
160 |     latency_ms = (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000
161 | 
162 |     stats = getattr(_retried_call, "statistics", {})
163 |     retry_count = max(0, stats.get("attempt_number", 1) - 1)
164 | 
165 |     usage = message.usage
166 |     prompt_tokens     = getattr(usage, "input_tokens",  0)
167 |     completion_tokens = getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0)
168 | 
169 |     from app.llm.usage_tracker import estimate_cost  # noqa: PLC0415
170 |     cost = estimate_cost(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)
171 | 
172 |     logger.info(
173 |         "[req=%s op=%s] LLM call completed: model=%s latency=%.0fms "
174 |         "prompt_tokens=%d completion_tokens=%d cost=$%.6f retries=%d",
175 |         request_id, operation, settings.claude_model, latency_ms,
176 |         prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost, retry_count,
177 |     )
178 | 
179 |     return message.content[0].text or ""

1 | """
2 | GraphMemoryManager — single entry point for all graph operations.
3 | 
4 | Architecture
5 | ------------
6 | SQL tables remain the system of record. The NetworkX graph is a derived,
7 | in-memory operational layer maintained by this manager.
8 | 
9 | Every node stores:
10 |     source_document_ids : set[int]  — which documents contributed this concept
11 |     evidence_count      : int       — number of contributing documents
12 |

14 |     source_document_ids : set[int]  — which documents support this relationship
15 |     evidence_count      : int       — number of supporting documents
16 |

18 | ---------

20 |                               workspaces that have at least one complete document.
21 | get_workspace_graph()       — returns the in-memory graph; builds from SQL on
22 |                               first access (cache miss).

25 | invalidate()                — evict the cached graph so the next access rebuilds.

106 | class GraphMemoryManager:
107 |     """
108 |     Manages the lifecycle of in-memory workspace graphs.
109 | 
110 |     One instance is created at module level as the application singleton.
111 |     All services call get_workspace_graph() instead of build_workspace_graph().

113 | 
114 |     def __init__(self) -> None:
115 |         self._store = WorkspaceGraphStore()
116 |         self._build_lock: dict[int, threading.Lock] = {}
117 |         self._meta_lock = threading.Lock()

121 |     def startup_load(self) -> None:
122 |         """
123 |         Load all workspaces with at least one complete document into memory.
124 |         Called once from main.py lifespan after init_db().
125 |         """
126 |         db = SessionLocal()
127 |         try:
128 |             from app.db.models import Document  # local import avoids circular dependency
129 |             workspace_ids = (
130 |                 db.query(Workspace.id)
131 |                 .join(Document, Document.workspace_id == Workspace.id)
132 |                 .filter(Document.upload_status == "complete")
133 |                 .distinct()
134 |                 .all()
135 |             )
136 |             ws_ids = [row[0] for row in workspace_ids]
137 |             logger.info(
138 |                 "[graph_memory] Startup load: %d workspace(s) with complete documents.",
139 |                 len(ws_ids),
140 |             )
141 |             for ws_id in ws_ids:
142 |                 t0 = time.monotonic()
143 |                 G = _build_provenance_graph(db, ws_id)
144 |                 self._store.put(ws_id, G)
145 |                 logger.info(
146 |                     "[graph_memory] ws=%d loaded: %d nodes, %d edges (%.0fms)",
147 |                     ws_id, G.number_of_nodes(), G.number_of_edges(),
148 |                     (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,
149 |                 )
150 |         except Exception:
151 |             logger.exception("[graph_memory] Startup load failed — graphs will be built on first access.")
152 |         finally:
153 |             db.close()

157 |     def get_workspace_graph(self, workspace_id: int, db: Session | None = None) -> nx.DiGraph:
158 |         """
159 |         Return the in-memory graph for this workspace.
160 | 
161 |         If the graph is not yet loaded, builds it from SQL (cache miss).
162 |         A per-workspace lock prevents duplicate builds when two requests arrive
163 |         simultaneously for an un-loaded workspace.
164 | 
165 |         Parameters
166 |         ----------
167 |         workspace_id : the workspace to retrieve.
168 |         db           : optional SQLAlchemy session; only used on cache miss.
169 |                        If None on a miss, a new session is opened internally.
170 |         """
171 |         G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
172 |         if G is not None:
173 |             return G
174 | 
175 |         build_lock = self._get_build_lock(workspace_id)
176 |         with build_lock:
177 |             # Re-check after acquiring the lock — another thread may have built it.
178 |             G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
179 |             if G is not None:
180 |                 return G
181 | 
182 |             return self._build_and_store(workspace_id, db)

186 |     def add_document_contributions(self, workspace_id: int, document_id: int, db: Session) -> None:
187 |         """
188 |         Incrementally add a document's concepts and relationships to the
189 |         workspace graph.  If the graph is not loaded, performs a full build
190 |         from SQL (which will include the new document's contributions naturally).
191 | 
192 |         This is called by the ingestion pipeline immediately after
193 |         upload_status is set to "complete".
194 |         """
195 |         G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
196 |         if G is None:
197 |             self._build_and_store(workspace_id, db)
198 |             logger.info(
199 |                 "[graph_memory] ws=%d doc=%d — graph was not loaded; performed full build.",
200 |                 workspace_id, document_id,
201 |             )
202 |             self._bump_graph_version(db, workspace_id)
203 |             return
204 | 
205 |         t0 = time.monotonic()
206 |         build_lock = self._get_build_lock(workspace_id)
207 |         with build_lock:

210 |                 db.query(Concept)

214 |             new_relationships = (

218 |                     Relationship.source_document_id == document_id,
219 |                 )

223 |             nodes_added = 0
224 |             edges_added = 0

226 |             for c in new_concepts:

232 |                     G.nodes[c.id]["evidence_count"] = len(existing_ids)
233 |                 else:

239 |                     continue

241 |                     # Merge provenance into existing edge.
242 |                     existing_ids = G.edges[r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id].get(
243 |                         "source_document_ids", set()
244 |                     )
245 |                     existing_ids.add(document_id)
246 |                     G.edges[r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id]["source_document_ids"] = existing_ids
247 |                     G.edges[r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id]["evidence_count"] = len(existing_ids)
248 |                 else:
249 |                     G.add_edge(
250 |                         r.source_concept_id,
251 |                         r.target_concept_id,
252 |                         **_edge_attrs_from_relationship(r),
253 |                     )
254 |                     edges_added += 1
255 | 
256 |         self._bump_graph_version(db, workspace_id)
257 |         logger.info(
258 |             "[graph_memory] ws=%d doc=%d — incremental add: +%d nodes, +%d edges (%.0fms)",
259 |             workspace_id, document_id, nodes_added, edges_added,
260 |             (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,

263 |     # ── incremental remove ────────────────────────────────────────────
