265 |     def remove_document_contributions(self, workspace_id: int, document_id: int) -> None:
266 |         """
267 |         Remove a document's evidence from the workspace graph.
268 | 
269 |         Nodes and edges that still have other supporting documents are kept;
270 |         only those whose entire evidence base was this document are removed.
271 |         This is called by the documents API immediately before the DB delete.
272 |         """
273 |         G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
274 |         if G is None:
275 |             # Nothing cached — the next access will rebuild from updated SQL.
276 |             return
277 | 
278 |         t0 = time.monotonic()
279 |         build_lock = self._get_build_lock(workspace_id)
280 |         with build_lock:
281 |             # Remove document from edge provenance; collect edges to delete.
282 |             edges_to_remove: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
283 |             for src, tgt, data in list(G.edges(data=True)):
284 |                 doc_ids: set[int] = data.get("source_document_ids", set())
285 |                 doc_ids.discard(document_id)
286 |                 if not doc_ids:
287 |                     edges_to_remove.append((src, tgt))
288 |                 else:
289 |                     data["source_document_ids"] = doc_ids
290 |                     data["evidence_count"] = len(doc_ids)
291 | 
292 |             for src, tgt in edges_to_remove:
293 |                 G.remove_edge(src, tgt)
294 | 
295 |             # Remove document from node provenance; collect nodes to delete.
296 |             nodes_to_remove: list[int] = []
297 |             for node_id, data in list(G.nodes(data=True)):
298 |                 doc_ids = data.get("source_document_ids", set())
299 |                 doc_ids.discard(document_id)
300 |                 if not doc_ids:
301 |                     nodes_to_remove.append(node_id)
302 |                 else:
303 |                     data["source_document_ids"] = doc_ids
304 |                     data["evidence_count"] = len(doc_ids)
305 | 
306 |             for node_id in nodes_to_remove:
307 |                 G.remove_node(node_id)
308 | 
309 |         logger.info(
310 |             "[graph_memory] ws=%d doc=%d removed: -%d nodes, -%d edges (%.0fms)",
311 |             workspace_id, document_id, len(nodes_to_remove), len(edges_to_remove),
312 |             (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,
313 |         )
314 | 
315 |     # ── invalidate / rebuild ──────────────────────────────────────────
316 | 
317 |     def invalidate(self, workspace_id: int) -> None:
318 |         """Evict the cached graph; next get_workspace_graph() will rebuild from SQL."""
319 |         self._store.evict(workspace_id)
320 |         logger.debug("[graph_memory] ws=%d evicted from cache.", workspace_id)
321 | 
322 |     def rebuild_workspace_graph(self, workspace_id: int, db: Session) -> nx.DiGraph:
323 |         """Force a full SQL rebuild for one workspace, replacing the cached graph."""
324 |         self._store.evict(workspace_id)
325 |         return self._build_and_store(workspace_id, db)
326 | 
327 |     # ── internals ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
328 | 
329 |     def _build_and_store(self, workspace_id: int, db: Session | None) -> nx.DiGraph:
330 |         t0 = time.monotonic()
331 |         own_session = db is None
332 |         if own_session:
333 |             db = SessionLocal()
334 |         try:
335 |             G = _build_provenance_graph(db, workspace_id)
336 |             self._store.put(workspace_id, G)
337 |             logger.info(
338 |                 "[graph_memory] ws=%d full build: %d nodes, %d edges (%.0fms)",
339 |                 workspace_id, G.number_of_nodes(), G.number_of_edges(),
340 |                 (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,
341 |             )
342 |             return G
343 |         finally:
344 |             if own_session:
345 |                 db.close()
346 | 
347 |     def _get_build_lock(self, workspace_id: int) -> threading.Lock:
348 |         with self._meta_lock:
349 |             if workspace_id not in self._build_lock:
350 |                 self._build_lock[workspace_id] = threading.Lock()
351 |             return self._build_lock[workspace_id]
352 | 
353 |     def _bump_graph_version(self, db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> None:
354 |         """Increment graph_version and set graph_last_updated on the Workspace row."""
355 |         try:
356 |             ws = db.get(Workspace, workspace_id)
357 |             if ws:
358 |                 ws.graph_version = (ws.graph_version or 0) + 1
359 |                 ws.graph_last_updated = datetime.utcnow()
360 |                 db.commit()
361 |         except Exception:
362 |             logger.exception(
363 |                 "[graph_memory] ws=%d — failed to bump graph_version.", workspace_id
364 |             )

15 | def build_workspace_graph(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> nx.DiGraph:
16 |     """
17 |     Build a directed, weighted NetworkX graph for the given workspace.
18 | 
19 |     Node attributes : name, type, description, source_document_id,
20 |                       source_excerpt, confidence
21 |     Edge attributes : relationship_type, source_document_id,
22 |                       strength, weight (= 1/strength for path algorithms)
23 |     """
24 |     G = nx.DiGraph()
25 | 
26 |     concepts = db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).all()
27 |     for c in concepts:
28 |         G.add_node(
29 |             c.id,

31 |             type=c.type or "General",
32 |             description=c.description or "",
33 |             source_document_id=c.source_document_id,
34 |             source_excerpt=c.source_excerpt or "",
35 |             confidence=getattr(c, "confidence", 0.8),
36 |         )
37 |

47 |             relationship_type=r.relationship_type,

56 | def graph_to_react_flow(G: nx.DiGraph) -> dict:
57 |     """
58 |     Convert NetworkX graph to React Flow–compatible node/edge format.
59 |     Edge thickness hint (strokeWidth) is derived from strength so the UI
60 |     can render stronger relationships as visually heavier lines.
61 |     """
62 |     if len(G.nodes) == 0:
63 |         return {"nodes": [], "edges": []}
64 | 
65 |     pos = nx.spring_layout(G, seed=42, k=2.5)
66 | 
67 |     nodes = []
68 |     for node_id, data in G.nodes(data=True):
69 |         x, y = pos.get(node_id, (0.0, 0.0))
70 |         nodes.append({
71 |             "id": str(node_id),
72 |             "data": {
73 |                 "label": data.get("name", str(node_id)),
74 |                 "type": data.get("type", "General"),
75 |                 "description": data.get("description", ""),
76 |                 "source_document_id": data.get("source_document_id"),
77 |                 "source_excerpt": data.get("source_excerpt", ""),
78 |                 "confidence": data.get("confidence", 0.8),
79 |             },
80 |             "position": {"x": float(x) * 500, "y": float(y) * 500},
81 |             "type": "default",
82 |         })
83 | 
84 |     edges = []
85 |     for src, tgt, data in G.edges(data=True):
86 |         strength = data.get("strength", 0.7)

88 |             "id": f"e{src}-{tgt}",

92 |             "data": {

95 |                 "strength": strength,
96 |                 "strokeWidth": max(1, round(strength * 4)),

1 | """
2 | Graph traversal — semantic node matching and strength-filtered BFS.
3 | 
4 | find_nodes_semantic()    — multi-signal, cumulative scoring across all
5 |                            keywords: exact name match > substring > type >
6 |                            description. Confidence-weighted so high-confidence
7 |                            nodes rank above equally-matching low-confidence ones.
8 | get_neighbourhood()      — strength-gated BFS; weak edges are skipped
9 |                            below the configured threshold.
10 | shortest_weighted_path() — uses edge weight (1/strength) to surface
11 |                            the most confident concept chain between two nodes.
12 | """
13 | from __future__ import annotations
14 | import networkx as nx
15 | 
16 | from app.db.models import Concept
17 | 
18 | 
19 | def find_nodes_semantic(
20 |     G: nx.DiGraph,
21 |     keywords: list[str],
22 |     top_k: int = 20,
23 | ) -> list[tuple[int, float]]:
24 |     """
25 |     Score every graph node against the keyword list and return the
26 |     top-k (node_id, relevance) pairs sorted highest-first.
27 | 
28 |     Scoring is cumulative across all keywords rather than winner-takes-all,
29 |     so a node that matches many keywords outranks a node that only matches
30 |     one keyword perfectly. Scores are also weighted by the node's own
31 |     confidence value so high-confidence concepts are preferred when two
32 |     nodes have equal keyword relevance.
33 | 
34 |     Per-keyword contribution tiers:
35 |       1.0  — exact name match (case-insensitive)
36 |       0.85 — keyword is a substring of the concept name
37 |       0.70 — concept name is a substring of the keyword
38 |       0.55 — keyword matches the concept type
39 |       0.30 — keyword appears in the concept description
40 |       0.0  — no match (excluded from that keyword's contribution)
41 | 
42 |     Final score = (sum of per-keyword contributions / n_keywords) * confidence_boost
43 |     where confidence_boost = 0.9 + 0.1 * node_confidence  (range 0.9–1.0).
44 |     """
45 |     if not keywords:
46 |         return []
47 | 
48 |     kw_lower = [k.lower() for k in keywords]
49 |     n_kw = len(kw_lower)
50 |     scored: list[tuple[int, float]] = []
51 | 
52 |     for node_id, data in G.nodes(data=True):
53 |         name_lower = data.get("name", "").lower()
54 |         type_lower = data.get("type", "").lower()
55 |         desc_lower = data.get("description", "").lower()
56 |         confidence = float(data.get("confidence", 0.8))
57 | 
58 |         total = 0.0
59 |         for kw in kw_lower:
60 |             if kw == name_lower:
61 |                 total += 1.0
62 |             elif kw in name_lower:
63 |                 total += 0.85
64 |             elif name_lower in kw:
65 |                 total += 0.70
66 |             elif kw in type_lower:
67 |                 total += 0.55
68 |             elif kw in desc_lower:
69 |                 total += 0.30
70 | 
71 |         if total == 0.0:
72 |             continue
73 | 
74 |         # Normalise to [0, 1] then apply a small confidence boost (±10%)
75 |         normalised = total / n_kw
76 |         confidence_boost = 0.9 + 0.1 * min(confidence, 1.0)
77 |         scored.append((node_id, round(normalised * confidence_boost, 6)))
78 | 
79 |     scored.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
80 |     return scored[:top_k]
81 | 
82 | 
83 | def find_nodes_by_keywords(G: nx.DiGraph, keywords: list[str]) -> list[int]:
84 |     """Return node IDs matching any keyword (no scoring). Wraps find_nodes_semantic."""
85 |     return [nid for nid, _ in find_nodes_semantic(G, keywords, top_k=len(G.nodes) + 1)]

88 | def get_neighbourhood(
89 |     G: nx.DiGraph,
90 |     node_id: int,
91 |     hops: int = 2,
92 |     strength_threshold: float = 0.0,
93 |     max_nodes: int = 60,
94 | ) -> tuple[list[int], list[tuple[int, int, dict]]]:
95 |     """
96 |     Return the N-hop neighbourhood of node_id using BFS.
97 | 
98 |     Parameters
99 |     ----------
100 |     strength_threshold : only follow edges with strength >= this value.
101 |                          Default 0.0 keeps backward compatibility (all edges).
102 |     max_nodes          : cap on neighbourhood size to avoid context explosion.
103 |     """
104 |     if not G.has_node(node_id):
105 |         return [], []
106 | 
107 |     undirected = G.to_undirected(as_view=True)
108 |     subgraph_nodes: set[int] = {node_id}
109 |     frontier: set[int] = {node_id}
110 | 
111 |     for _ in range(hops):
112 |         if len(subgraph_nodes) >= max_nodes:
113 |             break
114 |         next_frontier: set[int] = set()
115 |         for n in frontier:
116 |             for neighbour in undirected.neighbors(n):
117 |                 if neighbour in subgraph_nodes:
118 |                     continue
119 |                 edge_data = (
120 |                     G.get_edge_data(n, neighbour)
121 |                     or G.get_edge_data(neighbour, n)
122 |                     or {}
123 |                 )
124 |                 edge_strength = edge_data.get("strength", 0.7)
125 |                 if edge_strength >= strength_threshold:
126 |                     next_frontier.add(neighbour)
127 |                     subgraph_nodes.add(neighbour)
128 |                     if len(subgraph_nodes) >= max_nodes:
129 |                         break
130 |             if len(subgraph_nodes) >= max_nodes:
131 |                 break
132 |         frontier = next_frontier
133 | 
134 |     subgraph_edges: list[tuple[int, int, dict]] = [
135 |         (src, tgt, data)
136 |         for src, tgt, data in G.edges(data=True)
137 |         if src in subgraph_nodes and tgt in subgraph_nodes
138 |     ]
139 | 
140 |     return list(subgraph_nodes), subgraph_edges
141 | 
142 | 
143 | def shortest_weighted_path(
144 |     G: nx.DiGraph,
145 |     source_id: int,
146 |     target_id: int,
147 | ) -> list[int]:
148 |     """
149 |     Return the shortest path from source to target weighted by edge strength
150 |     (weight = 1/strength, so stronger edges are 'shorter').
151 |     Returns an empty list if no path exists.
152 |     """
153 |     try:
154 |         return nx.shortest_path(G, source=source_id, target=target_id, weight="weight")
155 |     except (nx.NetworkXNoPath, nx.NodeNotFound):
156 |         return []

1 | """
2 | Workspace graph store — thread-safe in-process cache of per-workspace NetworkX graphs.
3 | 
4 | The store is the single source of graph instances. No code outside
5 | GraphMemoryManager should ever read from or write to this store directly.
6 | """
7 | from __future__ import annotations
8 | 
9 | import threading
10 | 
11 | import networkx as nx
12 | 
13 | 
14 | class WorkspaceGraphStore:
15 |     """
16 |     Thread-safe dictionary mapping workspace_id → nx.DiGraph.
17 | 
18 |     All mutations acquire an RLock so that concurrent ingestion pipelines
19 |     (each running in a background thread) cannot corrupt a graph that is
20 |     simultaneously being traversed by a QA or deliverable request.
21 |     """
22 | 
23 |     def __init__(self) -> None:
24 |         self._graphs: dict[int, nx.DiGraph] = {}
25 |         self._lock = threading.RLock()
26 | 
27 |     # ── read ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
28 | 
29 |     def get(self, workspace_id: int) -> nx.DiGraph | None:
30 |         """Return the cached graph for this workspace, or None if not loaded."""
31 |         with self._lock:
32 |             return self._graphs.get(workspace_id)
33 | 
34 |     def has(self, workspace_id: int) -> bool:
35 |         """Return True if a graph is loaded for this workspace."""
36 |         with self._lock:
37 |             return workspace_id in self._graphs
38 | 
39 |     def workspace_ids(self) -> list[int]:
40 |         """Return sorted list of workspace IDs currently in the store."""
41 |         with self._lock:
42 |             return sorted(self._graphs.keys())
43 | 
44 |     # ── write ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
45 | 
46 |     def put(self, workspace_id: int, graph: nx.DiGraph) -> None:
47 |         """Replace (or set) the graph for this workspace."""
48 |         with self._lock:
49 |             self._graphs[workspace_id] = graph
50 | 
51 |     def evict(self, workspace_id: int) -> None:
52 |         """Remove the graph for this workspace from the store."""
53 |         with self._lock:
54 |             self._graphs.pop(workspace_id, None)
55 | 
56 |     def clear(self) -> None:
57 |         """Remove all graphs (used in tests)."""
58 |         with self._lock:
59 |             self._graphs.clear()

1 | """
2 | Centralised upload validation layer.
3 | 
4 | Validation order for every uploaded file:
5 |   1. Stream the first 8 KB — enough for magic-byte detection, avoids loading
6 |      the full file into memory before we know it is safe.
7 |   2. Identify the true MIME type from magic bytes — extension and Content-Type
8 |      headers are both attacker-controlled and are not trusted for security decisions.
9 |   3. Reject if the detected MIME type is not in the explicit allow-list.
10 |   4. Read the remainder and enforce the MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES size limit.
11 | 
12 | All upload endpoints must call validate_upload() before reading file contents.
13 | No duplicate validation logic elsewhere.
14 | """
15 | from __future__ import annotations
16 | 
17 | import logging
18 | from typing import NamedTuple
19 | 
20 | import filetype
21 | from fastapi import HTTPException, UploadFile
22 | 
23 | from app.config import settings
24 | 
25 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
26 | 
27 | # Allowed MIME types and the internal file_type label each maps to.
28 | _ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES: dict[str, str] = {
29 |     "application/pdf": "pdf",
30 |     "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document": "docx",
31 |     "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation": "pptx",
32 | }
33 | 
34 | # Bytes read for magic-byte detection — 8 KB is more than enough for all
35 | # supported formats; PDF/DOCX/PPTX signatures are in the first handful of bytes.
36 | _MAGIC_READ_BYTES = 8192
37 | 
38 | 
39 | class ValidationResult(NamedTuple):
40 |     file_type: str   # 'pdf' | 'docx' | 'pptx'
41 |     content: bytes   # full file bytes, ready for the parser
42 | 
43 | 
44 | async def validate_upload(file: UploadFile) -> ValidationResult:
45 |     """
46 |     Validate a single uploaded file and return its content.
47 | 
48 |     Raises HTTPException (413 or 422) on any violation.
49 |     On success, returns (file_type, full_content_bytes).
50 |     """
51 |     filename = file.filename or "(unknown)"
52 | 
53 |     # ── Step 1: read first chunk for magic-byte detection ─────────────
54 |     first_chunk = await file.read(_MAGIC_READ_BYTES)
55 |     if not first_chunk:
56 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f"'{filename}' is empty.")
57 | 
58 |     # ── Step 2: detect true MIME type from magic bytes ─────────────────
59 |     # filetype.guess() inspects the binary signature, ignoring filename/extension.
60 |     kind = filetype.guess(first_chunk)
61 |     detected_mime = kind.mime if kind else None
62 |     file_type = _ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES.get(detected_mime or "")
63 |     if file_type is None:
64 |         logger.warning(
65 |             "Upload rejected — unsupported magic-byte MIME '%s' for file '%s'",
66 |             detected_mime, filename,
67 |         )
68 |         raise HTTPException(
69 |             status_code=422,
70 |             detail=(
71 |                 f"Unsupported file type detected for '{filename}'. "
72 |                 "Accepted formats: PDF, DOCX, PPTX. "
73 |                 f"(Detected: {detected_mime or 'unknown'})"
74 |             ),
75 |         )
76 | 
77 |     # ── Step 3: read remainder and enforce size limit ──────────────────
78 |     max_bytes = settings.upload_max_bytes
79 |     remaining = await file.read(max_bytes)
80 |     full_content = first_chunk + remaining
81 | 
82 |     # One extra byte read — if non-empty the file exceeds the limit.
83 |     overflow = await file.read(1)
84 |     if overflow:
85 |         max_mb = max_bytes / (1024 * 1024)
86 |         raise HTTPException(
87 |             status_code=413,
88 |             detail=f"'{filename}' exceeds the maximum upload size of {max_mb:.0f} MB.",
89 |         )
90 | 
91 |     logger.debug(
92 |         "Upload validated: '%s' — type=%s size=%d bytes",
93 |         filename, file_type, len(full_content),
94 |     )
95 |     return ValidationResult(file_type=file_type, content=full_content)
96 |

1 | """
2 | LLM usage tracker — persists one row per API call to the llm_usage table.
3 | 
4 | Token counts come from the Anthropic response object's usage field.
5 | Cost estimates use configurable per-token prices; updating prices requires
6 | only a config change, not a code change.
7 | 
8 | Pricing defaults (USD per token) reflect Claude Sonnet 3.5 / 4 pricing
9 | as of 2025. Override via environment variables:
10 |   LLM_COST_PER_1K_INPUT_TOKENS
11 |   LLM_COST_PER_1K_OUTPUT_TOKENS
12 | """
13 | from __future__ import annotations
14 | 
15 | import logging
16 | from datetime import datetime
17 | 
18 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
19 | 
20 | from app.config import settings
21 | from app.db.models import LLMBudget, LLMUsage
22 | 
23 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
24 | 
25 | # Cost per 1 000 tokens in USD — configurable via Settings
26 | _INPUT_COST_PER_1K  = settings.llm_cost_per_1k_input_tokens
27 | _OUTPUT_COST_PER_1K = settings.llm_cost_per_1k_output_tokens
28 | 
29 | 
30 | def estimate_cost(prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int) -> float:
31 |     """Return estimated USD cost for a single API call."""
32 |     return (
33 |         prompt_tokens  / 1000.0 * _INPUT_COST_PER_1K +
34 |         completion_tokens / 1000.0 * _OUTPUT_COST_PER_1K
35 |     )
36 | 
37 | 
38 | def record_usage(
39 |     db: Session,
40 |     workspace_id: int | None,
41 |     operation_type: str,
42 |     model_name: str,
43 |     prompt_tokens: int,
44 |     completion_tokens: int,
45 | ) -> LLMUsage:
46 |     """
47 |     Persist one LLMUsage row and update the workspace's running budget totals.
48 |     Re-raises on failure after logging — callers decide whether to absorb the error.
49 |     """
50 |     cost = estimate_cost(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)
51 | 
52 |     try:
53 |         usage = LLMUsage(
54 |             workspace_id=workspace_id,
55 |             operation_type=operation_type,
56 |             model_name=model_name,
57 |             prompt_tokens=prompt_tokens,
58 |             completion_tokens=completion_tokens,
59 |             estimated_cost_usd=cost,
60 |             request_timestamp=datetime.utcnow(),
61 |         )
62 |         db.add(usage)
63 | 
64 |         if workspace_id is not None:
65 |             _update_budget(db, workspace_id, prompt_tokens + completion_tokens, cost)
66 | 
67 |         db.commit()
68 | 
69 |         logger.info(
70 |             "[ws=%s] LLM call recorded: op=%s model=%s tokens=%d+%d cost=$%.6f",
71 |             workspace_id, operation_type, model_name,
72 |             prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost,
73 |         )
74 |         return usage
75 | 
76 |     except Exception as exc:
77 |         logger.error("Failed to record LLM usage: %s", exc)
78 |         db.rollback()
79 |         raise
80 | 
81 | 
82 | def _update_budget(db: Session, workspace_id: int, total_tokens: int, cost: float) -> None:
83 |     """Create or update the LLMBudget row for this workspace."""
84 |     budget = (
85 |         db.query(LLMBudget)
86 |         .filter(LLMBudget.workspace_id == workspace_id)
87 |         .first()
88 |     )
89 |     if budget is None:
90 |         budget = LLMBudget(workspace_id=workspace_id)
91 |         db.add(budget)
92 | 
93 |     budget.current_token_usage = (budget.current_token_usage or 0) + total_tokens
94 |     budget.current_cost_usage  = (budget.current_cost_usage  or 0.0) + cost
95 |     budget.updated_at = datetime.utcnow()
96 |

1 | """
2 | Secret management abstraction layer.
3 | 
4 | Application code retrieves secrets only through a SecretProvider — never
5 | via direct os.getenv() or settings attribute access outside this module.
6 | This makes the secret source swappable without changing any caller.
7 | 
8 | Current implementation: EnvironmentSecretProvider (reads from environment
9 | variables loaded by pydantic-settings). No runtime dependencies beyond the
10 | standard library.
11 | 
12 | Future providers (add without touching callers):
13 |   - AWSSecretsManagerProvider  — fetches from AWS Secrets Manager, supports
14 |                                   automatic rotation via version stages
15 |   - IBMSecretsManagerProvider  — IBM Cloud Secrets Manager API
16 |   - AzureKeyVaultProvider       — Azure Key Vault secrets
17 | 
18 | Rotation workflow
19 | -----------------
20 | 1. Generate new secret value in your secret store.
21 | 2. Update the secret version (AWS: add AWSPENDING label; IBM: create new version).
22 | 3. During deployment, the provider fetches the latest active version automatically.
23 | 4. Revoke the old version after confirming the new one is live.
24 | 5. No application restart required when using a cloud provider.
25 | """
26 | from __future__ import annotations
27 | 
28 | import logging
29 | import os
30 | from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
31 | from functools import lru_cache
32 | 
33 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
34 | 
35 | 
36 | class SecretProvider(ABC):
37 |     """Interface for retrieving named secrets."""
38 | 
39 |     @abstractmethod
40 |     def get_secret(self, secret_name: str) -> str:
41 |         """
42 |         Return the current value of the named secret.
43 |         Raises KeyError if the secret does not exist.
44 |         """
45 | 
46 | 
47 | class EnvironmentSecretProvider(SecretProvider):
48 |     """
49 |     Reads secrets from environment variables.
50 | 
51 |     secret_name maps directly to an environment variable name.
52 |     Suitable for local development and CI.
53 | 
54 |     For production: replace with AWSSecretsManagerProvider and set
55 |     CLAUDE_SECRET_NAME=anthropic-api-key (or whatever name you registered
56 |     in your secret store) instead of placing the raw key in the environment.
57 |     """
58 | 
59 |     def get_secret(self, secret_name: str) -> str:
60 |         value = os.environ.get(secret_name)
61 |         if not value:
62 |             raise KeyError(
63 |                 f"Secret '{secret_name}' not found in environment. "
64 |                 "Set the corresponding environment variable or switch to a "
65 |                 "cloud secret provider for production."
66 |             )
67 |         logger.debug("Secret '%s' retrieved from environment.", secret_name)
68 |         return value
69 | 
70 | 
71 | @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
72 | def get_secret_provider() -> SecretProvider:
73 |     """
74 |     Return the active SecretProvider singleton.
75 | 
76 |     To swap providers (e.g. in tests or for a different deployment target),
77 |     call get_secret_provider.cache_clear() and override the factory here.
78 |     """
79 |     return EnvironmentSecretProvider()
80 |

1 | """
2 | LLM governance layer — budget enforcement and workspace-level rate limiting.
3 | 
4 | Budget enforcement
5 | ------------------
6 | Before every LLM call, check_budget() queries the workspace's LLMBudget row.
7 |   - If monthly_token_limit > 0 and current_token_usage >= limit → HTTP 429
8 |   - If monthly_cost_limit  > 0 and current_cost_usage  >= limit → HTTP 429
9 |   - Limits of 0 mean unlimited (default for new workspaces).
10 | 
11 | Rate limiting
12 | -------------
13 | A simple in-process sliding-window counter per workspace.
14 |   - Window: 60 seconds (configurable via LLM_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS)
15 |   - Limit:  MAX_LLM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE per workspace (default 60)
16 |   - Returns HTTP 429 when the window is full.
17 | 
18 | Note: this in-process rate limiter is suitable for a single-process deployment.
19 | For a multi-process/multi-node deployment replace with a Redis-backed counter.
20 | """
21 | from __future__ import annotations
22 | 
23 | import collections
24 | import logging
25 | import threading
26 | import time
27 | 
28 | from fastapi import HTTPException
29 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
30 | 
31 | from app.config import settings
32 | from app.db.models import LLMBudget
33 | 
34 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
35 | 
36 | 
37 | # ── Budget enforcement ────────────────────────────────────────────────
38 | 
39 | def check_budget(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> None:
40 |     """
41 |     Raise HTTP 429 if the workspace has exceeded its monthly token or cost budget.
42 |     No-op if no budget row exists (unlimited by default).
43 |     """
44 |     budget = (
45 |         db.query(LLMBudget)
46 |         .filter(LLMBudget.workspace_id == workspace_id)
47 |         .first()
48 |     )
49 |     if budget is None:
50 |         return
51 | 
52 |     if budget.monthly_token_limit > 0:
53 |         if budget.current_token_usage >= budget.monthly_token_limit:
54 |             logger.warning(
55 |                 "[ws=%d] Token budget exceeded: %d / %d",
56 |                 workspace_id, budget.current_token_usage, budget.monthly_token_limit,
57 |             )
58 |             raise HTTPException(
59 |                 status_code=429,
60 |                 detail=(
61 |                     f"Workspace LLM token budget exceeded "
62 |                     f"({budget.current_token_usage:,} / {budget.monthly_token_limit:,} tokens used this month)."
63 |                 ),
64 |             )
65 | 
66 |     if budget.monthly_cost_limit > 0.0:
67 |         if budget.current_cost_usage >= budget.monthly_cost_limit:
68 |             logger.warning(
69 |                 "[ws=%d] Cost budget exceeded: $%.4f / $%.4f",
70 |                 workspace_id, budget.current_cost_usage, budget.monthly_cost_limit,
71 |             )
72 |             raise HTTPException(
73 |                 status_code=429,
74 |                 detail=(
75 |                     f"Workspace LLM cost budget exceeded "
76 |                     f"(${budget.current_cost_usage:.4f} / ${budget.monthly_cost_limit:.4f} spent this month)."
77 |                 ),
78 |             )
79 | 
80 | 
81 | # ── Rate limiting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
82 | 
83 | _rate_lock   = threading.Lock()
84 | # workspace_id → deque of request timestamps (float, monotonic)
85 | _rate_windows: dict[int, collections.deque] = collections.defaultdict(
86 |     lambda: collections.deque()
87 | )
88 | 
89 | 
90 | def check_rate_limit(workspace_id: int) -> None:
91 |     """
92 |     Raise HTTP 429 if the workspace has made more than
93 |     MAX_LLM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE LLM calls in the last LLM_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS.
94 |     """
95 |     limit  = settings.max_llm_requests_per_minute
96 |     window = settings.llm_rate_window_seconds
97 |     now    = time.monotonic()
98 |     cutoff = now - window
99 | 
100 |     with _rate_lock:
101 |         dq = _rate_windows[workspace_id]
102 |         # Remove timestamps outside the current window
103 |         while dq and dq[0] < cutoff:
104 |             dq.popleft()
105 | 
106 |         if len(dq) >= limit:
107 |             logger.warning(
108 |                 "[ws=%d] LLM rate limit hit: %d requests in %.0fs window.",
109 |                 workspace_id, len(dq), window,
110 |             )
111 |             raise HTTPException(
112 |                 status_code=429,
113 |                 detail=(
114 |                     f"LLM request rate limit exceeded "
115 |                     f"({limit} requests per {window:.0f}s). Please slow down."
116 |                 ),
117 |             )
118 | 
119 |         dq.append(now)
120 |

1 | """
2 | Circuit breaker for LLM calls.
3 | 
4 | Protects the application from cascading failures when the LLM provider is
5 | unavailable, rate-limiting, or timing out.
6 | 
7 | State machine
8 | -------------
9 | CLOSED   — normal operation; failures are counted
10 | OPEN     — breaker is tripped; all calls are rejected immediately
11 | HALF_OPEN — recovery probe; a single call is allowed through to test health
12 | 
13 | Transition rules
14 | ----------------
15 | CLOSED  → OPEN      when consecutive_failures >= failure_threshold
16 | OPEN    → HALF_OPEN after recovery_timeout_seconds have elapsed
17 | HALF_OPEN → CLOSED  on successful call
18 | HALF_OPEN → OPEN    on failed call (resets the recovery timer)
19 | 
20 | Configuration (all via environment / Settings):
21 |   LLM_CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD   default 5   failures before opening
22 |   LLM_CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT    default 60  seconds before half-open probe
23 | """
24 | from __future__ import annotations
25 | 
26 | import logging
27 | import threading
28 | import time
29 | from enum import Enum
30 | 
31 | from fastapi import HTTPException
32 | 
33 | from app.config import settings
34 | 
35 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
36 | 
37 | 
38 | class BreakerState(str, Enum):
39 |     CLOSED    = "closed"
40 |     OPEN      = "open"
41 |     HALF_OPEN = "half_open"
42 | 
43 | 
44 | class CircuitBreaker:
45 |     """
46 |     Thread-safe circuit breaker.
47 | 
48 |     Usage::
49 | 
50 |         breaker = CircuitBreaker()
51 | 
52 |         with breaker:
53 |             result = call_llm_api()
54 |     """
55 | 
56 |     def __init__(
57 |         self,
58 |         failure_threshold: int | None = None,
59 |         recovery_timeout: float | None = None,
60 |     ) -> None:
61 |         self._threshold = failure_threshold or settings.llm_cb_failure_threshold
62 |         self._timeout   = recovery_timeout  or settings.llm_cb_recovery_timeout
63 |         self._failures  = 0
64 |         self._state     = BreakerState.CLOSED
65 |         self._opened_at: float | None = None
66 |         self._lock      = threading.Lock()
67 | 
68 |     # ── public API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
69 | 
70 |     @property
71 |     def state(self) -> BreakerState:
72 |         with self._lock:
73 |             return self._evaluated_state()
74 | 
75 |     def record_success(self) -> None:
76 |         with self._lock:
77 |             self._failures = 0
78 |             self._state    = BreakerState.CLOSED
79 |             self._opened_at = None
80 |         logger.debug("Circuit breaker: call succeeded → CLOSED")
81 | 
82 |     def record_failure(self) -> None:
83 |         with self._lock:
84 |             self._failures += 1
85 |             if self._failures >= self._threshold:
86 |                 self._state     = BreakerState.OPEN
87 |                 self._opened_at = time.monotonic()
88 |                 logger.warning(
89 |                     "Circuit breaker OPEN after %d consecutive failures.", self._failures
90 |                 )
91 | 
92 |     def __enter__(self) -> "CircuitBreaker":
93 |         with self._lock:
94 |             state = self._evaluated_state()
95 | 
96 |         if state == BreakerState.OPEN:
97 |             logger.warning("Circuit breaker is OPEN — rejecting LLM request.")
98 |             raise HTTPException(
99 |                 status_code=503,
100 |                 detail="LLM service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.",
101 |             )
102 |         return self
103 | 
104 |     def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> bool:
105 |         if exc_type is None:
106 |             self.record_success()
107 |         else:
108 |             # Only count genuine provider/network errors, not validation errors.
109 |             if not issubclass(exc_type, (ValueError, HTTPException)):
110 |                 self.record_failure()
111 |         return False  # never suppress exceptions
112 | 
113 |     # ── internals ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
114 | 
115 |     def _evaluated_state(self) -> BreakerState:
116 |         """
117 |         Transition OPEN → HALF_OPEN if the recovery timeout has elapsed.
118 |         Must be called with self._lock held.
119 |         """
120 |         if self._state == BreakerState.OPEN and self._opened_at is not None:
121 |             elapsed = time.monotonic() - self._opened_at
122 |             if elapsed >= self._timeout:
123 |                 self._state = BreakerState.HALF_OPEN
124 |                 logger.info(
125 |                     "Circuit breaker: recovery timeout elapsed (%.0fs) → HALF_OPEN",
126 |                     elapsed,
127 |                 )
128 |         return self._state
129 | 
130 | 
131 | # Application-level singleton — shared across all threads in one process.
132 | # Tests can call circuit_breaker._failures = 0; circuit_breaker._state = CLOSED
133 | # to reset between cases.
134 | circuit_breaker = CircuitBreaker()
135 |

1 | """
2 | LLM retry policy — tenacity-based retry with exponential backoff + jitter.
3 | 
4 | Transient errors that are retried:
5 |   - httpx.TimeoutException  (connect, read, write, pool timeout)
6 |   - httpx.ConnectError      (DNS failure, TCP refused)
7 |   - httpx.RemoteProtocolError
8 |   - anthropic.APIStatusError with status 429 (rate-limited by upstream)
9 |   - anthropic.APIStatusError with status 5xx (provider-side errors)
10 | 
11 | Errors that are NOT retried (fail immediately):
12 |   - anthropic.AuthenticationError  (bad API key)
13 |   - anthropic.PermissionDeniedError
14 |   - anthropic.NotFoundError
15 |   - anthropic.UnprocessableEntityError  (invalid prompt / request body)
16 |   - fastapi.HTTPException              (circuit breaker open, budget exceeded)
17 |   - ValueError / TypeError             (programming errors)
18 | 
19 | Configuration (via settings):
20 |   LLM_MAX_RETRIES      default 4   attempts before giving up (1 original + 3 retries)

43 | # ── Transient-error predicate ──────────────────────────────────────────

45 | def _is_transient(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
46 |     """
47 |     Return True if the exception is a transient failure that is safe to retry.
48 |     Anything returning False will propagate immediately without further attempts.
49 |     """
50 |     # Network-level transients (timeout, connection refused, broken pipe)
51 |     if isinstance(exc, (httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.ConnectError, httpx.RemoteProtocolError)):
52 |         return True
53 | 
54 |     # Upstream HTTP status codes that indicate a temporary condition
55 |     if isinstance(exc, anthropic.APIStatusError):
56 |         return exc.status_code in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504)
57 | 
58 |     # Everything else (auth errors, validation errors, circuit-breaker 503s) → fail fast
59 |     return False
60 | 
61 | 
62 | # ── Retry decorator factory ────────────────────────────────────────────
63 | 
64 | def llm_retry():
65 |     """
66 |     Return a tenacity @retry decorator configured from application settings.
67 | 
68 |     Called as a factory so the decorator always reads the live settings values
69 |     (useful in tests that monkeypatch settings).
70 | 
71 |     Usage::
72 | 
73 |         @llm_retry()
74 |         def _call_api(...):
75 |             ...
76 |     """
77 |     return retry(
78 |         retry=retry_if_exception(_is_transient),
79 |         stop=stop_after_attempt(settings.llm_max_retries + 1),   # +1 = original attempt
80 |         wait=wait_exponential_jitter(
81 |             initial=1.0,
82 |             max=settings.llm_retry_max_wait,
83 |             jitter=1.0,
84 |         ),
85 |         before_sleep=before_sleep_log(logger, logging.WARNING),
86 |         reraise=False,   # raises tenacity.RetryError on exhaustion — caller normalises it
87 |     )

91 |     """Return True when tenacity has given up after all attempts."""

1 | # Knowledge Intelligence Platform
2 | 
3 | **An evidence-grounded knowledge compiler that transforms consulting assets into a connected intelligence layer of concepts, relationships, consulting patterns, and reusable expertise.**
4 | 
5 | Every AI-generated insight is traceable back to source evidence from uploaded assets. No external knowledge. No fabricated citations.

8 | 
9 | ## Problem Statement
10 | 
11 | Organisations produce vast amounts of institutional knowledge — Points of View, Business Requirements Documents, proposal decks, architecture documents, research papers, case studies, and delivery playbooks. This knowledge is trapped across disconnected files, siloed in individual experts, and rarely reused effectively.
12 | 
13 | When a practitioner starts a new engagement, they have no reliable way to ask:
14 | - *Has this problem been solved before, and where is the evidence?*
15 | - *How do these concepts connect across our body of work?*
16 | - *What is our organisation's documented position on this topic?*
17 | 
18 | The result: knowledge is repeatedly rediscovered, deliverables are drafted from scratch, and AI tools produce answers from their training data rather than from your organisation's own documented expertise.
19 | 
20 | ---
21 | 
22 | ## Solution
23 | 
24 | The Knowledge Intelligence Platform compiles your consulting content into a structured, connected knowledge layer:
25 | 
26 | | What you upload | What the platform builds |
27 | |---|---|
28 | | PDFs, DOCX, PPTX files | **Concepts** — named, typed, with verbatim source excerpts |
29 | | Documents across a domain | **Relationships** — how concepts connect across documents |
30 | | A body of work | **Consulting Patterns** — recurring approaches to recurring problems |
31 | | All of the above | **Knowledge Graph** — an interactive, explorable intelligence layer |
32 | | Questions | **Evidence-grounded answers** — every claim traced to a source document |
33 | | A topic + audience | **Client-ready deliverables** — POVs, executive summaries, roadmaps |

37 | ## LLM Governance
38 | 
39 | Every LLM call passes through a governance pipeline before reaching the provider:
40 | 
41 | | Layer | What it does |
42 | |---|---|
43 | | **Secret Provider** | API key fetched via `SecretProvider` abstraction — never directly from `os.environ` in business logic. Swap to `AWSSecretsManagerProvider` for production with zero code changes |
44 | | **Circuit Breaker** | Opens after 5 consecutive failures; auto-recovers after 60s. Rejects all calls while open (HTTP 503) to prevent cascade failures |
45 | | **Rate Limiter** | Per-workspace sliding-window counter — default 60 requests/min. Returns HTTP 429 when exceeded |
46 | | **Budget Check** | Per-workspace monthly token and cost limits enforced before each call. Returns HTTP 429 when exceeded |
47 | | **Usage Tracker** | Every call writes one `LLMUsage` row with token counts and estimated cost. Running totals accumulated in `LLMBudget` |
48 | | **Observability** | Structured log lines include workspace ID, operation, latency, token counts, and cost estimate. API keys, prompts, and credentials are never logged |
49 | 
50 | Admin visibility: `GET /admin/llm/usage` and `GET /admin/llm/budgets` return usage aggregates and budget status.
51 | 
52 | ---
53 | 
54 | ## Upload Security
55 | 
56 | Every uploaded file passes through a three-stage validation pipeline before it touches the filesystem or a parser:
57 | 
58 | | Stage | What is checked | How |
59 | |---|---|---|
60 | | **Magic-byte detection** | Actual file format — not the filename or `Content-Type` header | `filetype` library reads the binary signature from the first 8 KB |
61 | | **Allow-list enforcement** | Only PDF, DOCX, PPTX are accepted | Any other detected MIME type returns HTTP 422 |
62 | | **Size limit** | Default 25 MB per file, configurable via `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | Streamed check — oversized files return HTTP 413 before being fully buffered |
63 | 
64 | **Why magic bytes instead of extensions?** A file named `malware.pdf` with a ZIP or executable binary inside will pass an extension check but fail the magic-byte check. Attackers control the filename and `Content-Type` header; they do not control the binary content signature.
65 | 
66 | All parsers (PyMuPDF, python-docx, python-pptx) are wrapped with defensive exception handling. A corrupt or malformed file marks the document as `failed` with a clean error message — no stack traces are ever exposed to the client.

73 | Isolated knowledge domains. Each workspace contains its own documents, concepts, relationships, and patterns. No cross-workspace knowledge leakage.

81 | - **Relationship Agent** — discovers how concepts connect across documents using fuzzy name resolution

The assistant retrieves relevant context using graph-first traversal (not keyword search), assembles evidence from the knowledge graph, and generates answers that cite their exact source document and excerpt. If the answer is not in your documents, it says so explicitly. Fabrication is architecturally prevented.

301 | ## How It Works
302 | 
303 | ### 1. Knowledge Compilation (Upload → Concepts → Graph)
304 | 
305 | When you upload a document, the platform runs three chained extraction agents:
306 | 
307 | 1. **Concept Agent** — reads the document text and extracts named concepts with verbatim source excerpts and confidence scores. Concepts below the confidence threshold are discarded.
308 | 2. **Relationship Agent** — looks across all workspace concepts and identifies how this document's concepts connect to existing ones. Relationship strength is scored and stored.
309 | 3. **Pattern Agent** — examines the full workspace concept and relationship map and identifies recurring consulting patterns.
310 | 
311 | Every extracted item carries a `source_document_id` and `source_excerpt`. Items without traceable sources are rejected before storage.
312 | 
313 | ### 2. Evidence-Grounded Q&A (Question → Answer)
314 | 
315 | When you ask a question:
316 | 
317 | 1. Keywords are extracted from the question (LLM-assisted, temperature=0)
318 | 2. Concept nodes are scored using **cumulative multi-signal matching** across all keywords — exact name, substring, type, description — weighted by concept confidence
319 | 3. The top seeds are expanded via **strength-filtered BFS** through the knowledge graph
320 | 4. Retrieved concepts are sorted deterministically: seed relevance DESC, confidence DESC, then concept ID as tie-break
321 | 5. Near-duplicate source excerpts are deduplicated before the context window is assembled
322 | 6. Claude generates an answer from the context at temperature=0, citing every claim with `[Source: Document Name]`
323 | 7. If the answer is non-empty but sources are empty, it is rejected — the grounding rule is enforced at the `SourcedResponseMixin` schema level, not just in a prompt
324 | 
325 | ### 3. Grounding Rule (Hard Constraint)
326 | 
327 | The platform does not use internet search, web browsing, or general knowledge for any compilation, answer, or deliverable. The `SourcedResponseMixin` in `schemas.py` is a Pydantic `model_validator` that runs before any AI response leaves the API. An answer without sources is a schema validation error.

1 | # Knowledge Intelligence Platform — System Architecture
2 | 
3 | ---
4 | 
5 | ## 1. Vision & Positioning
6 | 
7 | The Knowledge Intelligence Platform is an **evidence-grounded knowledge compiler** for IBM Consulting.
8 | It is not a chatbot, not a document search tool, and not a generic RAG pipeline.
9 | It transforms fragmented institutional knowledge — POVs, BRDs, case studies, playbooks, architecture documents — into a structured, connected, evidence-traceable knowledge layer.
10 | 
11 | **The grounding rule is architectural, not just a prompt constraint:**
12 | Every compiled item (concept, relationship, pattern) carries a `source_document_id` and `source_excerpt` in the database.
13 | Every AI-generated response (answer, comparison, deliverable) returns a structured `sources` field — enforced at the Pydantic schema level before any response leaves the API.
14 | 
15 | ---
16 | 
17 | ## 2. System Architecture
18 |

30 | │                                                                  │
31 | │  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  │
32 | │  │  Document        │  │  Knowledge       │  │  Graph Engine  │  │

60 | 
61 | ## 3. Knowledge Compilation Pipeline
62 | 
63 | The extraction pipeline has three chained agents, each running after every document ingestion:
64 | 
65 | ```
66 | Upload (PDF / DOCX / PPTX)
67 |         │
68 |         ▼
69 | Magic-byte validation → file-type detection → route to parser
70 |   PDF  → PyMuPDF
71 |   DOCX → python-docx
72 |   PPTX → python-pptx
73 |         │
74 |         ▼
75 | Store Document row (status=processing, raw_text saved)
76 |         │
77 |         ▼
78 | ┌── Agent 1: Concept Compiler ─────────────────────────────────┐
79 | │  Prompt LLM with chunked document text                       │
80 | │  Extracts: {name, type, description, source_excerpt}         │
81 | │  source_excerpt = verbatim quote from document text          │
82 | │  Pydantic validation → reject any item missing source_excerpt│
83 | │  Insert Concept rows (source_document_id = this doc)         │
84 | └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
85 |         │
86 |         ▼
87 | ┌── Agent 2: Relationship Compiler ────────────────────────────┐
88 | │  Load all workspace Concepts                                 │
89 | │  Prompt LLM with concept list + document text                │
90 | │  Extracts: {source, target, relationship_type}               │
91 | │  Fuzzy-match concept names → resolve to Concept IDs         │
92 | │  Only accept relationships where both concepts exist in DB   │
93 | │  Insert Relationship rows                                    │
94 | └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
95 |         │
96 |         ▼
97 | ┌── Agent 3: Pattern Compiler ─────────────────────────────────┐
98 | │  Load workspace Concepts + Relationships                     │
99 | │  Prompt LLM with full workspace knowledge context            │
100 | │  Extracts: {name, problem_statement, ibm_approach[], ...}    │
101 | │  Upsert ConsultingPattern rows (by name within workspace)    │
102 | └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
103 |         │
104 |         ▼
105 | Update Document: status=complete
106 | (on exception: status=failed, error_message=str(e))
107 | ```
108 | 
109 | **Why this chained agent approach?**
110 | Concept extraction is scoped to a single document — it only needs that document's text.
111 | Relationship extraction needs the full workspace concept map to avoid hallucinating concept names.
112 | Pattern extraction needs the full workspace graph — it looks for cross-document recurring structures.
113 | Chaining these three agents lets each one benefit from the work of the previous while keeping the extraction logic separated and testable.
114 | 
115 | ---
116 | 
117 | ## 4. Evidence-Grounded Q&A Pipeline (Graph-First Retrieval)
118 | 
119 | ```
120 | User question → POST /workspaces/{id}/ask
121 |         │
122 |         ▼
123 | 1. Keyword extraction (LLM-assisted + token fallback)
124 |         │
125 |         ▼
126 | 2. Graph-first retrieval:
127 |    Load workspace NetworkX graph (built from Concept + Relationship rows)
128 |    Match concept nodes by keyword → expand N-hop neighbourhood (default: 2 hops)
129 |         │
130 |         ▼
131 | 3. Evidence assembly:
132 |    Pull source_excerpt for every node in the subgraph
133 |    Pull ConsultingPattern rows referencing matched concepts
134 |    Assemble context window: {concept, description, excerpt, source doc}
135 |         │
136 |         ▼
137 | 4. LLM generates answer (Claude, context-only):
138 |    System prompt: "Answer ONLY from the provided context.
139 |    If context doesn't support the answer, say: not found in the uploaded knowledge.
140 |    Cite every claim with [Source: Document Name]."
141 |         │
142 |         ▼
143 | 5. Validation: answer is non-"not found" AND sources is empty → reject, return not-found
144 |         │
145 |         ▼
146 | 6. Persist ChatMessage rows (user + assistant)
147 |    Return: {answer, sources: [{document_name, excerpt}]}
148 | ```
149 | 
150 | **Why graph-first, not embeddings-first?**
151 | Graph traversal surfaces structured relationships — ISO 20022 *implements* SWIFT *enables* real-time settlement — that embedding similarity cannot. For IBM Consulting use cases where the *connection between concepts* is the value, graph traversal produces better context than nearest-neighbour vector retrieval. Embeddings can be layered in as a fallback if keyword matching proves too sparse, but graph traversal is the primary retrieval mechanism.
152 | 
153 | ---
154 | 
155 | ## 5. Data Model
156 | 
157 | ```
158 | Workspace ─── Document ─── Concept ─── Relationship (Concept → Concept)
159 |     │              │                        │
160 |     │              └──────────────► source_document_id
161 |     │
162 |     ├── ConsultingPattern (related_concept_ids[], source_document_ids[])
163 |     ├── Deliverable       (source_concept_ids[], source_document_ids[])
164 |     └── ChatMessage       (source_document_ids[])
165 | ```
166 | 
167 | All JSON list fields (`topics`, `ibm_approach`, `related_concept_ids`, etc.) are stored as JSON text via a `TypeDecorator` — transparent on read/write, portable across SQLite and PostgreSQL.
168 | 
169 | All foreign keys are indexed. Cascade delete on workspace removes all associated rows.
170 | 
171 | ---
172 | 
173 | ## 6. Repository / Interface Layer
174 | 
175 | Every storage operation goes through a SQLAlchemy ORM query — no raw SQL. This means:
176 | - SQLite → PostgreSQL: change `DATABASE_URL`, zero code changes required.
177 | - NetworkX → Neo4j: implement `GraphRepository` with the same interface as `builder.py` + `traversal.py`.
178 | 
179 | ---
180 | 
181 | ## 7. MVP vs Phase 2 Architecture
182 | 
183 | | Component | MVP | Phase 2 |
184 | |---|---|---|
185 | | Database | SQLite | RDS PostgreSQL (same ORM) |
186 | | Graph engine | NetworkX in-process | Amazon Neptune / Neo4j |
187 | | Task queue | FastAPI BackgroundTasks | SQS + Celery worker fleet |
188 | | File storage | Local disk (`./uploads`) | S3 |
189 | | Deployment | `uvicorn` local | ECS Fargate + CloudFront |
190 | | Auth | None | IBM SSO / Cognito |
191 | | LLM | Anthropic direct API | Amazon Bedrock (Claude) |
192 | | Vector search (optional) | None | pgvector / OpenSearch |
193 | 
194 | ---
195 | 
196 | ## 8. Non-Goals (Phase 2)
197 | 
198 | Authentication, multi-tenant isolation, CI/CD, production deployment, real-time collaborative editing, IBM enterprise system integrations (SharePoint, Teams, Confluence), document versioning.
199 |

1 | # ADR: Payments Center Brain
2 | 
3 | **Status:** Proposed — not implemented  
4 | **Date:** 2025  
5 | **Deciders:** Knowledge Intelligence Platform team  
6 | 
7 | ---
8 | 
9 | ## Context
10 | 
11 | The Knowledge Intelligence Platform currently operates on a per-workspace model. Each workspace is an isolated knowledge domain: practitioners upload documents, the platform compiles them into a knowledge graph, and all retrieval and generation is scoped exclusively to that workspace.
12 | 
13 | This design is correct for project-specific and engagement-specific knowledge. However, it creates a gap for **practice-level institutional knowledge** — the accumulated domain expertise that belongs to an entire practice (e.g. the Payments Center of Excellence) rather than to any single engagement.
14 | 
15 | Today, this practice-level knowledge is either:
16 | - Uploaded repeatedly into individual workspaces (duplicated effort, inconsistent across workspaces), or
17 | - Not available to the platform at all (practitioners miss relevant institutional context when generating deliverables).
18 | 
19 | ---
20 | 
21 | ## Decision
22 | 
23 | We will design a **Payments Center Brain** — a centralised, shared institutional knowledge graph built from practice-wide assets and maintained by practice leads.
24 | 
25 | This is a **future enhancement**. It is documented here to preserve architectural intent and inform implementation decisions made before this feature is built.
26 | 
27 | ---
28 | 
29 | ## Proposed Design
30 | 
31 | ### What it is
32 | 
33 | A shared, read-only knowledge graph scoped to the Payments Center of Excellence (and extensible to other practices). It is compiled from curated practice assets — canonical POVs, reference architectures, domain standards documents, methodology guides — and maintained by designated practice knowledge owners.
34 | 
35 | Unlike workspace knowledge graphs (which are project-specific and mutable by any workspace member), the Payments Center Brain is:
36 | - **Shared** — visible to practitioners across all workspaces
37 | - **Curated** — managed by practice leads, not individual project teams
38 | - **Additive** — it supplements workspace knowledge, never replaces it
39 | 
40 | ### Data sources
41 | 
42 | The Payments Center Brain will ingest from:
43 | - SharePoint document libraries (Payments Center of Excellence repository)
44 | - Box repositories (shared practice knowledge stores)
45 | - Bulk-imported domain documents (standards, regulatory frameworks, methodology guides)
46 | 
47 | Ingestion uses the same three-agent compilation pipeline (Concept → Relationship → Pattern) already implemented for workspace documents.
48 | 
49 | ### Knowledge scope selector
50 | 
51 | When a practitioner generates a deliverable (POV, BRD, PRD, Executive Summary, Roadmap), they will be offered a knowledge scope choice:
52 | 
53 | ```
54 | Knowledge Scope
55 | ───────────────
56 | ( ) Workspace Only
57 |     Use only documents uploaded to this workspace.
58 | 
59 | (●) Workspace + Payments Center Brain
60 |     Include institutional practice knowledge alongside workspace documents.
61 |     Source citations will identify whether each claim came from workspace
62 |     documents or from the shared practice knowledge base.
63 | ```
64 | 
65 | The default is **Workspace Only** to preserve the current behaviour and workspace isolation guarantee.
66 | 
67 | When **Workspace + Payments Center Brain** is selected:
68 | - The retrieval pipeline queries both the workspace graph and the shared graph
69 | - Retrieved concepts from both sources are merged and ranked together
70 | - Source citations distinguish between workspace sources and shared knowledge sources
71 | - The grounding rule applies equally to both sources — every claim must trace to a document
72 | 
73 | ### Workspace behaviour is unchanged
74 | 
75 | Individual workspaces remain fully isolated from each other. The Payments Center Brain is an **opt-in additive layer**, not a shared context that is always present. Enabling it for one query does not affect other workspaces or other queries.
76 | 
77 | ---
78 | 
79 | ## Consequences
80 | 
81 | ### Benefits
82 | - Practitioners gain access to canonical institutional knowledge without uploading it to every workspace
83 | - Practice leads can ensure consistent, authoritative information is available across all engagements
84 | - Deliverables can synthesise both project-specific findings and practice-wide expertise in a single, source-cited output
85 | 
86 | ### Risks and mitigations
87 | - **Staleness:** Shared knowledge must be actively maintained. Implement a `last_reviewed` date on shared documents and surface a warning when knowledge is older than a configurable threshold.
88 | - **Authority conflicts:** When workspace knowledge contradicts shared knowledge, the system must surface both views and let the practitioner decide. Never silently merge conflicting claims.
89 | - **Access control:** The Payments Center Brain requires authentication and role-based access before it can be safely shared across practitioners. This feature is therefore blocked on authentication implementation.
90 | - **Context explosion:** Combining two knowledge graphs risks assembling too much context. The existing `QA_TOP_K` and `GRAPH_MAX_NODES` caps apply independently to each source and must be configured appropriately.
91 | 
92 | ---
93 | 
94 | ## Implementation Prerequisites
95 | 
96 | Before this feature can be built:
97 | 
98 | 1. **Authentication and authorisation** — practitioners must have verified identities before shared knowledge can be exposed
99 | 2. **SharePoint / Box connectors** — bulk ingestion from external repositories requires OAuth integration with those systems
100 | 3. **Multi-source retrieval** — the retrieval pipeline must support querying and merging results from two independent knowledge graphs
101 | 4. **Source provenance display** — the frontend must distinguish workspace citations from shared knowledge citations
102 | 
103 | ---
104 | 
105 | ## Out of Scope for this ADR
106 | 
107 | - Implementation timeline
108 | - Specific SharePoint or Box API integration details
109 | - Authentication mechanism selection
110 | - Multi-practice generalisation (this ADR scopes to Payments Center; other practices are analogous but separate decisions)
111 |

"""
Pattern evolution tracker and threshold engine.

Determines whether pattern extraction should run after a graph update,
based on how much the workspace's knowledge has grown since the last run.
Records each extraction decision as a PatternExtractionRun audit row.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from datetime import datetime

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.config import settings
from app.db.models import Concept, PatternExtractionRun, Relationship, Workspace

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def should_run_pattern_extraction(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> bool:
    """
    Return True if the workspace knowledge has grown enough since the last
    pattern extraction run to justify re-running the pattern agent.

    Decision logic
    --------------
    1. If extraction has never run → always run.
    2. Compute growth percentage for both concepts and relationships since
       concept_count_at_last_pattern_run / relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run.
    3. If either metric grew by ≥ PATTERN_EXTRACTION_THRESHOLD_PERCENT → run.
    4. Otherwise skip and log the decision.
    """
    ws = db.get(Workspace, workspace_id)
    if ws is None:
        return False

    current_concept_count = (
        db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).count()
    )
    current_rel_count = (
        db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == workspace_id).count()
    )

    prev_concept_count = ws.concept_count_at_last_pattern_run or 0
    prev_rel_count = ws.relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run or 0

    # Always run if extraction has never happened
    if prev_concept_count == 0 and prev_rel_count == 0:
        logger.info(
            "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — first extraction, running unconditionally "
            "(concepts=%d, relationships=%d).",
            workspace_id, current_concept_count, current_rel_count,
        )
        return True

    threshold = settings.pattern_extraction_threshold_pct

    concept_growth = (
        ((current_concept_count - prev_concept_count) / prev_concept_count * 100)
        if prev_concept_count > 0
        else 100.0
    )
    rel_growth = (
        ((current_rel_count - prev_rel_count) / prev_rel_count * 100)
        if prev_rel_count > 0
        else 0.0
    )

    should_run = concept_growth >= threshold or rel_growth >= threshold

    logger.info(
        "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — concept growth=%.1f%% (prev=%d, now=%d), "
        "rel growth=%.1f%% (prev=%d, now=%d), threshold=%.1f%% → %s",
        workspace_id,
        concept_growth, prev_concept_count, current_concept_count,
        rel_growth, prev_rel_count, current_rel_count,
        threshold,
        "RUN" if should_run else "SKIP",
    )
    return should_run


def record_pattern_run(
    db: Session,
    workspace_id: int,
    concept_count: int,
    relationship_count: int,
    patterns_generated: int,
    status: str = "complete",
) -> PatternExtractionRun:
    """
    Persist a PatternExtractionRun audit row and update the Workspace
    knowledge-evolution counters so the next threshold check is accurate.
    """
    ws = db.get(Workspace, workspace_id)
    graph_version = ws.graph_version if ws else 0

    run = PatternExtractionRun(
        workspace_id=workspace_id,
        started_at=datetime.utcnow(),
        completed_at=datetime.utcnow(),
        concept_count=concept_count,
        relationship_count=relationship_count,
        patterns_generated=patterns_generated,
        graph_version=graph_version,
        status=status,
    )
    db.add(run)

    if ws:
        ws.last_pattern_extraction_at = datetime.utcnow()
        ws.concept_count_at_last_pattern_run = concept_count
        ws.relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run = relationship_count

    db.commit()
    logger.info(
        "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — run recorded: status=%s concepts=%d rels=%d patterns=%d graph_v=%d",
        workspace_id, status, concept_count, relationship_count, patterns_generated, graph_version,
    )
    return run

"""
GraphMemoryManager — single entry point for all graph operations.

Architecture
------------
SQL tables remain the system of record. The NetworkX graph is a derived,
in-memory operational layer maintained by this manager.

Every node stores:
    source_document_ids : set[int]  — which documents contributed this concept
    evidence_count      : int       — number of contributing documents

Every edge stores:
    source_document_ids : set[int]  — which documents support this relationship
    evidence_count      : int       — number of supporting documents

Lifecycle
---------
startup_load()              — called once on application startup; loads all
                              workspaces that have at least one complete document.
get_workspace_graph()       — returns the in-memory graph; builds from SQL on
                              first access (cache miss).
add_document_contributions()  — incremental node/edge additions after ingestion.
remove_document_contributions() — evidence-based pruning after document deletion.
invalidate()                — evict the cached graph so the next access rebuilds.
rebuild_workspace_graph()   — force a full SQL rebuild for one workspace.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import threading
import time
from datetime import datetime

import networkx as nx
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.db.models import Concept, Relationship, Workspace
from app.db.session import SessionLocal
from app.graph.builder import build_workspace_graph
from app.graph.store import WorkspaceGraphStore

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ── Provenance helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _node_attrs_from_concept(c: Concept) -> dict:
    """Build the node attribute dict for a concept, including provenance sets."""
    doc_ids: set[int] = {c.source_document_id} if c.source_document_id else set()
    return {
        "name": c.name,
        "type": c.type or "General",
        "description": c.description or "",
        "source_document_id": c.source_document_id,
        "source_excerpt": c.source_excerpt or "",
        "confidence": float(getattr(c, "confidence", 0.8)),
        # provenance
        "source_document_ids": doc_ids,
        "evidence_count": len(doc_ids),
    }


def _edge_attrs_from_relationship(r: Relationship) -> dict:
    """Build the edge attribute dict for a relationship, including provenance sets."""
    doc_ids: set[int] = {r.source_document_id} if r.source_document_id else set()
    strength = float(getattr(r, "strength", 0.7)) or 0.7
    return {
        "relationship_id": r.id,
        "relationship_type": r.relationship_type,
        "source_document_id": r.source_document_id,
        "strength": strength,
        "weight": round(1.0 / max(strength, 0.01), 4),
        # provenance
        "source_document_ids": doc_ids,
        "evidence_count": len(doc_ids),
    }


def _build_provenance_graph(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """
    Build a provenance-aware graph from SQL.

    Differs from builder.build_workspace_graph() in that each node and edge
    carries a `source_document_ids` set and `evidence_count` integer, which
    enable incremental add/remove operations without a full SQL rebuild.
    """
    G = nx.DiGraph()

    concepts = db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).all()
    for c in concepts:
        G.add_node(c.id, **_node_attrs_from_concept(c))

    relationships = db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == workspace_id).all()
    for r in relationships:
        if not (G.has_node(r.source_concept_id) and G.has_node(r.target_concept_id)):
            continue
        G.add_edge(r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id, **_edge_attrs_from_relationship(r))

    return G


# ── Manager ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


class GraphMemoryManager:
    """
    Manages the lifecycle of in-memory workspace graphs.

    One instance is created at module level as the application singleton.
    All services call get_workspace_graph() instead of build_workspace_graph().
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._store = WorkspaceGraphStore()
        self._build_lock: dict[int, threading.Lock] = {}
        self._meta_lock = threading.Lock()

    # ── startup ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def startup_load(self) -> None:
        """
        Load all workspaces with at least one complete document into memory.
        Called once from main.py lifespan after init_db().
        """
        db = SessionLocal()
        try:
            from app.db.models import Document  # local import avoids circular dependency
            workspace_ids = (
                db.query(Workspace.id)
                .join(Document, Document.workspace_id == Workspace.id)
                .filter(Document.upload_status == "complete")
                .distinct()
                .all()
            )
            ws_ids = [row[0] for row in workspace_ids]
            logger.info(
                "[graph_memory] Startup load: %d workspace(s) with complete documents.",
                len(ws_ids),
            )
            for ws_id in ws_ids:
                t0 = time.monotonic()
                G = _build_provenance_graph(db, ws_id)
                self._store.put(ws_id, G)
                logger.info(
                    "[graph_memory] ws=%d loaded: %d nodes, %d edges (%.0fms)",
                    ws_id, G.number_of_nodes(), G.number_of_edges(),
                    (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,
                )
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("[graph_memory] Startup load failed — graphs will be built on first access.")
        finally:
            db.close()

    # ── read ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def get_workspace_graph(self, workspace_id: int, db: Session | None = None) -> nx.DiGraph:
        """
        Return the in-memory graph for this workspace.

        If the graph is not yet loaded, builds it from SQL (cache miss).
        A per-workspace lock prevents duplicate builds when two requests arrive
        simultaneously for an un-loaded workspace.

        Parameters
        ----------
        workspace_id : the workspace to retrieve.
        db           : optional SQLAlchemy session; only used on cache miss.
                       If None on a miss, a new session is opened internally.
        """
        G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
        if G is not None:
            return G

        build_lock = self._get_build_lock(workspace_id)
        with build_lock:
            # Re-check after acquiring the lock — another thread may have built it.
            G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
            if G is not None:
                return G

            return self._build_and_store(workspace_id, db)

    # ── incremental add ───────────────────────────────────────────────

    def add_document_contributions(self, workspace_id: int, document_id: int, db: Session) -> None:
        """
        Incrementally add a document's concepts and relationships to the
        workspace graph.  If the graph is not loaded, performs a full build
        from SQL (which will include the new document's contributions naturally).

        This is called by the ingestion pipeline immediately after
        upload_status is set to "complete".
        """
        G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
        if G is None:
            self._build_and_store(workspace_id, db)
            logger.info(
                "[graph_memory] ws=%d doc=%d — graph was not loaded; performed full build.",
                workspace_id, document_id,
            )
            self._bump_graph_version(db, workspace_id)
            return

        t0 = time.monotonic()
        build_lock = self._get_build_lock(workspace_id)
        with build_lock:
            # Load only concepts and relationships from this document.
            new_concepts = (
                db.query(Concept)
                .filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id, Concept.source_document_id == document_id)
                .all()
            )
            new_relationships = (
                db.query(Relationship)
                .filter(
                    Relationship.workspace_id == workspace_id,
                    Relationship.source_document_id == document_id,
                )
                .all()
            )

            nodes_added = 0
            edges_added = 0

            for c in new_concepts:
                if G.has_node(c.id):
                    # Merge provenance into existing node.
                    existing_ids: set[int] = G.nodes[c.id].get("source_document_ids", set())
                    existing_ids.add(document_id)
                    G.nodes[c.id]["source_document_ids"] = existing_ids
                    G.nodes[c.id]["evidence_count"] = len(existing_ids)
                else:
                    G.add_node(c.id, **_node_attrs_from_concept(c))
                    nodes_added += 1

            for r in new_relationships:
                if not (G.has_node(r.source_concept_id) and G.has_node(r.target_concept_id)):
                    continue
                if G.has_edge(r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id):
                    # Merge provenance into existing edge.
                    existing_ids = G.edges[r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id].get(
                        "source_document_ids", set()
                    )
                    existing_ids.add(document_id)
                    G.edges[r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id]["source_document_ids"] = existing_ids
                    G.edges[r.source_concept_id, r.target_concept_id]["evidence_count"] = len(existing_ids)
                else:
                    G.add_edge(
                        r.source_concept_id,
                        r.target_concept_id,
                        **_edge_attrs_from_relationship(r),
                    )
                    edges_added += 1

        self._bump_graph_version(db, workspace_id)
        logger.info(
            "[graph_memory] ws=%d doc=%d — incremental add: +%d nodes, +%d edges (%.0fms)",
            workspace_id, document_id, nodes_added, edges_added,
            (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,
        )

    # ── incremental remove ────────────────────────────────────────────

    def remove_document_contributions(self, workspace_id: int, document_id: int) -> None:
        """
        Remove a document's evidence from the workspace graph.

        Nodes and edges that still have other supporting documents are kept;
        only those whose entire evidence base was this document are removed.
        This is called by the documents API immediately before the DB delete.
        """
        G = self._store.get(workspace_id)
        if G is None:
            # Nothing cached — the next access will rebuild from updated SQL.
            return

        t0 = time.monotonic()
        build_lock = self._get_build_lock(workspace_id)
        with build_lock:
            # Remove document from edge provenance; collect edges to delete.
            edges_to_remove: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
            for src, tgt, data in list(G.edges(data=True)):
                doc_ids: set[int] = data.get("source_document_ids", set())
                doc_ids.discard(document_id)
                if not doc_ids:
                    edges_to_remove.append((src, tgt))
                else:
                    data["source_document_ids"] = doc_ids
                    data["evidence_count"] = len(doc_ids)

            for src, tgt in edges_to_remove:
                G.remove_edge(src, tgt)

            # Remove document from node provenance; collect nodes to delete.
            nodes_to_remove: list[int] = []
            for node_id, data in list(G.nodes(data=True)):
                doc_ids = data.get("source_document_ids", set())
                doc_ids.discard(document_id)
                if not doc_ids:
                    nodes_to_remove.append(node_id)
                else:
                    data["source_document_ids"] = doc_ids
                    data["evidence_count"] = len(doc_ids)

            for node_id in nodes_to_remove:
                G.remove_node(node_id)

        logger.info(
            "[graph_memory] ws=%d doc=%d removed: -%d nodes, -%d edges (%.0fms)",
            workspace_id, document_id, len(nodes_to_remove), len(edges_to_remove),
            (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,
        )

    # ── invalidate / rebuild ──────────────────────────────────────────

    def invalidate(self, workspace_id: int) -> None:
        """Evict the cached graph; next get_workspace_graph() will rebuild from SQL."""
        self._store.evict(workspace_id)
        logger.debug("[graph_memory] ws=%d evicted from cache.", workspace_id)

    def rebuild_workspace_graph(self, workspace_id: int, db: Session) -> nx.DiGraph:
        """Force a full SQL rebuild for one workspace, replacing the cached graph."""
        self._store.evict(workspace_id)
        return self._build_and_store(workspace_id, db)

    # ── internals ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _build_and_store(self, workspace_id: int, db: Session | None) -> nx.DiGraph:
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        own_session = db is None
        if own_session:
            db = SessionLocal()
        try:
            G = _build_provenance_graph(db, workspace_id)
            self._store.put(workspace_id, G)
            logger.info(
                "[graph_memory] ws=%d full build: %d nodes, %d edges (%.0fms)",
                workspace_id, G.number_of_nodes(), G.number_of_edges(),
                (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000,
            )
            return G
        finally:
            if own_session:
                db.close()

    def _get_build_lock(self, workspace_id: int) -> threading.Lock:
        with self._meta_lock:
            if workspace_id not in self._build_lock:
                self._build_lock[workspace_id] = threading.Lock()
            return self._build_lock[workspace_id]

    def _bump_graph_version(self, db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> None:
        """Increment graph_version and set graph_last_updated on the Workspace row."""
        try:
            ws = db.get(Workspace, workspace_id)
            if ws:
                ws.graph_version = (ws.graph_version or 0) + 1
                ws.graph_last_updated = datetime.utcnow()
                db.commit()
        except Exception:
            logger.exception(
                "[graph_memory] ws=%d — failed to bump graph_version.", workspace_id
            )


# Application-level singleton — shared across all threads.
graph_memory_manager = GraphMemoryManager()
