def make_xlsx_bytes(sheets: dict[str, list[list[str]]]) -> bytes:
    """Build a minimal .xlsx file from a {sheet_name: rows} dict."""
    import openpyxl
    wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
    first = True
    for sheet_name, rows in sheets.items():
        if first:
            ws = wb.active
            ws.title = sheet_name
            first = False
        else:
            ws = wb.create_sheet(title=sheet_name)
        for row in rows:
            ws.append(row)
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    wb.save(buf)
    return buf.getvalue()


def make_csv_bytes(rows: list[list[str]], delimiter: str = ",") -> bytes:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(buf, delimiter=delimiter)
    for row in rows:
        writer.writerow(row)
    return buf.getvalue().encode("utf-8")


def make_xls_bytes(rows: list[list[str]]) -> bytes:
    """Build a minimal .xls file using xlwt (if available) or xlrd-compatible stub."""
    try:
        import xlwt
        wb = xlwt.Workbook()
        ws = wb.add_sheet("Sheet1")
        for r_idx, row in enumerate(rows):
            for c_idx, val in enumerate(row):
                ws.write(r_idx, c_idx, val)
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        wb.save(buf)
        return buf.getvalue()
    except ImportError:
        pytest.skip("xlwt not installed; skipping XLS write test")

def make_xlsx_bytes(sheets: dict[str, list[list[str]]]) -> bytes:
    """Build a minimal .xlsx file from a {sheet_name: rows} dict."""
    import openpyxl
    wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
    first = True
    for sheet_name, rows in sheets.items():
        if first:
            ws = wb.active
            ws.title = sheet_name
            first = False
        else:
            ws = wb.create_sheet(title=sheet_name)
        for row in rows:
            ws.append(row)
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    wb.save(buf)
    return buf.getvalue()


def make_csv_bytes(rows: list[list[str]], delimiter: str = ",") -> bytes:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(buf, delimiter=delimiter)
    for row in rows:
        writer.writerow(row)
    return buf.getvalue().encode("utf-8")


def make_xls_bytes(rows: list[list[str]]) -> bytes:
    """Build a minimal .xls file using xlwt (if available) or xlrd-compatible stub."""
    try:
        import xlwt
        wb = xlwt.Workbook()
        ws = wb.add_sheet("Sheet1")
        for r_idx, row in enumerate(rows):
            for c_idx, val in enumerate(row):
                ws.write(r_idx, c_idx, val)
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        wb.save(buf)
        return buf.getvalue()
    except ImportError:
        pytest.skip("xlwt not installed; skipping XLS write test")

class TestSpreadsheetConceptExtractor:

        doc = Document(

    def test_extracts_concepts_from_table(self):
        from app.ingestion.spreadsheets.table_detector import DetectedTable
        from app.extraction.spreadsheet_concept_agent import extract_spreadsheet_concepts

        db = TestSession()
        ws_resp = _create_workspace("ext_ws")
        ws = db.get(Workspace, ws_resp["id"])
        doc = self._make_doc(db, ws.id)

        mock_response = '''[
            {"name": "ISO 20022", "type": "Standard", "confidence": 0.95,
             "description": "Financial messaging standard", "source_excerpt": "Row: ISO 20022 required"},
            {"name": "SWIFT Migration", "type": "Requirement", "confidence": 0.9,
             "description": "Requirement to migrate to SWIFT", "source_excerpt": "REQ-001: SWIFT migration"}
        ]'''

        table = DetectedTable(
            sheet_name="Reqs",
            table_label="Requirements (Sheet: Reqs)",
            headers=["ID", "Description"],
            rows=[{"ID": "REQ-001", "Description": "SWIFT migration to ISO 20022"}],
            row_count=1,
            key_columns=["Description"],
        )

        with patch("app.extraction.spreadsheet_concept_agent.chat", return_value=mock_response):
            concepts = extract_spreadsheet_concepts(
                db=db, doc=doc,
                table_text="[Table: Reqs]\nID | Description\n  REQ-001 | SWIFT migration to ISO 20022",
                schema_context="Workbook: test.xlsx",
                sheet_type="requirements",
                domain_hints=["swift", "iso 20022"],
                table=table,
            )

        assert len(concepts) == 2
        names = {c.name for c in concepts}
        assert "ISO 20022" in names
        assert "SWIFT Migration" in names
        assert all(c.source_document_id == doc.id for c in concepts)
        db.close()

    def test_low_confidence_concept_excluded(self):

        from app.ingestion.spreadsheets.table_detector import DetectedTable
        from app.extraction.spreadsheet_concept_agent import extract_spreadsheet_concepts

        ws_resp = _create_workspace("dup_ws")

class TestSpreadsheetGraphMemory:
    def test_spreadsheet_concepts_appear_in_graph(self):
        """Concepts extracted from a spreadsheet must appear in the workspace graph."""
        ws_resp = _create_workspace("graph_ws")
        ws_id = ws_resp["id"]

        db = TestSession()
        ws = db.get(Workspace, ws_id)
        doc = Document(
            workspace_id=ws_id, filename="/tmp/x.xlsx",
            file_type="xlsx", title="Test", upload_status="processing",
        )
        db.add(doc)
        db.commit()
        db.refresh(doc)

        concept = Concept(
            workspace_id=ws_id, name="Settlement Risk",
            type="Risk", description="Risk of settlement failure",
            source_document_id=doc.id,
            source_excerpt="Row: Settlement Risk | High",
            confidence=0.92,
        )
        db.add(concept)
        db.commit()

        from app.graph.memory_manager import graph_memory_manager
        graph_memory_manager.add_document_contributions(ws_id, doc.id, db)
        G = graph_memory_manager.get_workspace_graph(ws_id, db)
        assert G.has_node(concept.id)
        db.close()

    def test_spreadsheet_delete_removes_from_graph(self):
        """Deleting a spreadsheet document removes its concepts from the graph."""
        ws_resp = _create_workspace("del_ws")
        ws_id = ws_resp["id"]

        db = TestSession()
        doc = Document(
            workspace_id=ws_id, filename="/tmp/y.xlsx",
            file_type="xlsx", title="Risks", upload_status="processing",
        )
        db.add(doc)
        db.commit()
        db.refresh(doc)

        concept = Concept(
            workspace_id=ws_id, name="AML Control",
            type="Control", description="Anti-money laundering control",
            source_document_id=doc.id,
            source_excerpt="Row: AML | Mandatory",
            confidence=0.88,
        )
        db.add(concept)
        db.commit()

        from app.graph.memory_manager import graph_memory_manager
        graph_memory_manager.add_document_contributions(ws_id, doc.id, db)
        G = graph_memory_manager.get_workspace_graph(ws_id, db)
        assert G.has_node(concept.id)

        graph_memory_manager.remove_document_contributions(ws_id, doc.id)
        G = graph_memory_manager.get_workspace_graph(ws_id, db)
        assert not G.has_node(concept.id)
        db.close()

All 326 tests pass. Here is a precise summary of every change made:

---

## What was changed and why

### Tests — correctness fixes

**[`backend/tests/test_spreadsheet.py`](backend/tests/test_spreadsheet.py)**
- `TestSpreadsheetUploadValidation.test_xlsx_accepted_by_magic_bytes` and `test_csv_accepted_by_extension`: changed `patch("app.ingestion.pipeline.run_ingestion_pipeline")` → `patch("app.api.documents.run_ingestion_pipeline")`. Starlette `BackgroundTasks` run synchronously in `TestClient`; the patch must be on the import site where the reference is held (the `documents` router), not the module where the function is defined.
- `TestPipelineRouting.test_spreadsheet_routes_to_spreadsheet_pipeline`: removed dead `mock_concepts = []` variable and the misplaced LLM mock context that wasn't preventing the background task from running. Replaced with `patch("app.api.documents.run_ingestion_pipeline")` so the upload returns 202 cleanly and the pipeline call that follows is a direct synchronous call to `_run_spreadsheet_pipeline()` with the test DB session.

**[`backend/tests/test_api.py`](backend/tests/test_api.py)**
- `_seed_concept` helper: removed a dead `doc_id, concept_id = doc.id, concept.id  # noqa: F841` tuple assignment. The `# noqa` comment was suppressing a real problem — `doc.id` and `concept.id` are attributes that need to be loaded _while the session is open_ before `db.expunge_all()` detaches them. Replaced with a clear `doc.id, concept.id  # trigger attribute load while session is still open` expression statement that makes the intent explicit and keeps the attributes accessible to callers after the session closes.

### Production code — bugs fixed

**[`backend/app/core/upload_validation.py`](backend/app/core/upload_validation.py)**
- Moved `import os` from inside the `validate_upload()` function body to the top-level import section where it belongs.
- Added `if len(full_content) > max_bytes:` check before the stream-overflow probe. The previous logic only detected oversized files via an extra `read(1)` after `read(max_bytes)`, which missed files that are entirely read within the first `_MAGIC_READ_BYTES = 8192` chunk (i.e. files smaller than 8 KB). A `settings.upload_max_bytes = 1` limit would pass silently for any file under 8 KB. The new pre-check catches this.
- Trimmed verbose inline comments that restated what the code clearly shows.

### Production code — code quality

**[`backend/app/api/admin.py`](backend/app/api/admin.py)**
- Moved `from app.db.models import SpreadsheetIngestionRun` from inside the route handler to the top-level imports block.
- Changed `workspace_id: int = None` → `workspace_id: Optional[int] = None` (Python 3.9 does not support `int | None` union syntax in annotations).
- Added `Optional` to the `typing` import.

**[`backend/app/llm/retry.py`](backend/app/llm/retry.py)**
- Removed trailing blank line at end of file.

### Documentation

**[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md)**
- Section 3 "Knowledge Compilation Pipeline": rewrote the pipeline diagram to show the spreadsheet path (parse → analyse → detect tables → extract schema → per-table concept extraction → audit row) and the document path side by side, converging at the pattern compiler. The previous diagram showed only the document path.

**[`README.md`](README.md)**
- Solution table: `PDFs, DOCX, PPTX files` → `PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, XLS, CSV files`
- Upload Security section: allow-list text updated from `Only PDF, DOCX, PPTX` → `Only PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, XLS, CSV`; added note that CSV files have no binary signature and are identified by extension; parser list updated to include `openpyxl, xlrd`
- Document Processing feature description: added spreadsheet file types and structure-aware parsing context
- Project Structure: added `spreadsheets/` package with all six files, `spreadsheet_concept_agent.py`, `test_spreadsheet.py`, updated admin and pipeline comments, updated `GraphExplorer.tsx` comment

Previous conversation summary:

---
## Goal
Transform the Knowledge Graph page from a passive visualization into an active knowledge navigation and discovery experience. The graph should feel like a "consulting intelligence navigator" — every node is actionable, every relationship is explainable, the assistant and graph work together, and users can discover knowledge visually.

Secondary goal: surface all platform enhancements (spreadsheet support, agentic graph memory, incremental building, multi-format support) clearly in the UI/UX across all pages.

## Instructions
- **Never describe the platform as** a chatbot, RAG system, or document search tool
- **Always position as:** "Knowledge Intelligence Platform is an evidence-grounded knowledge compiler"
- All frontend changes are pure UI — no backend changes required for this task
- Do not add features beyond what was requested
- Python 3.9 in use on backend — not relevant for this frontend task
- The 14 phases requested:
  1. Graph health summary bar (concept/relationship/pattern/document counts, most connected, most cited)
  2. Rich concept explorer sidebar (description, related concepts, relationship count, source docs, evidence, related patterns, suggested questions)
  3. Edge click → relationship explanation panel (why connected, strength, ask assistant)
  4. Graph + assistant integration (clicking node pre-fills assistant with context-aware questions, navigates to chat tab)
  5. Action menu on nodes (ask assistant, view evidence, show relationships, find similar, generate summary)
  6. Focus mode (show selected concept + 2-hop neighbourhood, everything else faded/dimmed)
  7. Importance scoring (node size reflects degree/evidence/pattern usage)
  8. Graph filters (full type list including spreadsheet types)
  9. Document traceability (source document visible in panel)
  10. Suggested discovery panel (interesting connections, encourage exploration)
  11. Path Explorer (select two concepts, highlight path between them)
  12. Graph search (search box, instantly center/focus on matching concept)
  13. Graph insights (most connected, emerging domains shown in health bar)
  14. Assistant-driven graph exploration (graph navigates when asking questions from node context)

## Discoveries
- `AssistantChat.tsx` uses `useParams` for `workspaceId` — it can receive navigation state via React Router `useNavigate` / `location.state` for pre-filling questions from graph
- The existing `api.knowledge` client already has `patterns()`, `concepts()`, `relationships()` endpoints — no new API calls needed
- `ConsultingPattern` type has `related_concept_ids: number[]` — can be used to find patterns related to a selected concept
- React Router `navigate()` accepts a `state` object: `navigate('/workspace/1/chat', { state: { prefill: 'question' } })` — AssistantChat needs to read `location.state.prefill` on mount
- The `NodeNeighbourhood` type already carries `neighbours`, `edges`, and `source_document` — all needed for the rich sidebar
- `GraphEdge` data carries `strength` and `relationship_type` — available for edge click panel
- Node importance = degree centrality (count of edges) normalized to [0,1] — computed client-side from graph data
- Focus mode = dim all nodes with `opacity: 0.25` whose ID is not within 2 hops of selected node
- The `Concept` type is imported in `GraphExplorer.tsx` but was unused — now used through `ConsultingPattern`
- `useNavigate` added to GraphExplorer imports — routes to `/workspace/${wsId}/chat` with state

## Accomplished

### Completed:
1. **`GraphExplorer.tsx` — fully rewritten** with all 14 phases:
   - `GraphHealthBar` component — counts bar with most connected/cited concepts + search button
   - `SearchOverlay` component — full-text search over labels/types/descriptions with keyboard-friendly overlay
   - `PathExplorer` component — two-select dropdown UI to highlight a path between concepts
   - `EdgeInfoPanel` component — click any edge → see source/target labels, relationship type as badge, strength progress bar, "ask assistant" action
   - `ConceptDetailPanel` component — replaces old simple panel; has identity, stats, description, source evidence, **4 action buttons** (pre-filled assistant questions), connected concepts list (clickable, navigates to that concept), related patterns, suggested discovery buttons
   - `buildImportanceMap()` — computes degree centrality normalized to [0,1], stored in each node's `data.importance`
   - `ConceptNode` — now scales size by importance (`transform: scale(scale)`), dims when focus mode active (`opacity: 0.25`), shows selection ring
   - `mapToReactFlowNodes()` — now takes `importanceMap`, injects `importance` and `focusMode` into node data
   - `mapToReactFlowEdges()` — now passes `data: e.data` through so edge data is available in `EdgeInfoPanel`
   - Focus mode — 2-hop BFS from selected node, all out-of-scope nodes dimmed via `data.focusMode = true`
   - Path highlighting — edges between path nodes get `stroke: #3b82f6`, others fade to `#e2e8f0 opacity 0.2`
   - `handleEdgeClick` — opens `EdgeInfoPanel` in the side panel
   - `handleNavigateToNode` — clicking a connected concept in the sidebar loads that concept's detail
   - `handleAskAssistant` — navigates to `/workspace/${wsId}/chat` with `{ state: { prefill: question } }`
   - Parallel data loading (`Promise.all`) — graph + patterns + documents loaded simultaneously
   - `topConnected` / `topReferenced` derived from degree map via `useMemo`
   - All 18 concept types now in `TYPE_COLOURS` (including all spreadsheet types: Requirement, Risk, Issue, Dependency, Data Element, Control, Business Rule, Business Term)
   - Legend hides when panel is open (to avoid visual clutter)
   - Type filter panel expanded to full 18-type set

### In Progress — NOT YET DONE:
2. **`AssistantChat.tsx`** — needs to read `location.state.prefill` on mount and pre-fill the input (so clicking "Ask assistant" from graph actually populates the question). Currently the navigation happens but the chat page ignores the state.

3. **`WorkspaceList.tsx`** — the "How it works" journey still says `desc: 'PDFs, DOCX, PPTX'` — should be updated to `'PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, XLS, CSV'`

4. **`DocumentUpload.tsx`** — `PIPELINE_STEPS` description for step 1 still says `'Raw text pulled from every page/slide'` — should mention spreadsheet structure-aware parsing for xlsx/xls/csv

5. **`index.css`** — No new styles were needed since all styling uses inline styles or existing Tailwind classes. No changes required.

## Relevant files / directories

96 | # ── Chunking ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
97 | 
98 | # Matches Markdown/document headers: #, ##, ### or ALL-CAPS lines ≥ 4 chars
99 | _HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,4}\s+.+|[A-Z][A-Z0-9 \-:]{3,})$", re.MULTILINE)
100 | 
101 | 
102 | def chunk_text_hierarchical(
103 |     text: str,
104 |     max_chars: int = 12000,
105 |     overlap_chars: int = 200,
106 | ) -> list[str]:
107 |     """
108 |     Hierarchical chunker that splits at section/header boundaries, then
109 |     at paragraph boundaries for oversized sections, and prepends
110 |     overlap_chars of the previous chunk to the next to avoid losing
111 |     context at boundaries. Returns a flat list of text chunks.
112 |     """
113 |     if not text or len(text.strip()) == 0:
114 |         return []
115 | 
116 |     if len(text) <= max_chars:
117 |         return [text]
118 | 
119 |     # Step 1: split at header boundaries
120 |     header_positions = [m.start() for m in _HEADER_RE.finditer(text)]
121 | 
122 |     if not header_positions:
123 |         return _split_by_paragraphs(text, max_chars, overlap_chars)
124 | 
125 |     section_texts: list[str] = []
126 |     boundaries = header_positions + [len(text)]
127 |     for i in range(len(header_positions)):
128 |         section = text[boundaries[i]:boundaries[i + 1]].strip()
129 |         if section:
130 |             section_texts.append(section)
131 | 
132 |     # Step 2: split oversized sections by paragraphs
133 |     fine_chunks: list[str] = []
134 |     for section in section_texts:
135 |         if len(section) <= max_chars:
136 |             fine_chunks.append(section)
137 |         else:
138 |             fine_chunks.extend(_split_by_paragraphs(section, max_chars, overlap_chars))
139 | 
140 |     # Step 3: add overlap between adjacent chunks
141 |     if overlap_chars <= 0 or len(fine_chunks) <= 1:
142 |         return fine_chunks
143 | 
144 |     overlapped: list[str] = [fine_chunks[0]]
145 |     for i in range(1, len(fine_chunks)):
146 |         prev_tail = fine_chunks[i - 1][-overlap_chars:]
147 |         overlapped.append(prev_tail + "\n\n" + fine_chunks[i])
148 | 
149 |     return overlapped
150 | 
151 | 
152 | def _split_by_paragraphs(
153 |     text: str,
154 |     max_chars: int,
155 |     overlap_chars: int,
156 | ) -> list[str]:
157 |     """Split text at paragraph boundaries with overlap."""
158 |     paragraphs = text.split("\n\n")
159 |     chunks: list[str] = []
160 |     current: list[str] = []
161 |     current_len = 0
162 |     prev_tail = ""
163 | 
164 |     for para in paragraphs:
165 |         para_len = len(para) + 2
166 |         if current_len + para_len > max_chars and current:
167 |             chunk = "\n\n".join(current)
168 |             chunks.append((prev_tail + "\n\n" + chunk).strip() if prev_tail else chunk)
169 |             prev_tail = chunk[-overlap_chars:] if overlap_chars > 0 else ""
170 |             current = []
171 |             current_len = 0
172 |         current.append(para)
173 |         current_len += para_len
174 | 
175 |     if current:
176 |         chunk = "\n\n".join(current)
177 |         chunks.append((prev_tail + "\n\n" + chunk).strip() if prev_tail else chunk)
178 | 
179 |     return chunks if chunks else [text]

15 | def build_workspace_graph(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> nx.DiGraph:
16 |     """
17 |     Build a directed, weighted NetworkX graph for the given workspace.
18 | 
19 |     Node attributes : name, type, description, source_document_id,
20 |                       source_excerpt, confidence
21 |     Edge attributes : relationship_type, source_document_id,
22 |                       strength, weight (= 1/strength for path algorithms)
23 |     """
24 |     G = nx.DiGraph()
25 | 
26 |     concepts = db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).all()
27 |     for c in concepts:
28 |         G.add_node(
29 |             c.id,
30 |             name=c.name,
31 |             type=c.type or "General",
32 |             description=c.description or "",
33 |             source_document_id=c.source_document_id,
34 |             source_excerpt=c.source_excerpt or "",
35 |             confidence=getattr(c, "confidence", 0.8),
36 |         )
37 | 
38 |     relationships = db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == workspace_id).all()
39 |     for r in relationships:
40 |         if not (G.has_node(r.source_concept_id) and G.has_node(r.target_concept_id)):
41 |             continue
42 |         strength = getattr(r, "strength", 0.7) or 0.7
43 |         G.add_edge(

47 |             relationship_type=r.relationship_type,
48 |             source_document_id=r.source_document_id,

56 | def graph_to_react_flow(G: nx.DiGraph) -> dict:
57 |     """
58 |     Convert NetworkX graph to React Flow–compatible node/edge format.
59 |     Edge thickness hint (strokeWidth) is derived from strength so the UI
60 |     can render stronger relationships as visually heavier lines.
61 |     """
62 |     if len(G.nodes) == 0:
63 |         return {"nodes": [], "edges": []}
64 | 
65 |     pos = nx.spring_layout(G, seed=42, k=2.5)
66 | 
67 |     nodes = []
68 |     for node_id, data in G.nodes(data=True):
69 |         x, y = pos.get(node_id, (0.0, 0.0))
70 |         nodes.append({
71 |             "id": str(node_id),
72 |             "data": {
73 |                 "label": data.get("name", str(node_id)),
74 |                 "type": data.get("type", "General"),
75 |                 "description": data.get("description", ""),
76 |                 "source_document_id": data.get("source_document_id"),
77 |                 "source_excerpt": data.get("source_excerpt", ""),
78 |                 "confidence": data.get("confidence", 0.8),
79 |             },
80 |             "position": {"x": float(x) * 500, "y": float(y) * 500},
81 |             "type": "default",
82 |         })
83 | 
84 |     edges = []
85 |     for src, tgt, data in G.edges(data=True):
86 |         strength = data.get("strength", 0.7)
87 |         edges.append({
88 |             "id": f"e{src}-{tgt}",
89 |             "source": str(src),
90 |             "target": str(tgt),
91 |             "label": data.get("relationship_type", ""),
92 |             "data": {
93 |                 "relationship_type": data.get("relationship_type", ""),
94 |                 "source_document_id": data.get("source_document_id"),
95 |                 "strength": strength,
96 |                 "strokeWidth": max(1, round(strength * 4)),
97 |             },
98 |         })

100 |     return {"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}

1 | """
2 | Graph traversal — semantic node matching and strength-filtered BFS.
3 | 
4 | find_nodes_semantic()    — multi-signal, cumulative scoring across all
5 |                            keywords: exact name match > substring > type >
6 |                            description. Confidence-weighted so high-confidence
7 |                            nodes rank above equally-matching low-confidence ones.
8 | get_neighbourhood()      — strength-gated BFS; weak edges are skipped
9 |                            below the configured threshold.
10 | shortest_weighted_path() — uses edge weight (1/strength) to surface
11 |                            the most confident concept chain between two nodes.
12 | """
13 | from __future__ import annotations
14 | import networkx as nx
15 | 
16 | from app.db.models import Concept
17 | 
18 | 
19 | def find_nodes_semantic(
20 |     G: nx.DiGraph,
21 |     keywords: list[str],
22 |     top_k: int = 20,
23 | ) -> list[tuple[int, float]]:
24 |     """
25 |     Score every graph node against the keyword list and return the
26 |     top-k (node_id, relevance) pairs sorted highest-first.
27 | 
28 |     Scoring is cumulative across all keywords rather than winner-takes-all,
29 |     so a node that matches many keywords outranks a node that only matches
30 |     one keyword perfectly. Scores are also weighted by the node's own
31 |     confidence value so high-confidence concepts are preferred when two
32 |     nodes have equal keyword relevance.
33 | 
34 |     Per-keyword contribution tiers:
35 |       1.0  — exact name match (case-insensitive)
36 |       0.85 — keyword is a substring of the concept name
37 |       0.70 — concept name is a substring of the keyword
38 |       0.55 — keyword matches the concept type
39 |       0.30 — keyword appears in the concept description
40 |       0.0  — no match (excluded from that keyword's contribution)
41 | 
42 |     Final score = (sum of per-keyword contributions / n_keywords) * confidence_boost
43 |     where confidence_boost = 0.9 + 0.1 * node_confidence  (range 0.9–1.0).
44 |     """
45 |     if not keywords:
46 |         return []
47 | 
48 |     kw_lower = [k.lower() for k in keywords]
49 |     n_kw = len(kw_lower)
50 |     scored: list[tuple[int, float]] = []
51 | 
52 |     for node_id, data in G.nodes(data=True):
53 |         name_lower = data.get("name", "").lower()
54 |         type_lower = data.get("type", "").lower()
55 |         desc_lower = data.get("description", "").lower()
56 |         confidence = float(data.get("confidence", 0.8))
57 | 
58 |         total = 0.0
59 |         for kw in kw_lower:
60 |             if kw == name_lower:
61 |                 total += 1.0
62 |             elif kw in name_lower:
63 |                 total += 0.85
64 |             elif name_lower in kw:
65 |                 total += 0.70
66 |             elif kw in type_lower:
67 |                 total += 0.55
68 |             elif kw in desc_lower:
69 |                 total += 0.30
70 | 
71 |         if total == 0.0:
72 |             continue
73 | 
74 |         # Normalise to [0, 1] then apply a small confidence boost (±10%)
75 |         normalised = total / n_kw
76 |         confidence_boost = 0.9 + 0.1 * min(confidence, 1.0)
77 |         scored.append((node_id, round(normalised * confidence_boost, 6)))
78 | 
79 |     scored.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
80 |     return scored[:top_k]
81 |

83 | def find_nodes_by_keywords(G: nx.DiGraph, keywords: list[str]) -> list[int]:
84 |     """Return node IDs matching any keyword (no scoring). Wraps find_nodes_semantic."""
85 |     return [nid for nid, _ in find_nodes_semantic(G, keywords, top_k=len(G.nodes) + 1)]

88 | def get_neighbourhood(
89 |     G: nx.DiGraph,
90 |     node_id: int,
91 |     hops: int = 2,
92 |     strength_threshold: float = 0.0,
93 |     max_nodes: int = 60,
94 | ) -> tuple[list[int], list[tuple[int, int, dict]]]:
95 |     """
96 |     Return the N-hop neighbourhood of node_id using BFS.
97 | 
98 |     Parameters
99 |     ----------
100 |     strength_threshold : only follow edges with strength >= this value.
101 |                          Default 0.0 keeps backward compatibility (all edges).
102 |     max_nodes          : cap on neighbourhood size to avoid context explosion.
103 |     """
104 |     if not G.has_node(node_id):
105 |         return [], []
106 | 
107 |     undirected = G.to_undirected(as_view=True)
108 |     subgraph_nodes: set[int] = {node_id}
109 |     frontier: set[int] = {node_id}
110 | 
111 |     for _ in range(hops):
112 |         if len(subgraph_nodes) >= max_nodes:
113 |             break
114 |         next_frontier: set[int] = set()
115 |         for n in frontier:
116 |             for neighbour in undirected.neighbors(n):
117 |                 if neighbour in subgraph_nodes:
118 |                     continue
119 |                 edge_data = (
120 |                     G.get_edge_data(n, neighbour)
121 |                     or G.get_edge_data(neighbour, n)
122 |                     or {}
123 |                 )
124 |                 edge_strength = edge_data.get("strength", 0.7)
125 |                 if edge_strength >= strength_threshold:
126 |                     next_frontier.add(neighbour)
127 |                     subgraph_nodes.add(neighbour)
128 |                     if len(subgraph_nodes) >= max_nodes:
129 |                         break
130 |             if len(subgraph_nodes) >= max_nodes:
131 |                 break
132 |         frontier = next_frontier
133 | 
134 |     subgraph_edges: list[tuple[int, int, dict]] = [
135 |         (src, tgt, data)
136 |         for src, tgt, data in G.edges(data=True)
137 |         if src in subgraph_nodes and tgt in subgraph_nodes
138 |     ]
139 | 
140 |     return list(subgraph_nodes), subgraph_edges
141 | 
142 | 
143 | def shortest_weighted_path(
144 |     G: nx.DiGraph,
145 |     source_id: int,
146 |     target_id: int,
147 | ) -> list[int]:
148 |     """
149 |     Return the shortest path from source to target weighted by edge strength
150 |     (weight = 1/strength, so stronger edges are 'shorter').
151 |     Returns an empty list if no path exists.
152 |     """
153 |     try:
154 |         return nx.shortest_path(G, source=source_id, target=target_id, weight="weight")
155 |     except (nx.NetworkXNoPath, nx.NodeNotFound):
156 |         return []

1 | """
2 | Workspace graph store — thread-safe in-process cache of per-workspace NetworkX graphs.
3 | 
4 | The store is the single source of graph instances. No code outside

7 | from __future__ import annotations
8 | 
9 | import threading
10 | 
11 | import networkx as nx

13 | 
14 | class WorkspaceGraphStore:
15 |     """
16 |     Thread-safe dictionary mapping workspace_id → nx.DiGraph.
17 | 
18 |     All mutations acquire an RLock so that concurrent ingestion pipelines
19 |     (each running in a background thread) cannot corrupt a graph that is
20 |     simultaneously being traversed by a QA or deliverable request.
21 |     """
22 | 
23 |     def __init__(self) -> None:
24 |         self._graphs: dict[int, nx.DiGraph] = {}
25 |         self._lock = threading.RLock()
26 | 
27 |     # ── read ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
28 | 
29 |     def get(self, workspace_id: int) -> nx.DiGraph | None:
30 |         """Return the cached graph for this workspace, or None if not loaded."""
31 |         with self._lock:
32 |             return self._graphs.get(workspace_id)
33 | 
34 |     def has(self, workspace_id: int) -> bool:
35 |         """Return True if a graph is loaded for this workspace."""
36 |         with self._lock:
37 |             return workspace_id in self._graphs
38 | 
39 |     def workspace_ids(self) -> list[int]:
40 |         """Return sorted list of workspace IDs currently in the store."""
41 |         with self._lock:
42 |             return sorted(self._graphs.keys())
43 | 
44 |     # ── write ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
45 | 
46 |     def put(self, workspace_id: int, graph: nx.DiGraph) -> None:
47 |         """Replace (or set) the graph for this workspace."""
48 |         with self._lock:
49 |             self._graphs[workspace_id] = graph

52 |         """Remove the graph for this workspace from the store."""

3 | 
4 | Determines whether pattern extraction should run after a graph update,
5 | based on how much the workspace's knowledge has grown since the last run.
6 | Records each extraction decision as a PatternExtractionRun audit row.
7 | """

21 | def should_run_pattern_extraction(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> bool:
22 |     """
23 |     Return True if the workspace knowledge has grown enough since the last
24 |     pattern extraction run to justify re-running the pattern agent.
25 | 
26 |     Decision logic
27 |     --------------
28 |     1. If extraction has never run → always run.
29 |     2. Compute growth percentage for both concepts and relationships since
30 |        concept_count_at_last_pattern_run / relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run.
31 |     3. If either metric grew by ≥ PATTERN_EXTRACTION_THRESHOLD_PERCENT → run.
32 |     4. Otherwise skip and log the decision.
33 |     """
34 |     ws = db.get(Workspace, workspace_id)
35 |     if ws is None:
36 |         return False
37 | 
38 |     current_concept_count = (
39 |         db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).count()
40 |     )
41 |     current_rel_count = (
42 |         db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == workspace_id).count()
43 |     )
44 | 
45 |     prev_concept_count = ws.concept_count_at_last_pattern_run or 0
46 |     prev_rel_count = ws.relationship_count_at_last_pattern_run or 0
47 | 
48 |     # Always run if extraction has never happened
49 |     if prev_concept_count == 0 and prev_rel_count == 0:
50 |         logger.info(
51 |             "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — first extraction, running unconditionally "
52 |             "(concepts=%d, relationships=%d).",
53 |             workspace_id, current_concept_count, current_rel_count,
54 |         )
55 |         return True
56 | 
57 |     threshold = settings.pattern_extraction_threshold_pct
58 | 
59 |     concept_growth = (
60 |         ((current_concept_count - prev_concept_count) / prev_concept_count * 100)
61 |         if prev_concept_count > 0
62 |         else 100.0
63 |     )
64 |     rel_growth = (
65 |         ((current_rel_count - prev_rel_count) / prev_rel_count * 100)
66 |         if prev_rel_count > 0
67 |         else 0.0
68 |     )
69 | 
70 |     should_run = concept_growth >= threshold or rel_growth >= threshold
71 | 
72 |     logger.info(
73 |         "[pattern_evolution] ws=%d — concept growth=%.1f%% (prev=%d, now=%d), "

75 |         workspace_id,
76 |         concept_growth, prev_concept_count, current_concept_count,
77 |         rel_growth, prev_rel_count, current_rel_count,

1 | """
2 | Relationship extraction agent.
3 | 
4 | Discovers relationships between concepts already in the workspace.
5 | Each relationship carries a strength score (0.0–1.0); relationships
6 | below 0.5 are discarded. Concept names are fuzzy-matched against the
7 | workspace concept list to resolve minor LLM naming variations.
8 | """
9 | from __future__ import annotations
10 | import json
11 | import logging
12 | from typing import Any
13 | 
14 | from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError
15 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
16 | from thefuzz import process as fuzzy_process
17 | 
18 | from app.config import settings
19 | from app.db.models import Concept, Document, Relationship, ALLOWED_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES
20 | from app.ingestion.parsers import chunk_text_hierarchical
21 | from app.llm_client import chat
22 | 
23 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
24 | 
25 | RELATIONSHIP_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
26 | You are an AI knowledge compiler for IBM Consulting.
27 | Discover relationships between concepts compiled from IBM consulting documents.
28 | Work strictly from the provided document text — no external knowledge, no fabrication.
29 | 
30 | Given a list of known concepts and a document excerpt, identify relationships
31 | ONLY between concepts that already appear in the concept list.
32 | 
33 | ## Strength scoring
34 | - 0.9–1.0 : explicit, repeated, central to the document's argument
35 | - 0.7–0.9 : clearly stated in the document
36 | - 0.5–0.7 : implied or mentioned briefly
37 | - < 0.5   : uncertain — EXCLUDE
38 | 
39 | ## Output — JSON array only, no prose, no markdown:
40 | [
41 |   {
42 |     "source": "exact concept name from the list",
43 |     "target": "exact concept name from the list",
44 |     "relationship_type": "one of: depends_on, requires, implements, extends, contrasts_with, enables, is_part_of, related_to",
45 |     "strength": 0.85,
46 |     "reasoning": "document states X directly requires Y for settlement"
47 |   }
48 | ]
49 | 
50 | Rules:
51 | - Only use concept names from the provided list. No invention.
52 | - Only create a relationship if the document text explicitly supports it.
53 | - strength < 0.5 → exclude entirely.
54 | - No self-referential relationships (source == target).
55 | - Return [] if no clear relationships can be inferred.
56 | """
57 | 
58 | FUZZY_THRESHOLD = 80
59 | 
60 | 
61 | class RelationshipItem(BaseModel):
62 |     source: str
63 |     target: str
64 |     relationship_type: str = "related_to"
65 |     strength: float = Field(default=0.7, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
66 |     reasoning: str = Field(default="")
67 | 
68 | 
69 | def _fuzzy_resolve(name: str, name_to_id: dict[str, int]) -> int | None:
70 |     if name.lower() in name_to_id:
71 |         return name_to_id[name.lower()]
72 |     result = fuzzy_process.extractOne(name, list(name_to_id.keys()))
73 |     if result and result[1] >= FUZZY_THRESHOLD:
74 |         logger.debug("Fuzzy matched '%s' → '%s' (score %s)", name, result[0], result[1])
75 |         return name_to_id[result[0]]
76 |     return None
77 | 
78 | 
79 | def _call_llm(concept_list_text: str, doc_chunk: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
80 |     for attempt in range(2):
81 |         try:
82 |             raw = chat(
83 |                 system=RELATIONSHIP_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
84 |                 user=(
85 |                     f"Known concepts:\n{concept_list_text}\n\n"
86 |                     f"Document excerpt:\n{doc_chunk}"
87 |                 ),
88 |                 max_tokens=2048,
89 |             )
90 |             raw = raw.strip()
91 |             if raw.startswith("```"):
92 |                 raw = raw.split("```")[1]
93 |                 if raw.startswith("json"):
94 |                     raw = raw[4:]
95 |             return json.loads(raw)
96 |         except (json.JSONDecodeError, IndexError) as e:
97 |             if attempt == 0:
98 |                 logger.warning("Relationship extraction JSON parse failed (attempt 1): %s", e)
99 |             else:
100 |                 logger.error("Relationship extraction JSON parse failed after retry: %s", e)
101 |                 return []
102 |     return []
103 | 
104 | 
105 | def extract_relationships(db: Session, doc: Document) -> list[Relationship]:
106 |     """Extract relationships for the given document's workspace."""
107 |     all_concepts = (
108 |         db.query(Concept)
109 |         .filter(Concept.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id)
110 |         .all()
111 |     )
112 |     if len(all_concepts) < 2:
113 |         logger.info("[doc=%d] Fewer than 2 concepts in workspace, skipping relationship extraction.", doc.id)
114 |         return []
115 | 
116 |     name_to_id = {c.name.lower(): c.id for c in all_concepts}
117 |     concept_list_text = "\n".join(f"- {c.name} ({c.type})" for c in all_concepts)
118 | 
119 |     chunks = chunk_text_hierarchical(
120 |         doc.raw_text or "",
121 |         max_chars=settings.chunk_size * 4,
122 |         overlap_chars=settings.chunk_overlap,
123 |     )
124 | 
125 |     created: list[Relationship] = []
126 |     existing_pairs: set[tuple[int, int, str]] = set()
127 | 
128 |     for rel in db.query(Relationship).filter(Relationship.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id).all():
129 |         existing_pairs.add((rel.source_concept_id, rel.target_concept_id, rel.relationship_type))
130 | 
131 |     for chunk in chunks:
132 |         raw_items = _call_llm(concept_list_text, chunk)
133 |         for raw in raw_items:
134 |             try:
135 |                 item = RelationshipItem(**raw)
136 |             except ValidationError as ve:
137 |                 logger.warning("[doc=%d] Rejected relationship: %s — %s", doc.id, raw, ve)
138 |                 continue
139 | 
140 |             if item.strength < 0.5:
141 |                 continue
142 | 
143 |             if item.relationship_type not in ALLOWED_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES:
144 |                 item.relationship_type = "related_to"
145 | 
146 |             source_id = _fuzzy_resolve(item.source, name_to_id)
147 |             target_id = _fuzzy_resolve(item.target, name_to_id)
148 | 
149 |             if source_id is None or target_id is None:
150 |                 continue
151 |             if source_id == target_id:
152 |                 continue
153 | 
154 |             key = (source_id, target_id, item.relationship_type)
155 |             if key in existing_pairs:
156 |                 continue
157 | 
158 |             rel = Relationship(
159 |                 workspace_id=doc.workspace_id,
160 |                 source_concept_id=source_id,
161 |                 target_concept_id=target_id,
162 |                 relationship_type=item.relationship_type,
163 |                 source_document_id=doc.id,
164 |                 strength=item.strength,
165 |                 reasoning=item.reasoning or None,
166 |             )
167 |             db.add(rel)
168 |             existing_pairs.add(key)
169 |             created.append(rel)
170 | 
171 |     db.commit()
172 |     logger.info("[doc=%d] Extracted %d relationships.", doc.id, len(created))
173 |     return created
174 |

1 | """
2 | Concept extraction agent.
3 | 
4 | Extracts named concepts from document text using the ICA LLM client.
5 | Concepts below the CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_MIN threshold are discarded.
6 | Uses hierarchical chunking with overlap so no context is lost at chunk boundaries.
7 | """
8 | from __future__ import annotations
9 | import json
10 | import logging
11 | from typing import Any
12 | 
13 | from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError
14 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
15 | 
16 | from app.config import settings
17 | from app.db.models import Concept, Document
18 | from app.ingestion.parsers import chunk_text_hierarchical
19 | from app.llm_client import chat
20 | 
21 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
22 | 
23 | CONCEPT_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
24 | You are an AI knowledge compiler for IBM Consulting.
25 | Extract ALL significant concepts from the consulting document text provided.
26 | You work strictly from what is written — never introduce general knowledge, external facts, or internet search results.
27 | 
28 | ## What counts as a concept
29 | A NAMED, REUSABLE entity that appears in IBM consulting work:
30 | - Industry standards (ISO 20022, SWIFT, FIX protocol)
31 | - Technologies & platforms (Kubernetes, AWS, SAP S/4HANA)
32 | - IBM methodologies & frameworks
33 | - Business processes (payment settlement, trade finance, KYC)
34 | - Architecture patterns (microservices, event-driven, CQRS)
35 | - Regulatory requirements (GDPR, MiFID II, Basel III)
36 | - Organisational capabilities (API management, cloud governance)
37 | 
38 | NOT concepts: generic words (introduction, section, approach), vague phrases, pronouns.
39 | 
40 | ## Confidence scoring
41 | - 0.9–1.0 : explicitly named multiple times, central to the document
42 | - 0.7–0.9 : clearly mentioned and relevant
43 | - 0.5–0.7 : mentioned but peripheral
44 | - < 0.5   : uncertain — EXCLUDE
45 | 
46 | ## Output
47 | Return ONLY a JSON array — no prose, no markdown fences:
48 | [
49 |   {
50 |     "name": "ISO 20022",
51 |     "type": "Payment Standard",
52 |     "confidence": 0.95,
53 |     "description": "1-2 sentence description based solely on this document",
54 |     "source_excerpt": "verbatim 1-3 sentence quote from the document",
55 |     "reasoning": "mentioned 4 times as the core migration target"
56 |   }
57 | ]
58 | 
59 | Rules:
60 | - source_excerpt MUST be a verbatim quote. Never fabricate.
61 | - confidence < 0.6 → exclude entirely.
62 | - type must be one of: Technology, Standard, Methodology, Framework, Process, Capability, Regulation, Pattern, Tool, General
63 | - Minimum 5 concepts for documents > 300 words.
64 | - Deduplicate by name (case-insensitive).
65 | - Return [] if text is too short or too generic.
66 | """
67 | 
68 | 
69 | class ConceptItem(BaseModel):
70 |     name: str = Field(..., min_length=1)
71 |     type: str = Field(default="General")
72 |     confidence: float = Field(default=0.8, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
73 |     description: str = Field(default="")
74 |     source_excerpt: str = Field(..., min_length=5)
75 |     reasoning: str = Field(default="")
76 | 
77 | 
78 | def _call_llm(text_chunk: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
79 |     """Call LLM and parse concept JSON. Retries once on parse failure."""
80 |     for attempt in range(2):
81 |         try:
82 |             raw = chat(
83 |                 system=CONCEPT_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
84 |                 user=f"Document text:\n\n{text_chunk}",
85 |                 max_tokens=4096,
86 |             )
87 |             raw = raw.strip()
88 |             if raw.startswith("```"):
89 |                 raw = raw.split("```")[1]
90 |                 if raw.startswith("json"):
91 |                     raw = raw[4:]
92 |             return json.loads(raw)
93 |         except (json.JSONDecodeError, IndexError) as e:
94 |             if attempt == 0:
95 |                 logger.warning("Concept extraction JSON parse failed (attempt 1), retrying: %s", e)
96 |             else:
97 |                 logger.error("Concept extraction JSON parse failed after retry: %s", e)
98 |                 return []
99 |     return []
100 | 
101 | 
102 | def extract_concepts(db: Session, doc: Document) -> list[Concept]:
103 |     """
104 |     Extract concepts from doc.raw_text and persist to DB.
105 |     Uses hierarchical chunking with overlap; filters by confidence threshold.
106 |     """
107 |     if not doc.raw_text or len(doc.raw_text.strip()) < 100:
108 |         logger.info("[doc=%d] Text too short for concept extraction, skipping.", doc.id)
109 |         return []
110 | 
111 |     chunks = chunk_text_hierarchical(
112 |         doc.raw_text,
113 |         max_chars=settings.chunk_size * 4,
114 |         overlap_chars=settings.chunk_overlap,
115 |     )
116 | 
117 |     created: list[Concept] = []
118 |     seen_names: set[str] = set()
119 | 
120 |     existing_names = {
121 |         c.name.lower()
122 |         for c in db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == doc.workspace_id).all()
123 |     }
124 | 
125 |     for chunk in chunks:
126 |         raw_items = _call_llm(chunk)
127 |         for raw in raw_items:
128 |             try:
129 |                 item = ConceptItem(**raw)
130 |             except ValidationError as ve:
131 |                 logger.warning("[doc=%d] Rejected concept (validation failed): %s — %s", doc.id, raw, ve)
132 |                 continue
133 | 
134 |             if item.confidence < settings.concept_confidence_min:
135 |                 logger.debug(
136 |                     "[doc=%d] Skipped low-confidence concept '%s' (confidence=%.2f < %.2f)",
137 |                     doc.id, item.name, item.confidence, settings.concept_confidence_min,
138 |                 )
139 |                 continue
140 | 
141 |             name_lower = item.name.lower().strip()
142 |             if name_lower in seen_names or name_lower in existing_names:
143 |                 continue
144 | 
145 |             concept = Concept(
146 |                 workspace_id=doc.workspace_id,
147 |                 name=item.name.strip(),
148 |                 type=item.type,
149 |                 description=item.description,
150 |                 source_document_id=doc.id,
151 |                 source_excerpt=item.source_excerpt,
152 |                 confidence=item.confidence,
153 |             )
154 |             db.add(concept)
155 |             seen_names.add(name_lower)
156 |             existing_names.add(name_lower)
157 |             created.append(concept)
158 | 
159 |     db.commit()
160 |     logger.info("[doc=%d] Extracted %d concepts (confidence ≥ %.2f).", doc.id, len(created), settings.concept_confidence_min)
161 |     return created

80 | def extract_patterns(db: Session, doc: Document) -> list[ConsultingPattern]:
81 |     """Extract consulting patterns for the workspace after document ingestion."""

1 | """
2 | Schema extractor — derives structured schema facts from a spreadsheet without
3 | relying solely on LLM inference.
4 | 
5 | Heuristics extract:
6 |   - Entity types from column names (e.g. "Requirement ID" → entity type Requirement)
7 |   - Column taxonomies (identifier, descriptor, status, owner, domain, reference)
8 |   - Cross-sheet relationships when columns share domain vocabulary
9 |   - Business objects implied by header patterns

12 | prior knowledge rather than asking the LLM to infer everything from raw text.
13 | """
14 | from __future__ import annotations

16 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field

18 | from app.ingestion.spreadsheets.excel_parser import WorkbookData, SheetData
19 | from app.ingestion.spreadsheets.sheet_analyzer import SheetAnalysis

21 | # Column role taxonomy patterns
22 | _IDENTIFIER_PATTERNS  = {"id", "identifier", "ref", "reference", "number", "code", "key"}
23 | _DESCRIPTOR_PATTERNS  = {"name", "title", "description", "summary", "detail", "notes", "comment"}
24 | _STATUS_PATTERNS      = {"status", "state", "stage", "phase", "progress"}
25 | _OWNER_PATTERNS       = {"owner", "assignee", "responsible", "accountable", "team", "author"}
26 | _DOMAIN_PATTERNS      = {"domain", "area", "category", "type", "classification", "workstream"}
27 | _REFERENCE_PATTERNS   = {"related", "linked", "maps to", "references", "dependency", "parent"}

30 | @dataclass

32 |     name: str
33 |     role: str       # "identifier" | "descriptor" | "status" | "owner" | "domain" | "reference" | "value"
34 |     sample_values: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

53 | def extract_schema(workbook: WorkbookData, analyses: list[SheetAnalysis]) -> WorkbookSchema:
54 |     """Derive the structural schema of a workbook from parsed data + analysis results."""
55 |     sheet_schemas: list[SheetSchema] = []

68 |     shared = [et for et, count in entity_type_counts.items() if count >= 2]

89 |             f"  Sheet '{ss.sheet_name}' ({ss.sheet_type}): entity={ss.entity_type}"
90 |             + (f", IDs=[{', '.join(identifiers)}]" if identifiers else "")

100 |     entity_type = _infer_entity_type(analysis.sheet_type, sheet.headers)

111 | def _classify_column(header: str, sheet: SheetData) -> ColumnSchema:
112 |     h_lower = header.lower().strip()
113 |     role = "value"
114 |     for pattern in _IDENTIFIER_PATTERNS:
115 |         if pattern in h_lower:
116 |             role = "identifier"; break
117 |     if role == "value":
118 |         for pattern in _DESCRIPTOR_PATTERNS:
119 |             if pattern in h_lower:
120 |                 role = "descriptor"; break
121 |     if role == "value":
122 |         for pattern in _STATUS_PATTERNS:
123 |             if pattern in h_lower:
124 |                 role = "status"; break
125 |     if role == "value":
126 |         for pattern in _OWNER_PATTERNS:
127 |             if pattern in h_lower:
128 |                 role = "owner"; break
129 |     if role == "value":
130 |         for pattern in _DOMAIN_PATTERNS:
131 |             if pattern in h_lower:
132 |                 role = "domain"; break
133 |     if role == "value":
134 |         for pattern in _REFERENCE_PATTERNS:
135 |             if pattern in h_lower:
136 |                 role = "reference"; break
137 | 
138 |     samples = [row[header] for row in sheet.rows[:5] if header in row and row[header]]
139 |     return ColumnSchema(name=header, role=role, sample_values=samples)

143 |     "requirements":       "Requirement",
144 |     "risk_register":      "Risk",
145 |     "issue_log":          "Issue",
146 |     "dependency_map":     "Dependency",
147 |     "data_dictionary":    "Data Element",
148 |     "capability_catalog": "Capability",
149 |     "process_inventory":  "Process",
150 |     "control_inventory":  "Control",
151 |     "mapping_sheet":      "Mapping",
152 |     "glossary":           "Business Term",
153 |     "raid_log":           "RAID Item",
154 |     "generic":            "General",
155 | }

158 | def _infer_entity_type(sheet_type: str, headers: list[str]) -> str:
159 |     mapped = _ENTITY_TYPE_MAP.get(sheet_type)
160 |     if mapped:
161 |         return mapped
162 |     # Fallback: look for a singular noun in the first header
163 |     if headers:
164 |         return headers[0].strip().title() or "General"
165 |     return "General"

169 |     """Detect column names that suggest references to other sheets (e.g. 'Related Requirements')."""

199 |     if not non_empty:

202 |     short_text_count = sum(1 for c in non_empty if len(c) <= 80 and not _is_numeric(c))

66 |     provider = get_secret_provider()
67 |     api_key = provider.get_secret(settings.claude_secret_name)
68 |     timeout = httpx.Timeout(
69 |         connect=settings.llm_connect_timeout,
70 |         read=settings.llm_read_timeout,
71 |         write=settings.llm_write_timeout,
72 |         pool=settings.llm_connect_timeout,
73 |     )
74 |     return anthropic.Anthropic(
75 |         api_key=api_key,
76 |         base_url=settings.claude_base_url,
77 |         timeout=timeout,
78 |     )

81 | # ── Core API call (retried) ───────────────────────────────────────────
82 | 
83 | def _call_api(
84 |     system: str,
85 |     user: str,
86 |     max_tokens: int,
87 |     temperature: float,
88 | ) -> anthropic.types.Message:
89 |     """
90 |     Execute one Anthropic messages.create call.
91 |     Wrapped by chat() with the tenacity retry decorator.
92 |     This function is intentionally thin — one responsibility: call the SDK.
93 |     """
94 |     client = _get_client()
95 |     return client.messages.create(
96 |         model=settings.claude_model,
97 |         max_tokens=max_tokens,
98 |         temperature=temperature,
99 |         system=system,
100 |         messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}],
101 |     )
102 | 
103 | 
104 | # ── Public interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
105 | 
106 | def chat(
107 |     system: str,
108 |     user: str,
109 |     max_tokens: int = 2048,
110 |     temperature: float = 0.2,
111 |     operation: str = "llm_call",
112 | ) -> str:
113 |     """
114 |     Send a single chat completion via Claude and return the text response.
115 | 
116 |     Parameters
117 |     ----------
118 |     system      : System prompt text.
119 |     user        : User turn content.
120 |     max_tokens  : Upper bound on generated tokens.
121 |     temperature : Sampling temperature (0.0 for deterministic QA).
122 |     operation   : Logical label for observability logs (e.g. 'concept_extraction').
123 | 
124 |     Raises
125 |     ------
126 |     fastapi.HTTPException(503) — circuit breaker open, or retries exhausted.
127 |     anthropic.AuthenticationError — bad API key (not retried).
128 |     """
129 |     request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
130 |     t0 = time.monotonic()
131 |     retry_count = 0
132 | 
133 |     # Build a fresh retry decorator each call so monkeypatching settings in
134 |     # tests immediately takes effect without restarting the process.
135 |     _retried_call = llm_retry()(_call_api)
136 | 
137 |     with circuit_breaker:
138 |         try:
139 |             message = _retried_call(system, user, max_tokens, temperature)
140 | 
141 |         except RetryError as exc:
142 |             # All attempts exhausted — unwrap and log the root cause.
143 |             cause = exc.last_attempt.exception()
144 |             retry_count = exc.last_attempt.attempt_number - 1
145 |             logger.error(
146 |                 "[req=%s op=%s] LLM call failed after %d retries. "
147 |                 "Final error: %s %s",
148 |                 request_id, operation, retry_count,
149 |                 type(cause).__name__, cause,
150 |             )
151 |             raise HTTPException(
152 |                 status_code=503,
153 |                 detail="LLM request failed after multiple retry attempts. Please try again shortly.",
154 |             ) from exc
155 | 
156 |         except Exception:
157 |             # Non-transient error (auth failure, budget 429, etc.) — let it propagate.
158 |             raise
159 | 
160 |     latency_ms = (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000
161 | 
162 |     stats = getattr(_retried_call, "statistics", {})
163 |     retry_count = max(0, stats.get("attempt_number", 1) - 1)
164 | 
165 |     usage = message.usage
166 |     prompt_tokens     = getattr(usage, "input_tokens",  0)
167 |     completion_tokens = getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0)
168 | 
169 |     from app.llm.usage_tracker import estimate_cost
170 |     cost = estimate_cost(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)
171 | 
172 |     logger.info(
173 |         "[req=%s op=%s] LLM call completed: model=%s latency=%.0fms "
174 |         "prompt_tokens=%d completion_tokens=%d cost=$%.6f retries=%d",
175 |         request_id, operation, settings.claude_model, latency_ms,
176 |         prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost, retry_count,
177 |     )
178 | 
179 |     return message.content[0].text or ""

1 | """
2 | Evidence-grounded QA service.
3 | 
4 | Retrieval strategy (designed for consistency):
5 |   1. LLM keyword extraction from the question (temperature=0)
6 |   2. Cumulative, confidence-weighted semantic node scoring (top-k=20)
7 |   3. Strength-filtered BFS from all seed nodes
8 |   4. Deterministic context assembly: sorted by relevance score DESC then
9 |      concept confidence DESC; near-duplicate excerpts are deduplicated
10 |   5. Grounded generation at temperature=0 for factual stability
11 | """
12 | from __future__ import annotations
13 | import hashlib
14 | import json
15 | import logging
16 | 
17 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
18 | 
19 | from app.config import settings
20 | from app.db.models import Concept, Document, ConsultingPattern, ChatMessage
21 | from app.graph.memory_manager import graph_memory_manager
22 | from app.graph.traversal import find_nodes_semantic, get_neighbourhood
23 | from app.llm_client import chat
24 | from app.schemas import AskResponse, SourceRef
25 | 
26 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
27 | 
28 | QA_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
29 | You are an AI knowledge compiler and assistant for IBM Consulting.
30 | You MUST answer ONLY from the context passages provided below — this is your only source of truth.
31 | Do NOT use general knowledge, training data, internet search, or any external information.
32 | If the context does not support the answer to the question, you MUST respond with exactly:
33 | "I could not find this in the uploaded knowledge. The question may fall outside the documents in this workspace."
34 | 
35 | For every factual claim in your answer, cite the source document inline using [Source: Document Name].
36 | When multiple passages describe the same topic, synthesise them into a single coherent answer rather
37 | than repeating or summarising each passage independently. Use the most specific and complete information
38 | available. Never fabricate citations. You are showing your work — every claim must trace back to a
39 | specific document in the workspace.
40 | """
41 | 
42 | KEYWORD_EXTRACTION_PROMPT = """\
43 | Extract the 3-7 most important topic keywords or concept names from the following question.
44 | Return ONLY a JSON array of strings. No prose.
45 | Example: ["ISO 20022", "payment messaging", "SWIFT"]
46 | """
47 | 
48 | 
49 | def _extract_keywords_llm(question: str) -> list[str]:
50 |     """Extract search keywords from the question using the LLM at temperature=0."""
51 |     try:
52 |         raw = chat(
53 |             system=KEYWORD_EXTRACTION_PROMPT,
54 |             user=question,
55 |             max_tokens=256,
56 |             temperature=0.0,
57 |         )
58 |         raw = raw.strip()
59 |         if raw.startswith("```"):
60 |             raw = raw.split("```")[1]
61 |             if raw.startswith("json"):
62 |                 raw = raw[4:]
63 |         return json.loads(raw)
64 |     except Exception as e:
65 |         logger.warning("LLM keyword extraction failed: %s", e)
66 |         return [w.strip(".,?!") for w in question.split() if len(w) > 4]

69 | def _excerpt_fingerprint(text: str) -> str:
70 |     """Return a short hash of a normalised excerpt for deduplication."""
71 |     normalised = " ".join(text.lower().split())
72 |     return hashlib.md5(normalised[:200].encode()).hexdigest()

74 | 
75 | def ask_workspace(db: Session, workspace_id: int, question: str) -> AskResponse:
76 |     """
77 |     Full evidence-grounded Q&A pipeline designed for retrieval consistency.
78 | 
79 |     Key consistency properties:
80 |     - Keyword extraction is deterministic (temperature=0).
81 |     - Seed nodes are selected by cumulative scoring across all keywords
82 |       (not winner-takes-all), so the same question reliably retrieves the
83 |       same top seeds regardless of keyword ordering.
84 |     - Retrieved concepts are assembled in a stable order: relevance score
85 |       DESC, then concept confidence DESC, then concept ID ASC as tie-break.
86 |     - Near-duplicate source excerpts are deduplicated before LLM generation
87 |       so important passages are not pushed out of the context window.
88 |     - Final generation is at temperature=0 to minimise structural variation.
89 |     """
90 | 
91 |     keywords = _extract_keywords_llm(question)
92 |     logger.info("[ws=%d] Q&A keywords: %s", workspace_id, keywords)
93 | 
94 |     G = graph_memory_manager.get_workspace_graph(workspace_id, db)
95 |     scored_seeds = find_nodes_semantic(G, keywords, top_k=settings.qa_top_k)
96 | 
97 |     # Fall back to direct DB name scan when the graph has no matching nodes
98 |     if not scored_seeds:
99 |         kw_lower = [k.lower() for k in keywords]
100 |         db_matched = db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.workspace_id == workspace_id).all()
101 |         scored_seeds = [
102 |             (c.id, 0.7)
103 |             for c in db_matched
104 |             if any(kw in c.name.lower() for kw in kw_lower)
105 |         ]
106 | 
107 |     seed_score: dict[int, float] = {nid: score for nid, score in scored_seeds}
108 |     all_relevant_nodes: set[int] = set()
109 |     all_relevant_edges: list = []
110 | 
111 |     for node_id, _score in scored_seeds:
112 |         nbr_nodes, nbr_edges = get_neighbourhood(
113 |             G,
114 |             node_id,
115 |             hops=settings.graph_hop_depth,
116 |             strength_threshold=settings.graph_strength_threshold,
117 |             max_nodes=settings.graph_max_nodes,
118 |         )
119 |         all_relevant_nodes.update(nbr_nodes)
120 |         all_relevant_edges.extend(nbr_edges)
121 | 
122 |     context_parts: list[str] = []
123 |     source_refs: list[SourceRef] = []
124 |     seen_doc_ids: set[int] = set()
125 |     seen_excerpt_hashes: set[str] = set()
126 | 
127 |     if all_relevant_nodes:
128 |         concepts = db.query(Concept).filter(Concept.id.in_(list(all_relevant_nodes))).all()
129 | 
130 |         # Stable sort: seed_score DESC → concept.confidence DESC → concept.id ASC
131 |         # Nodes reached via BFS (not direct seeds) get score 0.0 and sort last.
132 |         concepts.sort(
133 |             key=lambda c: (
134 |                 -seed_score.get(c.id, 0.0),
135 |                 -float(getattr(c, "confidence", 0.8)),
136 |                 c.id,
137 |             )
138 |         )
139 | 
140 |         for c in concepts:
141 |             if not c.source_excerpt:
142 |                 continue
143 | 
144 |             # Skip near-duplicate excerpts to avoid redundant context
145 |             fp = _excerpt_fingerprint(c.source_excerpt)
146 |             if fp in seen_excerpt_hashes:
147 |                 continue
148 |             seen_excerpt_hashes.add(fp)
149 | 
150 |             doc_name = "Unknown Document"
151 |             if c.source_document_id:
152 |                 doc = db.get(Document, c.source_document_id)
153 |                 if doc:
154 |                     doc_name = doc.title or doc.filename
155 | 
156 |             context_parts.append(
157 |                 f"[Concept: {c.name}] ({c.type})\n"
158 |                 f"Description: {c.description}\n"
159 |                 f"Excerpt from '{doc_name}': {c.source_excerpt}"
160 |             )
161 |             if c.source_document_id and c.source_document_id not in seen_doc_ids:
162 |                 seen_doc_ids.add(c.source_document_id)
163 |                 source_refs.append(SourceRef(
164 |                     document_id=c.source_document_id,
165 |                     document_name=doc_name,
166 |                     excerpt=c.source_excerpt[:300],
167 |                 ))
168 | 
169 |         # Consulting patterns that overlap with matched concepts
170 |         patterns = (
171 |             db.query(ConsultingPattern)
172 |             .filter(ConsultingPattern.workspace_id == workspace_id)
173 |             .all()
174 |         )
175 |         for p in patterns:
176 |             rel_ids = p.related_concept_ids or []
177 |             if any(nid in rel_ids for nid in all_relevant_nodes):
178 |                 steps = "\n".join(f"  {s}" for s in (p.ibm_approach or []))
179 |                 context_parts.append(
180 |                     f"[Pattern: {p.name}]\n"
181 |                     f"Problem: {p.problem_statement}\n"
182 |                     f"IBM Approach:\n{steps}"
183 |                 )
184 |                 for did in (p.source_document_ids or []):
185 |                     if did not in seen_doc_ids:
186 |                         doc = db.get(Document, int(did))
187 |                         if doc:
188 |                             seen_doc_ids.add(did)
189 |                             source_refs.append(SourceRef(
190 |                                 document_id=did,
191 |                                 document_name=doc.title or doc.filename,
192 |                                 excerpt="(Pattern source)",
193 |                             ))
194 | 
195 |     if not context_parts:
196 |         answer = (
197 |             "I could not find this in the uploaded knowledge. "
198 |             "The question may fall outside the documents in this workspace."
199 |         )
200 |         _save_chat(db, workspace_id, question, answer, [])
201 |         return AskResponse(answer=answer, sources=[])
202 | 
203 |     context_text = "\n\n---\n\n".join(context_parts)
204 | 
205 |     try:
206 |         answer = chat(
207 |             system=QA_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
208 |             user=f"Context:\n{context_text}\n\nQuestion: {question}",
209 |             max_tokens=2048,
210 |             temperature=0.0,
211 |         )
212 |     except Exception as e:
213 |         logger.error("QA generation failed: %s", e)
214 |         answer = "An error occurred while generating the answer. Please try again."
215 |         source_refs = []
216 | 
217 |     not_found_signal = any(
218 |         phrase in answer.lower()
219 |         for phrase in ("not found", "cannot find", "outside the documents", "could not find")
220 |     )
221 |     if not not_found_signal and not source_refs:
222 |         answer = (
223 |             "I could not find this in the uploaded knowledge. "
224 |             "The question may fall outside the documents in this workspace."
225 |         )
226 |         source_refs = []
227 | 
228 |     _save_chat(db, workspace_id, question, answer, [s.document_id for s in source_refs])
229 |     return AskResponse(answer=answer, sources=source_refs)
230 | 
231 | 
232 | def _save_chat(db: Session, workspace_id: int, question: str, answer: str, doc_ids: list[int]) -> None:
233 |     db.add(ChatMessage(workspace_id=workspace_id, role="user", content=question, source_document_ids=[]))
234 |     db.add(ChatMessage(workspace_id=workspace_id, role="assistant", content=answer, source_document_ids=doc_ids))
235 |     db.commit()

1 | """
2 | LLM governance layer — budget enforcement and workspace-level rate limiting.
3 | 
4 | Budget enforcement
5 | ------------------
6 | Before every LLM call, check_budget() queries the workspace's LLMBudget row.
7 |   - If monthly_token_limit > 0 and current_token_usage >= limit → HTTP 429
8 |   - If monthly_cost_limit  > 0 and current_cost_usage  >= limit → HTTP 429
9 |   - Limits of 0 mean unlimited (default for new workspaces).
10 | 
11 | Rate limiting
12 | -------------
13 | A simple in-process sliding-window counter per workspace.
14 |   - Window: 60 seconds (configurable via LLM_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS)
15 |   - Limit:  MAX_LLM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE per workspace (default 60)
16 |   - Returns HTTP 429 when the window is full.
17 | 
18 | Note: this in-process rate limiter is suitable for a single-process deployment.
19 | For a multi-process/multi-node deployment replace with a Redis-backed counter.
20 | """
21 | from __future__ import annotations
22 | 
23 | import collections
24 | import logging
25 | import threading
26 | import time
27 | 
28 | from fastapi import HTTPException
29 | from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
30 | 
31 | from app.config import settings
32 | from app.db.models import LLMBudget
33 | 
34 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
35 | 
36 | 
37 | # ── Budget enforcement ────────────────────────────────────────────────
38 | 
39 | def check_budget(db: Session, workspace_id: int) -> None:
40 |     """
41 |     Raise HTTP 429 if the workspace has exceeded its monthly token or cost budget.
42 |     No-op if no budget row exists (unlimited by default).
43 |     """
44 |     budget = (
45 |         db.query(LLMBudget)
46 |         .filter(LLMBudget.workspace_id == workspace_id)
47 |         .first()
48 |     )
49 |     if budget is None:
50 |         return
51 | 
52 |     if budget.monthly_token_limit > 0:
53 |         if budget.current_token_usage >= budget.monthly_token_limit:
54 |             logger.warning(
55 |                 "[ws=%d] Token budget exceeded: %d / %d",
56 |                 workspace_id, budget.current_token_usage, budget.monthly_token_limit,
57 |             )
58 |             raise HTTPException(
59 |                 status_code=429,
60 |                 detail=(
61 |                     f"Workspace LLM token budget exceeded "
62 |                     f"({budget.current_token_usage:,} / {budget.monthly_token_limit:,} tokens used this month)."
63 |                 ),
64 |             )
65 | 
66 |     if budget.monthly_cost_limit > 0.0:
67 |         if budget.current_cost_usage >= budget.monthly_cost_limit:
68 |             logger.warning(
69 |                 "[ws=%d] Cost budget exceeded: $%.4f / $%.4f",
70 |                 workspace_id, budget.current_cost_usage, budget.monthly_cost_limit,
71 |             )
72 |             raise HTTPException(
73 |                 status_code=429,
74 |                 detail=(
75 |                     f"Workspace LLM cost budget exceeded "
76 |                     f"(${budget.current_cost_usage:.4f} / ${budget.monthly_cost_limit:.4f} spent this month)."
77 |                 ),
78 |             )
79 | 
80 | 
81 | # ── Rate limiting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
82 | 
83 | _rate_lock   = threading.Lock()
84 | # workspace_id → deque of request timestamps (float, monotonic)
85 | _rate_windows: dict[int, collections.deque] = collections.defaultdict(
86 |     lambda: collections.deque()
87 | )
88 | 
89 | 
90 | def check_rate_limit(workspace_id: int) -> None:
91 |     """
92 |     Raise HTTP 429 if the workspace has made more than
93 |     MAX_LLM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE LLM calls in the last LLM_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS.
94 |     """
95 |     limit  = settings.max_llm_requests_per_minute
96 |     window = settings.llm_rate_window_seconds
97 |     now    = time.monotonic()
98 |     cutoff = now - window
99 | 
100 |     with _rate_lock:
101 |         dq = _rate_windows[workspace_id]
102 |         # Remove timestamps outside the current window
103 |         while dq and dq[0] < cutoff:
104 |             dq.popleft()
105 | 
106 |         if len(dq) >= limit:
107 |             logger.warning(
108 |                 "[ws=%d] LLM rate limit hit: %d requests in %.0fs window.",
109 |                 workspace_id, len(dq), window,
110 |             )
111 |             raise HTTPException(
112 |                 status_code=429,
113 |                 detail=(
114 |                     f"LLM request rate limit exceeded "
115 |                     f"({limit} requests per {window:.0f}s). Please slow down."
116 |                 ),
117 |             )
118 | 
119 |         dq.append(now)

1 | """
2 | Circuit breaker for LLM calls.
3 | 
4 | Protects the application from cascading failures when the LLM provider is
5 | unavailable, rate-limiting, or timing out.
6 | 
7 | State machine
8 | -------------
9 | CLOSED   — normal operation; failures are counted
10 | OPEN     — breaker is tripped; all calls are rejected immediately
11 | HALF_OPEN — recovery probe; a single call is allowed through to test health
12 | 
13 | Transition rules
14 | ----------------
15 | CLOSED  → OPEN      when consecutive_failures >= failure_threshold
16 | OPEN    → HALF_OPEN after recovery_timeout_seconds have elapsed
17 | HALF_OPEN → CLOSED  on successful call
18 | HALF_OPEN → OPEN    on failed call (resets the recovery timer)
19 | 
20 | Configuration (all via environment / Settings):
21 |   LLM_CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD   default 5   failures before opening
22 |   LLM_CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT    default 60  seconds before half-open probe
23 | """
24 | from __future__ import annotations
25 | 
26 | import logging
27 | import threading
28 | import time
29 | from enum import Enum
30 | 
31 | from fastapi import HTTPException
32 | 
33 | from app.config import settings
34 | 
35 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
36 | 
37 | 
38 | class BreakerState(str, Enum):
39 |     CLOSED    = "closed"
40 |     OPEN      = "open"
41 |     HALF_OPEN = "half_open"
42 | 
43 | 
44 | class CircuitBreaker:
45 |     """
46 |     Thread-safe circuit breaker.
47 | 
48 |     Usage::
49 | 
50 |         breaker = CircuitBreaker()
51 | 
52 |         with breaker:
53 |             result = call_llm_api()
54 |     """
55 | 
56 |     def __init__(
57 |         self,
58 |         failure_threshold: int | None = None,
59 |         recovery_timeout: float | None = None,
60 |     ) -> None:
61 |         self._threshold = failure_threshold or settings.llm_cb_failure_threshold
62 |         self._timeout   = recovery_timeout  or settings.llm_cb_recovery_timeout
63 |         self._failures  = 0
64 |         self._state     = BreakerState.CLOSED
65 |         self._opened_at: float | None = None
66 |         self._lock      = threading.Lock()
67 | 
68 |     # ── public API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
69 | 
70 |     @property
71 |     def state(self) -> BreakerState:
72 |         with self._lock:
73 |             return self._evaluated_state()
74 | 
75 |     def record_success(self) -> None:
76 |         with self._lock:
77 |             self._failures = 0
78 |             self._state    = BreakerState.CLOSED
79 |             self._opened_at = None
80 |         logger.debug("Circuit breaker: call succeeded → CLOSED")
81 | 
82 |     def record_failure(self) -> None:
83 |         with self._lock:
84 |             self._failures += 1
85 |             if self._failures >= self._threshold:
86 |                 self._state     = BreakerState.OPEN
87 |                 self._opened_at = time.monotonic()
88 |                 logger.warning(
89 |                     "Circuit breaker OPEN after %d consecutive failures.", self._failures
90 |                 )
91 | 
92 |     def __enter__(self) -> "CircuitBreaker":
93 |         with self._lock:
94 |             state = self._evaluated_state()
95 | 
96 |         if state == BreakerState.OPEN:
97 |             logger.warning("Circuit breaker is OPEN — rejecting LLM request.")
98 |             raise HTTPException(
99 |                 status_code=503,
100 |                 detail="LLM service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.",
101 |             )
102 |         return self
103 | 
104 |     def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> bool:
105 |         if exc_type is None:
106 |             self.record_success()
107 |         else:
108 |             # Only count genuine provider/network errors, not validation errors.
109 |             if not issubclass(exc_type, (ValueError, HTTPException)):
110 |                 self.record_failure()
111 |         return False  # never suppress exceptions
112 | 
113 |     # ── internals ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
114 | 
115 |     def _evaluated_state(self) -> BreakerState:
116 |         """
117 |         Transition OPEN → HALF_OPEN if the recovery timeout has elapsed.
118 |         Must be called with self._lock held.
119 |         """
120 |         if self._state == BreakerState.OPEN and self._opened_at is not None:
121 |             elapsed = time.monotonic() - self._opened_at
122 |             if elapsed >= self._timeout:
123 |                 self._state = BreakerState.HALF_OPEN
124 |                 logger.info(
125 |                     "Circuit breaker: recovery timeout elapsed (%.0fs) → HALF_OPEN",
126 |                     elapsed,
127 |                 )
128 |         return self._state
129 | 
130 | 
131 | # Application-level singleton — shared across all threads in one process.

1 | """
2 | LLM usage tracker — persists one row per API call to the llm_usage table.
3 | 
4 | Token counts come from the Anthropic response object's usage field.
5 | Cost estimates use configurable per-token prices; updating prices requires
6 | only a config change, not a code change.
7 | 
8 | Override pricing defaults via environment variables:
9 |   LLM_COST_PER_1K_INPUT_TOKENS
10 |   LLM_COST_PER_1K_OUTPUT_TOKENS
11 | """
12 | from __future__ import annotations
13 |
